heading.en: A chart is a table of positions

kicker.en: A chart records the sky at the moment you were born.
kicker.zh: 星盤記的是你出生那一刻的天空。

text.en: Think of the chart as a seating plan for that moment of sky: who sits in which section. When you read a chart, you find the seats one by one: first where the Sun sits, then the Moon, then where each of the other planets sits.
text.zh: 你可以把星盤想成「那一刻天空的座位表」：誰坐在哪一塊。讀盤時就照著座位一格一格找：先找太陽坐在哪一塊，再找月亮，最後看其他行星各自坐在哪裡。

text.en: A chart records the direction of each body in the sky. This app works out which degree of the zodiac each body sits on — where it appears, seen from Earth. So when you read a chart, what you look at is which section each body sits in.
text.zh: 盤上記的是每顆星在天空中的方向。本 App 算出每顆星落在黃道上的哪一度，也就是從地球看出去，它正坐在哪個位置。所以讀盤時，你要看的是每顆星坐在哪一格。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy takes the degree rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth as the starting point of the whole chart; everything else is counted from there.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 2 章，把出生那一刻東方地平線上升起的度數當成整張盤的起點，其他東西都從這一點開始排。

kicker.en: Planets are who, signs are the style, houses are which part of life.
kicker.zh: 行星是誰，星座是什麼風格，宮位是生活的哪一塊。

text.en: The things on a chart are easier to remember as three kinds: a planet is the who, a sign is the style, a house is which part of life. Take “Sun in Libra”: the Sun is the who, and Libra is its style — talking things out and smoothing things over. Read any row by asking three questions: who? in what style? in which part of life?
text.zh: 盤上的東西分三種比較好記：行星是「誰」，星座是「用什麼風格」，宮位是「在生活的哪一塊」。例如「太陽在天秤」：太陽是誰，天秤是它做事的風格——愛把話講開、把關係擺平。讀任何一格，都先問這三句：誰？什麼風格？在哪一塊？

text.en: What sets them apart is whether they need a birth time. Planets and signs come from the date alone (on a day when one changes sign, the candidates are listed). Houses and the Ascendant depend on the Earth's rotation, so they need a birth time to be worked out. With a time, the chart gains the house layer; until a time is entered, that layer stays blank and the planets and signs can still be read.
text.zh: 三種東西的差別，在於要不要出生時間。行星和星座只要日期就有（剛好換星座的那天會列出候選）；宮位和上升要靠地球自轉的角度，所以要有出生時間才算得出來。有了時間，盤上就多出宮位這一層；還沒填時間時，那一層留白，行星和星座照樣可以讀。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy sets out the nature of each of the seven planets one by one. William Lilly's Christian Astrology of 1647, in “Of the Twelve Houses,” names the first house the Ascendant, signifying life and the body.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 4 章一顆一顆寫出七顆行星的性質；William Lilly 一六四七年的《Christian Astrology》在〈Of the Twelve Houses〉寫明第一宮叫做上升，管生命與身體。

kicker.en: Astrology is a language for describing yourself.
kicker.zh: 占星是一套描述自己的語言。

text.en: Astrology is a long-lived symbolic language. It gives you words for describing yourself and angles for noticing things. You can hold those words up against your own life and see which fit you and which do not. Reading “Moon in Aries: under pressure, act first, think later,” think back to the last time someone rushed you: did you jump in, or stop and think?
text.zh: 占星是一套流傳很久的象徵語言，它給你描述自己的詞彙、觀察自己的角度。你可以拿這些詞彙對照自己的生活，看哪些說法貼近你、哪些不像你。例如讀到「月亮在牡羊，壓力一來先衝再想」，就回想上一次被人催的時候，你是先動手，還是先停下來想。

text.en: As you read, the small tag beside each paragraph tells you what it is. Positions are really computed and can be used as they are; readings are handed down and are there to check against yourself. Look at the tag first, then decide how to use the paragraph.
text.zh: 讀課文時，每一段旁邊的小標籤告訴你這段是什麼：星體位置是真的算出來的，可以直接拿來用；解讀是流傳下來的說法，拿來對照自己。先看標籤，再決定這段要怎麼用。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy argues that the motions of the heavens change the air and moisture around the Earth — seasons, tides, plants and animals shift with them — so inference is possible; ch. 3 then argues it is useful.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 2 章的理由是，天體的運行會改變地上的空氣和水氣，季節、潮水、動植物都跟著變，所以可以推論；第 3 章接著說這樣做有好處。

alt.en: Diagram: a double ring. The outer ring is divided into twelve parts for the signs, the inner ring stands for the houses, and a horizontal line on the left is labelled ASC, the point the chart is counted from. A concept figure with no real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個雙層圓環，外圈分成十二等分代表十二星座，內圈代表十二宮，左側有一條水平線標著 ASC，代表整張盤的起算點。這是概念圖，沒有真實度數。

caption.en: A circle cut into twelve, with the starting point on the left.
caption.zh: 一個圈分成十二等分，左邊是起算點。

caveat.en: These three lines use fixed demonstration placements, chosen to show how a chart can be read.
caveat.zh: 這三句用的是固定的示範位置，專門拿來示範一張盤可以怎麼讀。

lines.en: Sun in Libra: this person puts their energy into talking things out and smoothing things over.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤：這個人把力氣用在把話講開、把關係擺平。

lines.en: Moon in Aries: under pressure the reaction is fast — act first, think later.
lines.zh: 月亮在牡羊：壓力一來反應很快，先衝再想。

lines.en: Ascendant in Capricorn: at a first meeting they come across as steady and a bit formal.
lines.zh: 上升在摩羯：第一次見面看起來穩、有點正式。

limitations.en: Without a birth time, the Ascendant and house rows stay blank; enter a birth time and that layer appears.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，上升和宮位那一行會空著；填上出生時間，這一層就會出現。

limitations.en: Astrology is a language for describing yourself, not a prediction or a test result; use its words to check against your own life.
limitations.zh: 占星是一套描述自己的語言，不是預測，也不是檢測結果；拿它的詞彙來對照自己的生活。

limitations.en: The three example lines use demonstration placements. They are not a real person's chart and not computed from your data.
limitations.zh: 範例的三句用的是示範位置，不是真人的盤，也不是用你的資料算出來的。

claim.en: “A birth chart is the same as a horoscope column.”
claim.zh: 「星盤就是星座運勢。」

correction.en: A horoscope column usually uses the Sun sign alone — one reading for a twelfth of everybody. A chart is the full table of positions at your moment of birth, and the Sun is just one row of it.
correction.zh: 運勢欄通常只看太陽星座，一段話給十二分之一的人看；星盤是你出生那一刻的完整位置表，太陽只是其中一格。

claim.en: “The positions show how far the planets are from me.”
claim.zh: 「盤上的位置就是星星離我多遠。」

correction.en: A position on the chart is a direction: which degree of the zodiac each body falls on, seen from Earth. That degree is what the app records.
correction.zh: 盤上的位置是方向：每顆星從地球看出去，落在黃道的哪一度。App 記錄的就是這個度數。

claim.en: “Without a birth time you cannot have a chart.”
claim.zh: 「沒有出生時間就不能排盤。」

correction.en: You can. The date alone places each planet in a sign, and a body that changes sign that day is listed with its candidates. A birth time then adds the Ascendant and house layer.
correction.zh: 可以排。只靠日期，就能排出每顆行星落在哪個星座；剛好換星座的星會列出候選。有了出生時間，再多加上升和宮位這一層。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: if a chart is a table of positions, which row do you want to read first, and why?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：如果盤是一張位置表，你最想先看哪一格？為什麼？

objective.en: By the end you will know what a birth chart is, the three kinds of thing on it, and how to use it to describe yourself and check it against your own life.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道星盤是什麼、上面有哪三種東西，還有怎麼拿它來描述自己、對照自己的生活。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: look at three things only. The rest can wait.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：先只看三件事，其他的不用急。

personalSteps.en: Note the signs of your Sun and Moon. If there are two candidates, note both.
personalSteps.zh: 看太陽、月亮在哪個星座。有兩個候選的話，兩個都記下來。

personalSteps.en: Check whether you have an Ascendant. A birth time gives you one; if no time is entered yet, a blank row is the normal answer.
personalSteps.zh: 看有沒有上升。有出生時間就會有上升；還沒填時間的話，這一格留白是正常的。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: which of them feels least like you? Come back to it next lesson.
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：哪一項最不像你？下一堂再回來看。

title.zh: William Lilly, Christian Astrology（1647）

summary.en: A birth chart is a table of where things were in the sky at one moment, seen from one place.
summary.zh: 星盤就是某一刻、從某個地方看出去的天空位置表。

title.zh: 星盤是什麼

kicker.en: The Sun is the one people mean when they say “I’m a Leo.”
kicker.zh: 太陽就是大家說「我是什麼座」的那一個。

text.en: When people say “I’m a Leo,” they mean their Sun sign. The Sun describes where your vitality comes from, and the side of you that shines outward and gets seen; it can also be read as “who you are trying to become.” When you look at your own Sun, ask two things: what am I doing when I feel most alive? What do I most want people to see in me?
text.zh: 一般人說「我是什麼座」，講的就是太陽星座。太陽講的是你的生命力從哪裡來，也是你往外散發、被別人看見的那一面；也可以把它讀成「你想成為什麼樣的人」。看自己的太陽時，問兩句：我做什麼事時最有精神？我最希望別人看見我哪一點？

text.en: The Sun can usually be found from the birth date alone, with no birth time. The Earth takes about 365.26 days to go round the Sun, which works out at roughly one degree a day, and a sign only changes every 30 degrees. So apart from the changeover days, people born on the same date usually have the same Sun sign. That makes the Sun the easiest to look up — and the one most often mistaken for the whole chart.
text.zh: 太陽大多只要出生日期就能確定，不需要出生時間。地球繞太陽一圈約 365.26 天，算下來太陽每天只走大約一度，而星座每 30 度才換一個。所以除了換星座那幾天，同一天出生的人太陽通常在同一個星座。這讓太陽最好查，也最常被誤當成整張盤。

text.en: But if you were born on the day the Sun changed sign and you do not know your birth time, you genuinely have two possible Sun signs. This app lists both, so you can check each one against yourself.
text.zh: 可是如果你剛好在太陽換星座那天出生，又不知道出生時間，前後兩個星座都有可能。這時本 App 會兩個都列出來，讓你兩個都拿來對照自己。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 12 of the Tetrabiblos, while dealing with injuries and illness, Ptolemy lists which planet goes with which part of the body and gives the Sun sight, the brain and the heart.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 12 章在講身體受傷和生病時，列出每顆行星對應的身體部位，把視覺、腦、心臟歸給太陽。

kicker.en: The Moon is about what you need in order to feel settled.
kicker.zh: 月亮看的是你需要什麼才安心。

text.en: The Moon is about your inner needs and habitual reactions: what settles you, where you retreat under pressure, who you are around people you trust. It also explains “I know what to do, yet I still don’t do it”: the Sun wants to go one way while the Moon needs the familiar and the safe, and the two need not agree. Think of the first thing you want to do when you get home after a long day — that is the kind of thing the Moon describes.
text.zh: 月亮看的是你的內在需求和習慣反應：什麼讓你安心、壓力一來你會縮回哪裡、在熟人面前你是什麼樣子。它也能解釋「我明明知道該怎麼做，卻還是做不到」：太陽想往某個方向走，月亮卻需要熟悉和安全，兩邊不一定同路。想想你累了一整天回到家，最想做的第一件事是什麼——那就是月亮在講的事。

text.en: The Moon moves fast. It goes round in about 27.32 days, roughly 13 degrees a day, so it changes sign every two days or so. Someone born on a changeover day without a known birth time therefore has two possible Moon signs. This app clearly marks that case as unconfirmed.
text.zh: 月亮走得很快。它繞一圈約 27.32 天，算下來每天走約 13 度，大約兩天多就換一個星座。所以不知道出生時間、又剛好在月亮換星座那天出生的人，會有兩個可能的月亮星座。本 App 會把這種情況清楚標示成「不確定」。

text.en: When you check this against yourself, notice the gap between what you want to do and what you manage to do. That is more useful than deciding which one is the real you.
text.zh: 對照你自己時，先看見「想做的」和「做得到的」之間的落差，這比急著決定哪一個才是真正的你更有用。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 13 of the Tetrabiblos, “Of the Quality of the Soul,” Ptolemy gives the parts to do with reason and the mind to Mercury, and the sensory, non-rational part to the Moon. One planet takes thinking, the other feeling — a clear division of labour.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 13 章〈靈魂的性質〉寫，跟理性、心智有關的部分看水星，感受的、非理性的部分看月亮。兩顆星一個管想，一個管感受，分工很清楚。

kicker.en: The Ascendant is about the you that people see first.
kicker.zh: 上升看的是別人第一眼看到的你。

text.en: The Ascendant is the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment you were born. It describes the first impression you make and the way you walk into a new room. When friends say “at first I thought you were…, then I got to know you,” the first half is usually what the Ascendant describes.
text.zh: 上升是你出生那一刻，東方地平線上正在升起的那個星座。它看的是你給人的第一印象、你走進新場合的樣子。朋友常說「一開始覺得你很……，熟了才發現……」，前半句往往就是上升在講的樣子。

text.en: The Earth turns once in about 23.93 hours, and the twelve signs take turns crossing the eastern horizon — roughly two hours each — so the Ascendant depends entirely on the birth time. No time means no Ascendant and no houses — that whole layer of structure needs a birth time to be laid out. In that case this app shows a clearly labelled demonstration chart so you can learn the idea first.
text.zh: 地球自轉一圈約 23.93 小時，十二個星座輪流經過東方地平線，平均大約兩小時換一個，所以上升完全看出生時間。不知道時間就沒有上升，也沒有宮位——這一整層結構要靠出生時間才排得出來。這時本 App 會改用標示清楚的示範盤，讓你先看懂概念。

text.en: The Ascendant is like a doorway: people pass through it before they reach the rooms behind. So the impression it gives can differ from the side you most identify with. A mismatch between the two is normal, and both are really you.
text.zh: 上升就像一扇門口：別人要先經過門口，才進得了屋子。所以上升給人的印象，可以和你最認同的自己不一樣；兩者不一樣很正常，兩邊都是真的你。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy takes the rising degree at the moment of birth as the chart’s starting point. William Lilly’s Christian Astrology of 1647, in “Of the Twelve Houses,” names the first house the Ascendant, signifying life and the body, because it is rising on the eastern horizon.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 2 章把出生那一刻上升的度數，當成整張盤的起點；William Lilly 一六四七年的《Christian Astrology》在〈Of the Twelve Houses〉寫明第一宮叫做上升，管生命與身體，因為它正從東方地平線升起。

alt.en: Diagram: an outer ring labelled Sun, an inner ring labelled Moon, and a point at the bottom labelled Ascendant, stacked on one vertical line to show three different layers rather than real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：外圈標示太陽，中圈標示月亮，底部標示上升 ASC，三者排在同一條垂直線上，代表三個不同層次的位置，不是真實度數。

caption.en: How the Sun, Moon and Ascendant sit relative to each other.
caption.zh: 太陽、月亮、上升三個位置的相對關係。

caveat.en: One person, three different statements. The Sun alone suggests someone who goes along with everything; the Ascendant alone suggests someone cold. Read all three together and you get one whole person.
caveat.zh: 同一個人，三句話講的是三件事。只看太陽，會以為他什麼都好商量；只看上升，會以為他很冷淡。三句一起讀，才是同一個人的樣子。

lines.en: Sun in Libra: the energy goes into talking things through and smoothing things over.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤：力氣用在把話講開、把關係擺平。

lines.en: Moon in Aries: feelings come fast; when uncomfortable, acts first and talks later.
lines.zh: 月亮在牡羊：情緒來得快，不舒服時先動手做，之後才說。

lines.en: Ascendant in Capricorn: at first sight composed and a little distant — quieter than he really is.
lines.zh: 上升在摩羯：第一眼看起來穩重、有點距離，比實際的他安靜。

limitations.en: On a changeover day with no known birth time, the Sun or Moon is listed with both candidate signs; check each one against yourself.
limitations.zh: 換星座那天出生又不知道時間時，太陽或月亮會列出兩個候選星座，兩個都拿來對照自己。

limitations.en: Without a birth time, the whole Ascendant-and-houses layer stays blank; add a birth time and that layer appears.
limitations.zh: 不知道出生時間時，上升和宮位那一整層會空著；補上出生時間，這一層就會出現。

limitations.en: The three example lines are fixed demonstration placements, not a real person's chart.
limitations.zh: 範例三句是固定的示範位置，不是真人的盤。

claim.en: “The Ascendant is the real me; the Sun is just a surface.”
claim.zh: 「上升才是真正的我，太陽只是表面。」

correction.en: The three describe different layers, and all three are you. Reading them together shows more of you than picking one as the real you.
correction.zh: 三個位置講的是不同層面，三個都是你。把三個放在一起看，比挑一個當成「真正的我」更能看出你完整的樣子。

claim.en: “Without a birth time the chart is useless.”
claim.zh: 「不知道出生時間，就算了吧，盤沒有用。」

correction.en: The chart is still useful: the Sun and most planets’ signs hold from the date alone, a birth on a changeover day is listed with both candidates, and a time adds the Ascendant and the houses. This app shows what is certain, marks what is not, and never quietly fills in a time.
correction.zh: 盤照樣有用：太陽和大多數行星的星座只靠日期就成立，剛好在換星座那天出生的，會列出兩個候選；時間補上的是上升和宮位。本 App 能確定的照常顯示，不能確定的直接標出來，不會偷偷補一個時間。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: which of the three feels most like the self you know?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：三個位置裡，哪一個最像你認識的自己？

objective.en: By the end you will be able to tell which side of you the Sun, the Moon and the Ascendant each describe, and why reading all three together gives a fuller picture of a person.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會分得出太陽、月亮、上升各自在講你的哪一面，也會知道為什麼三個一起看，才看得到比較完整的一個人。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: here you only need to see where the three placements are.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：這一段只要看清楚三個位置各在哪裡就好。

personalSteps.en: Read out the three signs first, before deciding whether they fit.
personalSteps.zh: 先把三個位置的星座念出來，先別想準不準。

personalSteps.en: Pick one description that does not feel like you, and write down what is off.
personalSteps.zh: 挑一句你覺得「不太像我」的描述，寫下哪裡不像。

personalSteps.en: If the Ascendant is empty, note that this row needs a birth time; the rest of your chart can still be read.
personalSteps.zh: 如果上升是空的，記下這一格需要的是出生時間；盤上其他部分照樣能讀。

reason.en: The Sun moves about one degree a day, so the date is usually enough.
reason.zh: 太陽一天只走大約一度，知道日期通常就夠了。

text.en: Sun
text.zh: 太陽

reason.en: The Moon is usually settled by the date; only a changeover day needs the time to confirm it.
reason.zh: 月亮大多看日期就知道，只有出生當天剛好換星座時才需要時間來確定。

text.en: Moon
text.zh: 月亮

reason.en: The Ascendant changes sign roughly every two hours, so it cannot be worked out without a birth time.
reason.zh: 上升大約兩小時換一個星座，沒有出生時間就算不出來。

text.en: Ascendant
text.zh: 上升

prompt.en: Which placement depends entirely on the birth time?
prompt.zh: 哪一個位置完全看出生時間？

reason.en: That is what the Ascendant describes.
reason.zh: 那是上升在講的。

text.en: The first impression others get
text.zh: 別人第一眼的印象

reason.en: Yes — the Moon is read as safety, emotional habits and the private self.
reason.zh: 對，月亮被讀成安全感、情緒習慣和私下的樣子。

text.en: Inner needs and habitual reactions
text.zh: 內在需求和習慣反應

reason.en: That is what the Sun describes.
reason.zh: 那是太陽在講的。

text.en: Vitality and the side that shines outward
text.zh: 生命力和往外散發的那一面

prompt.en: What does the Moon mainly describe?
prompt.zh: 月亮主要在講什麼？

reason.en: The Sun is worked out reliably; the point is that it covers one side only.
reason.zh: 太陽算得很穩；要注意的是它只講一個面向。

text.en: The Sun is worked out inaccurately
text.zh: 太陽算得不準

reason.en: The three describe different layers; drop two and only a fragment is left.
reason.zh: 三個位置講不同層面，少了兩個就只剩一小塊。

text.en: It covers one side only, leaving out feelings and how you come across
text.zh: 它只講一個面向，漏掉了情緒和給人的樣子

reason.en: Your Sun sign is set at the moment of birth and stays the same for life; only a changeover day needs the birth time to settle it.
reason.zh: 你的太陽星座在出生那一刻就定下來，一輩子都是同一個；只有剛好在換星座那天出生，才需要出生時間來確定。

text.en: The Sun sign changes every year
text.zh: 太陽星座每年都會變

prompt.en: What is wrong with judging someone by their Sun sign alone?
prompt.zh: 只看太陽星座判斷一個人，問題在哪裡？

detail.en: Book III ch. 2 takes the rising degree at birth as the chart’s starting point. Ch. 12, while treating bodily injuries and diseases, lists the planetary rulerships of body parts and gives the Sun sight, the brain and the heart. Ch. 13, “Of the Quality of the Soul,” gives the rational part to Mercury and the sensory, non-rational part to the Moon. Only what these three chapters state literally is cited here.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 2 章以出生時刻的上升度數為整張盤的起算點；第 12 章在講身體的損傷與疾病時，列出行星對應的身體部位，把視覺、腦、心臟歸給太陽；第 13 章《靈魂的性質》把理性與心智歸水星、感受的與非理性的部分歸月亮。本課只引用這三章的字面陳述。

label.zh: 第三卷第 2 章（上升度數）
第三卷第 12 章（身體部位）

label.en: Book III ch. 13 (quality of the soul)
label.zh: 第三卷第 13 章（靈魂的性質）

detail.zh: 〈Of the Twelve Houses〉寫明第一宮稱為上升，管生命與身體，因為它正從東方地平線升起。原文沒有寫到第一印象。

summary.en: Three placements, three different sides — read them together.
summary.zh: 三個位置講三個不同的面向，三個一起看才完整。

title.zh: 太陽、月亮、上升

kicker.en: Signs move in three ways: starting, holding, shifting.
kicker.zh: 星座有三種動法：開場、守成、轉換。

text.en: These three groups are called cardinal, fixed and mutable — think starting, holding, shifting. The starting signs are Aries, Cancer, Libra and Capricorn; the holding signs are Taurus, Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius; the shifting signs are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces. Calling someone “very fixed” means that once they decide, they rarely change.
text.zh: 這三類叫基本、固定、變動，可以記成開場、守成、轉換。開場的是牡羊、巨蟹、天秤、摩羯；守成的是金牛、獅子、天蠍、水瓶；轉換的是雙子、處女、射手、雙魚。說一個人「很固定」，意思是他一旦決定了，就不太改。

text.en: The three groups answer how someone gets started, keeps going and turns a corner, and each has its own use. The same task can be done with starting energy or with holding energy.
text.zh: 這三類回答「一個人怎麼起步、怎麼撐下去、怎麼轉彎」，三類各有各的用處。同一件事，可以用開場的力氣做，也可以用守成的力氣做。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 11 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy divides the twelve signs into those at the equinoxes and solstices, the solid ones, and the bicorporeal ones. The split comes from where they sit along the zodiac and how that relates to the turn of the seasons.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 11 章把十二星座分成三類——落在分點和至點的、固定的（solid）、雙體的（bicorporeal）。分法根據的是它們在黃道上的哪一段，跟季節轉換有什麼關係。

kicker.en: The twelve signs fall into four groups: fire, earth, air, water.
kicker.zh: 十二星座分成火、土、風、水四組。

text.en: The four groups are fire, earth, air and water, and they describe what a person notices first: fire for drive, earth for the practical, air for information, water for feeling. At the same dinner, fire wants to pick the place, earth minds the budget, air is busy chatting, and water is watching how everyone feels.
text.zh: 這四組叫火、土、風、水，描述的是一個人先注意什麼：火看動力，土看實際，風看訊息，水看感受。同一場聚餐，火想先決定去哪，土在意預算，風忙著跟大家聊，水在留意每個人的心情。

text.en: Looking at your own chart, how your placements spread across the elements tells you more than any single sign. Count which groups they fall in.
text.zh: 看自己的盤時，元素怎麼分布，比單看一個星座更有用。數一數你的位置落在哪幾組。

text.en: If most placements land in one group, you probably reach for the same approach again and again; if they are spread out, it depends more on the situation. If a group is empty, ask whether that approach is one you seldom use and have to practise on purpose.
text.zh: 大部分位置落在同一組，你大概常用同一種方式處理事情；分散的話，就比較看場合。某一組一個都沒有的話，想想那種方式是不是你比較少用、需要刻意練習的。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 18 of the Tetrabiblos, “Of the Triangles,” divides the zodiac into four equilateral triangles — the first passing through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius — and sets out which planets govern each. The chapter deals with the familiarity the triangles bring and the planets that rule each one.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 18 章〈Of the Triangles〉把黃道分成四個等邊三角，第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手，並寫出每個三角由哪些行星管。這一章談的是三角帶來的親近關係，以及每個三角由哪些行星管轄。

kicker.en: A sign is an adjective; it needs a planet to mean anything.
kicker.zh: 星座是形容詞，要先有一顆行星才有意義。

text.en: Use a sign like an adjective. “Venus in Gemini” reads as “what they like leans toward talking, looking around and comparing”: Gemini describes how Venus shows itself. A sentence needs a planet in it before a sign has anything to describe.
text.zh: 星座最好當成形容詞來用。「金星在雙子」讀成「他喜歡的方式偏向多聊、多看、多比較」：雙子形容的是金星怎麼表現。句子裡一定要先有一顆行星，星座才有東西可以形容。

text.en: So a planet and a sign together make a sentence with content; a Sun sign by itself is one line shared by a twelfth of everyone. Read your own chart in the same order: name the planet first, then its style — for example “Moon in Aries: feelings act first, think later.”
text.zh: 所以把行星和星座一起講，句子才有內容；單講一個太陽星座，是十二分之一的人共用的一句話。自己讀盤時也照這個順序：先說是哪一顆星，再說它的風格，例如「月亮在牡羊：情緒先動再想」。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 12 of the Tetrabiblos divides the signs into masculine and feminine, taking turns. It is a classification that feeds later rules of judgement.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 12 章把十二星座分成陽性和陰性，一個接一個交替。那是一套分類，用來配合後面的判斷規則。

alt.en: Grouping table: fire is Aries, Leo, Sagittarius; earth is Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn; air is Gemini, Libra, Aquarius; water is Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces. Four groups of three signs each.
alt.zh: 分組表：火是牡羊、獅子、射手；土是金牛、處女、摩羯；風是雙子、天秤、水瓶；水是巨蟹、天蠍、雙魚。四組各三個星座。

caption.en: The twelve signs fall into four groups of three, each sign four signs from the next.
caption.zh: 十二星座分成四組，每組三個星座，彼此隔四個星座。

caveat.en: Fixed demonstration placements, used to show how the groupings are read; the grouping shows you where to look.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置，用來示範分組怎麼讀；分組告訴你可以往哪裡看。

lines.en: Sun in Libra (air, equinoctial): opens first and gets the talk going.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤（風、分點）：先開場，先把話接起來。

lines.en: Moon in Aries (fire, equinoctial): feelings act first and think later.
lines.zh: 月亮在牡羊（火、分點）：情緒也是先動再想。

lines.en: Both lean to starting: quick off the mark, but keeping going takes practice.
lines.zh: 兩個都偏開場：起步很快，但要撐下去得刻意練習。

limitations.en: The example uses fixed demonstration placements — not a real person and not your chart.
limitations.zh: 範例是固定的示範位置，不是真人，也不是你的盤。

claim.en: “I'm an air sign, so I'm rational.”
claim.zh: 「我是風象，所以我理性。」

correction.en: A chart holds several elements at once, and what you read is how they spread. Someone with a lot of air may often reason things through, but the fire, earth and water in the same chart show up at other times.
correction.zh: 一張盤裡同時有好幾個元素，要看的是它們怎麼分布。風象多的人可能常靠講道理處理事情，但盤裡的火、土、水也會在別的時候出場。

claim.en: “Some signs are simply better.”
claim.zh: 「某些星座天生比較好。」

correction.en: Each sign has its own style, with its own strengths and weak spots: starting signs get going fast, holding signs last, shifting signs adjust quickly.
correction.zh: 每個星座各有自己的風格，也各有擅長和吃力的地方：開場的起頭快，守成的撐得久，轉換的調整快。

claim.en: “A sign explains a person.”
claim.zh: 「星座就能說明一個人。」

correction.en: A sign needs a planet to describe: the planet is the subject, and the sign says how it acts.
correction.zh: 星座要配一顆行星才有意義：行星是主詞，星座形容它怎麼做。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: what does your biggest element group make easy for you, and what does it make harder?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你最多的那一組元素，讓你哪裡比較輕鬆、哪裡比較麻煩？

objective.en: By the end you will be able to tell the twelve signs apart by two groupings — how they move and which element they belong to — and say why a sign describes a person's way of doing things.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會用「動法」和「元素」兩種分組，說出十二星座的差別，也會知道為什麼星座講的是一個人做事的方式。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: instead of reading one sign, look at how they spread.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：這一堂不讀單一星座，改看分布。

personalSteps.en: Sort the placements you are sure of into the four elements and count them.
personalSteps.zh: 把你確定的位置照元素分成四組，數數看哪一組最多。

personalSteps.en: Then sort them into starting, holding and shifting, and see which you lean to.
personalSteps.zh: 再照開場、守成、轉換分成三組，看你偏哪一種。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: does the biggest group match how you usually are?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：最多的那一組，跟你平常的樣子像不像？

reason.en: Yes — count which groups your placements fall in to see which approach you reach for.
reason.zh: 對，數數你的位置落在哪幾組，就看得出你常用哪種方式。

text.en: What a person notices first: drive, the practical, information, feeling
text.zh: 一個人先注意什麼：動力、實際、訊息、感受

reason.en: Each group has its own use; what you read is how your placements spread.
reason.zh: 四組各有各的用處，看的是你的位置怎麼分布。

text.en: Which signs are better
text.zh: 哪些星座比較好

reason.en: Part of life is what houses describe; elements are about what you notice first.
reason.zh: 生活的哪一塊是宮位在講的；元素講的是你先注意什麼。

text.en: Which part of your life
text.zh: 你生活的哪一塊

prompt.en: What do the four groups — fire, earth, air, water — describe?
prompt.zh: 火、土、風、水四組，看的是什麼？

reason.en: The planet is the subject and the sign the adjective; together they make a whole sentence.
reason.zh: 行星是主詞，星座是形容詞，兩個合起來才是一句完整的話。

text.en: A planet comes first; the sign describes how that planet works
text.zh: 要先有一顆行星，星座才是在形容某件事

reason.en: The order is sentence structure; both are needed.
reason.zh: 先後順序是句子結構，兩個都要用到。

text.en: Signs matter more than planets
text.zh: 星座比行星重要

reason.en: An adjective changes the meaning, so read it together with the planet.
reason.zh: 形容詞會改變意思，一定要一起看。

text.en: Signs are decoration and can be skipped
text.zh: 星座只是裝飾，可以不看

prompt.en: What does it mean that a sign is an adjective?
prompt.zh: 「星座是形容詞」是什麼意思？

detail.en: Book I ch. 11 separates the equinoctial and solstitial signs, the solid ones and the bicorporeal ones; ch. 12 divides the signs into masculine and feminine; ch. 18 divides the zodiac into four equilateral triangles, the first through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius. The cardinal/fixed/mutable and fire/earth/air/water names, and using elements to describe character, are later usage and are labelled as such in the text.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 11 章分出分點／至點座、固定座與雙體座；第 12 章把星座分陰陽；第 18 章把黃道分成四個等邊三角，第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手。基本／固定／變動與火土風水這些名稱，以及用元素描述性格，都是後世說法，課文已分開標示。

label.en: Book I ch. 11 (solstitial, equinoctial, solid, bicorporeal signs)
label.zh: 第一卷第 11 章（至點、分點、固定、雙體座）

label.en: Book I ch. 12 (masculine and feminine signs)
label.zh: 第一卷第 12 章（星座分陰陽）
第一卷第 18 章（四個三角）

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: A sign is an adjective: it tells you how.
summary.zh: 星座是形容詞：它說的是「怎麼做」。

title.en: The Language of the Twelve Signs
title.zh: 十二星座的性格語言

kicker.en: Mercury is about how you think and how you say it.
kicker.zh: 水星看的是你怎麼想、怎麼說。

text.en: Mercury works like “head plus mouth”: how you take news in, think it over and say it out loud. Do you talk first and think later, or think it through before you speak? Do you go straight to the point, or tell the whole story?
text.zh: 水星就像「腦袋加嘴巴」：你怎麼接收消息、怎麼想、怎麼說出口。像是你習慣先講再想，還是想清楚才開口；喜歡直接講重點，還是喜歡把來龍去脈說完。

text.en: It describes a habit. Wherever Mercury falls, each way of thinking and talking has what it does easily, and you can use that to know yourself.
text.zh: 它說的是你「習慣的方式」。不管水星落在哪裡，每一種想法和說法都有它順手的地方，可以拿來認識自己。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy says only two things about Mercury — it stays near the Sun, and it changes quickly. Book III ch. 13 gives it the rational, thinking part of the soul.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密在《四書》第一卷第 4 章寫水星，只講了兩件事——它離太陽不遠，而且變化很快。第三卷第 13 章把「理性、心智」這一塊歸給水星。

heading.en: Why it stays by the Sun

kicker.en: Your Mercury sign is your Sun sign or the one next door.
kicker.zh: 你的水星星座，不是跟太陽同一個，就是隔壁那個。

text.en: Mercury's orbit lies closer to the Sun than ours, so from Earth it always circles near the Sun. In signs, that means your Mercury is in your Sun sign or in the sign just before or after it.
text.zh: 水星的軌道比地球更靠近太陽，所以從地球看出去，它永遠在太陽附近打轉。換成星座來說：你的水星只會落在太陽星座本身，或是它前後隔壁的那一個。

text.en: That helps explain something familiar: two Libras can talk very differently, and the difference often lies in which side Mercury fell on. With Mercury also in Libra, speech minds the mood first; with Mercury in Scorpio, speech is more guarded, watching before speaking.
text.zh: 這也說明一件常見的事：兩個同樣是天秤座的人，講話方式可以差很多——差別往往就在水星落在哪一邊。水星也在天秤的人，講話先顧著氣氛；水星在天蠍的人，講話比較保留，習慣先觀察再開口。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 17 of the Tetrabiblos says Mercury “never moves more than one sign from the Sun in either direction.”
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 17 章寫，水星「在任一方向都不會離太陽超過一個星座」。

text.en: Astronomy: Mercury goes round the Sun in about 88 days, the fastest planet in the solar system (NASA figure).
text.zh: 天文資料：水星繞太陽一圈約 88 天，是太陽系裡最快的行星（依 NASA 數值）。

kicker.en: Look at your habits of handling things.
kicker.zh: 看的是你處理事情的習慣。

text.en: Find which sign your Mercury is in, then compare it with your Sun: the same sign, or next door?
text.zh: 先找到你的水星在哪個星座，再跟太陽比一比：是同一個星座，還是隔壁？

text.en: With Mercury in the Sun's sign, what you think and what you show tend to match; with Mercury next door, people often feel “what I think and what comes out are not quite the same.”
text.zh: 水星跟太陽同座的人，心裡想的跟表現出來的比較一致；落在隔壁的人，常覺得「我心裡想的，跟我說出來的不太一樣」。

text.en: Checking is simple. Hold it up against the last real conversation you had. Does it fit? Note where it fits and where it does not; both are clues to who you are.
text.zh: 對照的方法很簡單：拿你最近一次跟人說話的經驗對照看看，像不像？像的地方記下來，不像的地方也記下來，兩種都是認識自己的線索。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 13 of the Tetrabiblos warns that judgements like this need many conditions weighed together before any conclusion.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第三卷第 13 章提醒，這類判斷要把很多條件放在一起看，綜合起來才下定論。

alt.en: Diagram: a horizontal line stands for the zodiac with the Sun's glyph at the centre and Mercury's glyph on each side, inside a frame showing that Mercury only appears in that stretch near the Sun. The width is not a real measurement.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一條橫線代表黃道，中間是太陽符號，左右各有一個水星符號，外框表示水星只會出現在太陽附近這一段。寬度不是真實度數。

caption.en: Mercury always stays near the Sun, ahead of it or behind.
caption.zh: 水星總在太陽附近，可能在前，也可能在後。

caveat.en: These are fixed demonstration placements, used to show how the same Sun with a different Mercury changes the way of talking.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置，用來示範同一個太陽配上不同水星，說話方式會怎麼變。

lines.en: Sun in Libra, Mercury in Libra: thinking and talking point the same way, both minding the relationship first.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤、水星也在天秤：想的和說的方向一致，都先顧著關係。

lines.en: Move Mercury to Scorpio: speech gets more guarded, watching before speaking.
lines.zh: 如果水星改落在天蠍：講話更保留，習慣先觀察再開口。

lines.en: Same Sun sign, different way of talking — the difference is Mercury.
lines.zh: 太陽星座沒變，說話方式卻變了——差別來自水星。

limitations.en: The retrograde mark tells you Mercury appears to move backwards while the planet itself keeps moving forward; astrology is a language for describing yourself, not a guide to what to do on which day.
limitations.zh: 逆行標示告訴你水星看起來在往回走，行星本身一直往前走；占星是描述自己的語言，不拿來決定哪天該做什麼。

limitations.en: The example uses fixed demonstration placements — not a real person and not computed from your data.
limitations.zh: 範例是固定的示範位置，不是真人，也不是從你的資料算出來的。

claim.en: “Mercury shows how smart you are.”
claim.zh: 「水星代表聰不聰明。」

correction.en: Mercury is about your habits of thinking and talking, and every one of those habits has what it does well.
correction.zh: 水星看的是你習慣怎麼想、怎麼說，每一種方式都有它順手的地方。

claim.en: “Mercury can be in any sign.”
claim.zh: 「水星可以落在任何星座。」

correction.en: It always stays near the Sun, so it is your Sun sign or the sign just before or after.
correction.zh: 它永遠在太陽附近，所以只會是你的太陽星座，或前後隔壁的那一個。

claim.en: “Mercury is retrograde, so don't discuss anything today.”
claim.zh: 「水星逆行，所以今天不要談事情。」

correction.en: This app marks retrograde so you know that Mercury appears to move backwards for a while. As NASA explains, that is an effect of Earth's own motion; the planet itself keeps moving forward along its orbit. Lesson 19 covers it.
correction.zh: 本 App 會標出逆行，讓你知道那段時間水星看起來在往回走。依 NASA 的說明，這是地球自己在動造成的視覺效果，行星本身一直照著軌道往前走。第 19 堂會細講。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: do you talk first and think later, or think before you speak? Give one recent example.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你比較像先講再想，還是想清楚才開口？舉一個最近的例子。

objective.en: By the end you will know which side of you Mercury describes, and why it always stays near the Sun.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道水星在講你的哪一面，以及為什麼它總在太陽旁邊。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: find Mercury first, then see how it sits with your Sun.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：先找到水星，再看它跟太陽的關係。

personalSteps.en: Find your Mercury sign. If it changed sign on your birthday you will see two candidates — keep both for now.
personalSteps.zh: 找到你的水星星座。出生那天剛好換星座的話，會有兩個候選，兩個都先留著。

personalSteps.en: Compare it with your Sun: the same sign, the one before, or the one after?
personalSteps.zh: 跟太陽比：同一個星座，還是前一個、後一個？

personalSteps.en: Write one line about a recent time you knew exactly what you meant but did not say it clearly, and compare.
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句你最近「心裡很清楚、嘴巴卻沒講清楚」的經驗，對照看看。

reason.en: Yes — Mercury works like head plus mouth.
reason.zh: 對，水星就像腦袋加嘴巴。

text.en: How you think and talk
text.zh: 你怎麼想、怎麼說

reason.en: It describes your habits of thinking and talking.
reason.zh: 它看的是你習慣怎麼想、怎麼說。

text.en: How clever you are
text.zh: 你聰不聰明

reason.en: Mercury is about how you handle information.
reason.zh: 水星看的是你處理訊息的方式。

text.en: Whether today is lucky
text.zh: 你今天運氣好不好

prompt.en: Which side of you does Mercury mainly describe?
prompt.zh: 水星主要在講你的哪一面？

reason.en: So Mercury is your Sun sign or the one either side.
reason.zh: 所以水星只會是你的太陽星座，或前後隔壁那個。

text.en: Its orbit is inside ours, so it always looks near the Sun
text.zh: 它的軌道比地球靠近太陽，看起來永遠在太陽附近

reason.en: It is actually the fastest planet; the limit comes from where it sits relative to the Sun.
reason.zh: 它其實是最快的行星，限制來自它跟太陽的位置。

text.en: Because it moves slowly
text.zh: 因為它走得很慢

reason.en: The app computes every position; Mercury staying near the Sun is a fact of astronomy.
reason.zh: App 會算全部位置；水星總在太陽附近，是天文事實。

text.en: Because the app only computes a few signs
text.zh: 因為 App 只算幾個星座

prompt.en: Why does your Mercury sign have so few options?
prompt.zh: 為什麼你的水星星座選擇不多？

detail.en: Book I ch. 4 states that Mercury is never far removed in longitude from the Sun and therefore alternates between drying and humidifying, changing quickly; Book I ch. 17 states that it never goes more than one sign from the Sun in either direction, which is why Gemini and Virgo fell to it; Book III ch. 13 gives the rational and mental part to Mercury and the sensory part to the Moon, and says such judgments need many conditions together. Reading it as “how you think and speak” is later usage and is labelled as such.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 4 章寫水星在黃經上從不遠離太陽，因此乾濕交替、變化很快；第一卷第 17 章寫水星在任一方向都不會離太陽超過一個星座，並據此分得雙子與處女；第三卷第 13 章把理性與心智歸水星、感受的部分歸月亮，並說這類判斷要許多條件一起看。「思考與說話的方式」是後世讀法，課文已分開標示。

label.zh: 第一卷第 4 章（行星的性質）

label.zh: 第一卷第 17 章（行星各自的星座）

label.zh: 第三卷第 13 章（靈魂的性質）

title.zh: NASA NSSDCA, Mercury Fact Sheet（2024-01-11 更新）

summary.en: Mercury is about how you think and talk, and it never strays far from the Sun.
summary.zh: 水星看的是你怎麼想、怎麼說；它永遠離太陽不遠。

title.zh: 水星：思考與說話

kicker.en: Venus is about what you like and what feels worth it.
kicker.zh: 金星看的是你喜歡什麼、覺得什麼值得。

text.en: Venus is about what you like, what you value and how you show affection. Would you rather spend money on a good meal, a good-looking piece of clothing, or a trip? Do you show you like someone with gifts, with time spent together, or by saying it out loud?
text.zh: 金星看的是「你喜歡什麼、覺得什麼有價值、怎麼表達好感」。像是你願意把錢花在一頓好吃的飯、一件好看的衣服，還是一趟旅行；你表達喜歡的方式是送東西、花時間陪伴，還是直接說出口。

text.en: When you look at your own Venus, ask two things: where does this force go, and how smoothly does it run? Check straight away against what you have liked and cared about lately.
text.zh: 看自己的金星時，問兩件事：這股力氣用在哪裡？用得順不順？直接拿你最近喜歡、在意的事來對照。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy says Venus has the same mild powers as Jupiter but acts the opposite way — slightly warming because she is near the Sun, and mainly moistening. Ch. 5 counts Venus with Jupiter and the Moon as beneficent because of that mild nature; in the text the label means mild rather than extreme. Book IV ch. 4, on what kind of work a person does, says to look at Mars, Venus and Mercury.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 4 章說，金星的力量和木星一樣溫和，但作用方向相反——因為靠近太陽而稍微帶熱，主要是帶濕。第 5 章因為它性質溫和，把它和木星、月亮列為吉星；古書的吉凶，是看性質溫和還是極端。第四卷第 4 章講一個人做什麼樣的事時，說要看火星、金星、水星三顆。

kicker.en: When you read love, read Venus, the Moon and the Sun together.
kicker.zh: 讀感情時，金星、月亮、太陽一起看。

text.en: In love, Venus is about who you are drawn to, how you show affection and what feels worth it on a date; the Moon is about what you need in a relationship to feel settled; the Sun is about who you are trying to become. Read the three together to see the whole of you in love.
text.zh: 在感情裡，金星看的是你被什麼樣的人吸引、怎麼表達好感、約會時覺得什麼值得；月亮看的是你在關係裡需要什麼才安心；太陽看的是你想成為什麼樣的人。三顆一起看，才看得出你在感情裡完整的樣子。

text.en: Think back to a time someone caught your heart. What drew you in? That is the Venus part. What let you feel safe and at ease? That is the Moon part. The two answers often differ — write both down.
text.zh: 回想一段讓你心動的相處：吸引你的是什麼？那是金星的部分。讓你覺得安心、放得下心的又是什麼？那是月亮的部分。兩個答案不一樣很正常，把兩個都寫下來。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book IV ch. 5 of the Tetrabiblos, on marriage, opens by saying that for men you look at the position of the Moon, and for wives the Sun. Venus appears in descriptions of what happens when it joins them, in a supporting part.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第四卷第 5 章〈婚姻〉一開頭就說，男性的盤看月亮的位置，女性的盤看太陽。金星在那一章出現在「跟它們碰在一起會怎樣」的描述裡，是配角。

heading.en: Venus also stays near the Sun

kicker.en: Your Venus is at most two signs from your Sun sign.
kicker.zh: 你的金星，最多離太陽星座兩個星座。

text.en: Venus’s orbit also lies inside Earth’s, so from here it too always appears near the Sun — though it can sit further out than Mercury. Venus goes round the Sun in about 224.701 days (NASA figure).
text.zh: 金星的軌道也在地球內側，所以從地球看，它也永遠在太陽附近，只是可以比水星離得遠一些。金星繞太陽一圈約 224.701 天（依 NASA 數值）。

text.en: In degrees: NASA gives the semi-major axes as Venus 108.210 and Earth 149.598 million km. Treating both orbits as circles, Venus gets at most about 46 degrees from the Sun; the same arithmetic gives Mercury about 23. Venus’s orbital eccentricity is only 0.0068, almost a circle, so the real value barely changes; Mercury’s is 0.206, so its value swings much more. So your Venus sign is your Sun sign or one of those within two of it.
text.zh: 換成角度來算：依 NASA 的數值，金星的軌道半長軸 108.210、地球 149.598（百萬公里）。把兩條軌道當成圓形，金星離太陽最遠約 46 度；同樣算法，水星約 23 度。金星軌道的偏心率只有 0.0068，幾乎是圓的，實際值變化很小；水星偏心率 0.206，實際值擺動得多。所以你的金星星座，不是太陽星座本身，就是前後兩個以內的那幾個。

text.en: Two people with the same Sun sign can like very different things, and the difference often lies in where Venus fell. Among Libras, Venus in Scorpio is single-minded about what matters; Venus also in Libra likes balance and atmosphere.
text.zh: 兩個太陽星座一樣的人，喜歡的東西卻差很多，差別常常就在金星落在哪裡。同是天秤，金星在天蠍的人在意的東西很專一；金星也在天秤的人，喜歡的東西講究平衡和氣氛。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos notes that Venus is near the Sun and uses that to explain her slight warmth. Book I ch. 17, on which signs go to which planet, says Venus “at most is never more than two signs removed from the sun in either direction,” which is among the reasons Libra and Taurus went to her.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 4 章提到金星「靠近太陽」，用這點解釋它為什麼稍微帶熱。第一卷第 17 章講每顆行星分到哪些星座時寫，金星「在任一方向最多不會離太陽超過兩個星座」，這也是它分到天秤和金牛的理由之一。

alt.en: Diagram: a horizontal line for the zodiac with the Sun at the centre, Mercury's glyph on each side inside a narrow frame, and Venus's glyph on each side in a wider frame, showing Venus can sit further out. The widths are not real measurements.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一條橫線代表黃道，中間是太陽符號，內框左右各有一個水星符號，外框左右各有一個金星符號，表示金星可以離太陽稍遠。寬度不是真實度數。

caption.en: Venus and Mercury both stay near the Sun, and Venus can sit a little further out.
caption.zh: 金星和水星都在太陽附近，金星可以離得稍遠。

caveat.en: These are fixed demonstration placements, used to show how the same Sun with a different Venus changes what someone likes.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置，用來示範同一個太陽配上不同金星，喜好會怎麼變。

lines.en: Sun in Libra, Venus in Scorpio: easy-going on the outside, but single-minded about what really matters.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤、金星在天蠍：對外很好商量，真正在意的卻很專一。

lines.en: Move Venus to Libra: what they like also leans toward balance and atmosphere.
lines.zh: 如果金星改落在天秤：喜歡的東西也變成講究平衡和氣氛。

lines.en: Same Sun, different taste — the difference is where Venus fell.
lines.zh: 太陽沒變，喜好卻換了一種——差別在金星落在哪裡。

limitations.en: “About 46 degrees” treats both orbits as circles, so the real angle differs slightly.
limitations.zh: 「最遠約 46 度」是把兩條軌道當成圓形算出的近似值，實際角度會略有不同。

limitations.en: The example uses fixed demonstration placements — not a real person and not computed from your data.
limitations.zh: 範例是固定的示範位置，不是真人，也不是從你的資料算出來的。

claim.en: “For relationships, always look at Venus.”
claim.zh: 「看感情一定看金星。」

correction.en: Venus shows who you like and how you show affection; what you need to feel settled in a relationship is the Moon; who you are trying to become is the Sun. Read all three together.
correction.zh: 金星看你喜歡什麼樣的人、怎麼表達好感；你在關係裡需要什麼才安心，要看月亮；你想成為什麼樣的人，看太陽。三顆一起看才完整。

claim.en: “Venus is benefic, so Venus things go well.”
claim.zh: 「金星是吉星，所以金星的事都順。」

correction.en: “Benefic” means mild in nature: Venus is counted benefic because her nature is mild. When you read your own Venus, look at where the force goes and how smoothly it runs.
correction.zh: 吉星指的是性質溫和：金星被列為吉星，是因為它性質溫和。讀自己的金星時，看的是這股力氣用在哪裡、用得順不順。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: what makes something feel worth it to you — and does that match how your Sun comes across?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你覺得「值得」的標準是什麼？跟你太陽給人的樣子一樣嗎？

objective.en: By the end you will know which side of you Venus describes, why it stays near the Sun, and which bodies to read together when you look at love.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道金星在講你的哪一面、為什麼它總在太陽附近，以及讀感情時要把哪幾顆星一起看。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: find Venus first, then set it beside your Sun.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：先找到金星，再跟太陽比一比。

personalSteps.en: Find your Venus sign. If it changed sign on your birthday you will see two candidates — keep both for now.
personalSteps.zh: 找到你的金星星座。出生那天剛好換星座的話，會有兩個候選，兩個都先留著。

personalSteps.en: Compare it with your Sun: the same sign, or one of those beside it?
personalSteps.zh: 跟太陽比：同一個星座，還是前後那幾個？

personalSteps.en: Write one line about the last thing you spent money or time on and felt was worth it, and compare.
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句你最近「花錢或花時間，覺得很值得」的事，對照看看。

reason.en: Yes — what draws you and what settles you often differ, so read both.
reason.zh: 對，吸引你的和讓你安心的常常不一樣，兩個都要看。

text.en: Venus shows what you like, the Moon what you need to feel settled
text.zh: 金星看你喜歡什麼，月亮看你需要什麼才安心

reason.en: Venus is worked out accurately; you read both because they describe different things.
reason.zh: 金星算得很準；兩顆一起看，是因為它們講的是不同的事。

text.en: Because Venus is worked out badly
text.zh: 因為金星算不準

reason.en: Venus shows what draws you and how you show affection — an important part of love.
reason.zh: 金星看你被什麼吸引、怎麼表達好感，是感情裡重要的一塊。

text.en: Because Venus has nothing to do with love
text.zh: 因為金星跟感情無關

prompt.en: Why read Venus and the Moon together for love?
prompt.zh: 讀感情時，為什麼要把金星和月亮一起看？

reason.en: So Venus usually sits close to your Sun sign.
reason.zh: 所以金星通常在太陽星座前後不遠的地方。

text.en: Its orbit is inside Earth’s, so it always looks near the Sun
text.zh: 它的軌道在地球內側，看起來總在太陽附近

reason.en: It goes round in about 224.701 days; the few options come from where it sits relative to the Sun.
reason.zh: 它約 224.701 天繞一圈；選擇不多，是因為它總在太陽附近。

text.en: Because Venus is the slowest
text.zh: 因為金星走得最慢

reason.en: What decides Venus’s sign is where it is in its stretch near the Sun at the time.
reason.zh: 決定金星星座的，是它當時在太陽附近的哪一段。

text.en: Because Venus only enters benefic signs
text.zh: 因為金星只走吉星的星座

prompt.en: Why does your Venus sign have few options?
prompt.zh: 為什麼你的金星星座選擇不多？

detail.en: Book I ch. 4 gives Venus the same tempered powers as Jupiter, warming mildly through nearness to the Sun and chiefly humidifying; Book I ch. 17 states that she is at most never more than two signs from the Sun in either direction; ch. 5 counts her beneficent on account of that tempered nature; Book IV ch. 4 reads the quality of action from Mars, Venus and Mercury; Book IV ch. 5 opens by observing the Moon for men and the Sun for wives. Reading Venus as taste and value is later usage and is labelled as such, and the chapter's framing of gender and marriage is not carried over.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 4 章寫金星與木星同屬溫和、靠近太陽而稍帶熱、主要帶濕；第一卷第 17 章寫金星在任一方向最多不離太陽超過兩個星座；第 5 章把金星列為吉星，理由是性質溫和；第四卷第 4 章說行動的性質要看火星、金星、水星；第四卷第 5 章開頭說男性看月亮、妻子看太陽。「喜歡什麼、覺得什麼有價值」是後世讀法，課文已分開標示；該章的性別與婚姻框架未沿用。

label.zh: 第一卷第 4 章（行星的性質）

label.en: Book I ch. 5 (beneficent and maleficent planets)
label.zh: 第一卷第 5 章（吉星與凶星）

label.en: Book I ch. 17 (the houses of the several planets)
label.zh: 第一卷第 17 章（行星各自的星座）

label.en: Book IV ch. 4 (the quality of action)
label.zh: 第四卷第 4 章（行動的性質）

detail.zh: 公轉週期 224.701 天、半長軸 108.210 百萬公里、軌道偏心率 0.00677。「不超過兩個星座」這個界線由原文第一卷第 17 章提供；「最遠約 46 度」是本課以這些數值假設圓軌道換算，不是原文或本表寫出的數字。

title.zh: NASA NSSDCA, Venus Fact Sheet（2024-01-11 更新）

summary.en: Venus is about what you like and what feels worth having.
summary.zh: 金星看的是你喜歡什麼、覺得什麼值得。

title.zh: 金星：喜歡與價值

kicker.en: Mars is about how you push and how you get angry.
kicker.zh: 火星看的是你怎麼出力、怎麼生氣。

text.en: Mars is about drive, push and the way you get angry. Faced with something unfair, do you speak up on the spot, or hold it in and think it over at home? With a hard job, do you charge through in one go, or push a little every day?
text.zh: 火星看的是「行動力、衝勁、你怎麼生氣」。像是遇到不公平的事，你會馬上站出來講，還是先忍著、回家再想；要完成一件難事，你是一口氣衝完，還是每天推一點。

text.en: When you look at your own Mars, ask two things: where does this force usually go? Can you put it down afterwards? You can answer both from your own recent experience.
text.zh: 看自己的火星時，問兩件事：這股力氣平常用在哪裡？用完以後收得回來嗎？這兩個問題可以直接拿你最近的經驗來回答。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy says the nature of Mars is mainly to dry and to burn, in keeping with its fiery colour and its nearness to the Sun’s sphere. Ch. 5 counts Mars and Saturn as maleficent — Mars for too much dryness, Saturn for too much cold; the label rests on whether a nature is mild or extreme. Book IV ch. 4 makes Mars one of the three planets to look at for what kind of work a person does.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 4 章說，火星的性質主要是乾燥和燃燒，因為它是火紅色，又靠近太陽那一層。第 5 章把火星和土星列為凶星——火星是太乾，土星是太冷；分吉凶看的是性質溫和還是極端。第四卷第 4 章講一個人做什麼樣的事時，火星是要看的三顆之一。

kicker.en: Mars changes sign about every two months on average.
kicker.zh: 火星平均大約兩個月換一個星座。

text.en: Mars goes round the Sun in about 686.980 days (NASA figure). Shared across twelve signs, that is about two months a sign. It is an average — retrograde motion can take it back and forth inside one sign, so a single stay can be longer.
text.zh: 火星繞太陽一圈約 686.980 天（依 NASA 數值），平均分給十二個星座，每個星座大約待兩個月。這是平均值——逆行會讓它在同一個星座裡來回走，實際待得可能更久。

text.en: So a Mars sign changes far more slowly than the Moon’s, and people born in the same month often share one. To tell people apart, add the house it fell in, and that needs a birth time.
text.zh: 所以火星星座換得比月亮慢很多，同一個月出生的人，常常是同一個火星星座。要看出每個人的不同，再加上它落在哪一宮，那需要出生時間。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy talks about the qualities of Mars and its positions relative to the other bodies.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密談的是火星的性質，以及它和其他星體的位置關係。

kicker.en: Mars is about how you push.
kicker.zh: 火星看的是你怎麼使力。

text.en: Mars describes how you push. Hands on first, or terms first? More force when blocked, or a different route? When angry, does it come out or stay in? It describes the way you push.
text.zh: 火星描述你出力的方式：先動手，還是先談條件？被擋住時加大力氣，還是換條路？生氣時是爆出來，還是悶著？它描述的是你使力的方式。

text.en: Mars and the Sun can point different ways: the side the Sun wants seen and the place you are willing to put in effort may be two separate things.
text.zh: 火星和太陽可以往不同方向：太陽想被看見的那一面，和你真正願意出力的地方，可能是兩回事。

text.en: When you check yourself, looking at the gap between the two is often more useful than the Mars sign alone. Ask yourself: is what you most want to put effort into the same as the self you want others to see?
text.zh: 對照自己時，看看這兩者之間的落差，常常比單看火星星座更有用。想一想：你最願意出力的事，和你希望別人看到的你，是同一件事嗎？

text.en: What the old texts say: Book IV ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos places Mars inside the question of what kind of work a person does, together with Venus and Mercury, and adds that the sign it is in matters.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第四卷第 4 章把火星放在「一個人做什麼樣的事」這個問題裡，跟金星、水星一起看，還說要看它所在的星座。

alt.en: Table: the Moon stays in a sign about two days, the Sun about a month, Mars about two months, Jupiter about a year and Saturn about two and a half years. All averages from NASA orbit periods; retrograde motion changes any single pass.
alt.zh: 對照表：月亮一個星座約兩天多，太陽約一個月，火星約兩個月，木星約一年，土星約兩年半。都是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值，逆行會讓實際時間不同。

caption.en: Roughly how long each body stays in one sign. The figures are averages worked out from NASA orbit periods.
caption.zh: 幾顆星體在一個星座大約待多久。數字是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值。

caveat.en: These are fixed demonstration placements, used to show how the same Sun with a different Mars changes the way someone pushes.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置，用來示範同一個太陽配上不同火星，使力的方式會怎麼變。

lines.en: Sun in Libra, Mars in Capricorn: polite when talking, but pushes a job right to the end.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤、火星在摩羯：講話客氣，做事卻硬推到底。

lines.en: Move Mars to Cancer: the effort goes into protecting people first, the task second.
lines.zh: 如果火星改落在巨蟹：出力的方式變成先護著人，再處理事。

lines.en: Same Sun, a completely different way of pushing — the difference is Mars.
lines.zh: 太陽沒變，使力的方式卻完全不同——差別來自火星。

limitations.en: The example uses fixed demonstration placements — not a real person and not your chart.
limitations.zh: 範例是固定的示範位置，不是真人，也不是你的盤。

claim.en: “Mars is malefic, so Mars things go badly.”
claim.zh: 「火星是凶星，所以火星的事都不好。」

correction.en: “Malefic” means an extreme nature — too much dryness. When you read your own Mars, look at where the force goes and whether you can put it down afterwards.
correction.zh: 凶星的「凶」指的是性質太極端（太乾）。讀自己的火星時，看的是這股力氣用在哪裡、用完收不收得回來。

claim.en: “A Mars sign shows how big someone's temper is.”
claim.zh: 「火星星座可以看出一個人脾氣大小。」

correction.en: Mars describes the way you push. People born in the same month often share a Mars sign, so telling them apart also takes the house it fell in.
correction.zh: 火星講的是出力的方式。同一個月出生的人常是同一個火星星座，要分出每個人的不同，還要看它落在哪一宮。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: does the way you push match the way you want to be seen?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你出力的方式，跟你希望被看到的樣子一樣嗎？

objective.en: By the end you will know which side of you Mars describes, how long it stays in a sign, and how to check the force it stands for against your own life.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道火星在講你的哪一面、它在一個星座待多久，以及怎麼拿自己的經驗對照火星這股力氣。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: find Mars, then think of something you recently really pushed on.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：先找到火星，再想一件你最近真的出過力的事。

personalSteps.en: Find your Mars sign. If it changed sign on your birthday, keep both candidates for now.
personalSteps.zh: 找到你的火星星座。出生那天剛好換星座的話，兩個候選都先留著。

personalSteps.en: Compare it with your Sun: the same direction, or not quite?
personalSteps.zh: 跟太陽比：方向一樣，還是不太一樣？

personalSteps.en: Write one line about the last time you forced something through, and see which side it looks like.
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句你最近「硬撐過去」的事，看看比較像哪一邊。

reason.zh: 對，火星看的是你使力的方式，和用完收不收得回來。

text.zh: 你會不會遇到意外

prompt.zh: 火星主要在講你的哪一面？

title.zh: NASA NSSDCA, Mars Fact Sheet（2025-05-19 更新）

summary.en: Mars is about how you push and how you get angry.
summary.zh: 火星看的是你怎麼出力、怎麼生氣。

title.zh: 火星：行動與衝勁

kicker.en: Jupiter is about reaching out, Saturn about setting limits.
kicker.zh: 木星看你往外擴，土星看你設下限度。

text.en: Jupiter is about reaching out and giving you room: where you are willing to try more and trust a little more. Saturn is about limits, duty and slow build-up: where you hold yourself to the rules and go one step at a time.
text.zh: 木星看的是「往外擴、給你機會」的地方：你在哪裡願意多嘗試、多相信一點。土星看的是「設限、責任、慢慢累積」的地方：你在哪裡要求自己守規矩、一步一步來。

text.en: The two are easiest to read side by side: one reaches out, one holds in. Learning something new, the Jupiter side wants to sign up for more classes and meet more people, while the Saturn side wants to get the basics solid first.
text.zh: 兩顆放在一起看最好懂：一邊往外、一邊收住。像學一樣新東西時，木星那一邊想多報幾門課、多認識人，土星那一邊想先把基本功練扎實。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy says Jupiter’s force is mild because its sphere lies between Saturn’s cooling and Mars’s burning; it both heats and moistens, and so brings winds that help things grow. The same chapter says Saturn mainly cools and dries a little, probably because it is furthest from the Sun’s heat. Ch. 5 counts Jupiter beneficent and Saturn maleficent, on a mild versus extreme nature.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 4 章說，木星的作用溫和，因為它的軌道在土星的冷和火星的燒中間；它帶熱也帶濕，所以會帶來助長生長的風。同一章說土星主要是使冷、稍微使乾，推測是因為它離太陽的熱最遠。第 5 章依性質溫和或極端，把木星列為吉星、土星列為凶星。

kicker.en: Jupiter changes sign about once a year, Saturn about every two and a half years.
kicker.zh: 木星大約一年換一個星座，土星大約兩年半。

text.en: Jupiter goes round the Sun in about 4,332.589 days (roughly 11.9 years) and Saturn in about 10,755.699 days (roughly 29.5 years), both NASA figures. Shared across twelve signs, Jupiter stays about a year in each and Saturn about two and a half. These are averages too; retrograde motion changes any single stay.
text.zh: 木星繞太陽一圈約 4,332.589 天（約 11.9 年），土星約 10,755.699 天（約 29.5 年），都依 NASA 數值。平均分給十二個星座，木星在一個星座大約待一年，土星大約兩年半。這也是平均值，逆行會讓實際停留時間不同。

text.en: So these two signs are shared by a whole group of people: those born in the same year usually share a Jupiter sign, and those two or three years apart often share a Saturn sign. They describe a backdrop a generation has in common. To read the part that is yours, add the house it fell in, and that needs a birth time.
text.zh: 所以這兩顆的星座，是一批人共用的：同年出生的人木星星座通常一樣，差兩三歲的人土星星座也常一樣。它們講的是一個世代共同的背景；要讀出你個人的部分，再看它落在哪一宮，那需要出生時間。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy writes that Saturn is furthest from the Sun’s heat and that Jupiter’s sphere lies between Saturn’s and Mars’s.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密寫到土星離太陽的熱最遠、木星的軌道在土星和火星之間。

kicker.en: Read them together: where you dare to try, and where you prepare first.
kicker.zh: 兩顆一起看：你在哪裡敢試，在哪裡要先準備。

text.en: A more useful question: where do you let yourself just try things (the Jupiter side)? And where do you feel you must be fully prepared before you start (the Saturn side)? You need both; together they keep things moving. Notice which matters each side covers in your own life.
text.zh: 比較實用的問法是：你在什麼事情上容易放手去試（木星那一邊）？又在什麼事情上，總覺得要先準備好才能開始（土星那一邊）？兩邊都需要，搭配起來事情才走得動。看看這兩邊在你身上各用在哪些事情上。

text.en: On your chart, first find the sign each of them is in, then the house. The sign tells you the style of each force, and the house tells you which part of life it goes into; houses need a birth time.
text.zh: 在你的盤上，先看木星和土星各落在哪個星座，再看它們落在哪一宮。星座告訴你這兩股力氣的風格，宮位告訴你它們用在生活的哪一塊；宮位要有出生時間才看得到。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 5 of the Tetrabiblos, the labels rest on a mild versus extreme nature; the text also says judgements like this need many conditions weighed together.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 5 章的吉凶，看的是性質溫和還是極端，原文也說，這類判斷要把很多條件放在一起看。

alt.en: Table: the Moon stays in a sign about two days, the Sun about a month, Mars about two months, Jupiter about a year and Saturn about two and a half years. All averages from NASA orbit periods; retrograde motion changes any single pass.
alt.zh: 對照表：月亮一個星座約兩天多，太陽約一個月，火星約兩個月，木星約一年，土星約兩年半。都是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值，逆行會讓實際時間不同。

caption.en: Jupiter and Saturn beside the others for pace. The figures are averages worked out from NASA orbit periods.
caption.zh: 把木星、土星放回其他星體旁邊比速度。數字是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值。

caveat.en: Fixed demonstration placements, used to show both sides at once. People born in the same year often share these two.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置，用來示範兩邊怎麼同時出現。同年出生的人，這兩個位置常常一樣。

lines.en: Jupiter in Gemini: happy to ask around and try things, gathering first and deciding later.
lines.zh: 木星在雙子：願意多問、多試，先收集再決定。

lines.en: Saturn in Capricorn: holds themselves to the rules, and will not speak until prepared.
lines.zh: 土星在摩羯：要求自己照規矩來，沒準備好就不開口。

lines.en: Both at once: plenty they want to try, but each one rehearsed three times before speaking.
lines.zh: 兩邊同時存在：想試的事很多，開口前卻先排練三遍。

limitations.en: Jupiter and Saturn placements describe your tendencies, not luck, and are not used to predict what happens in any year.
limitations.zh: 木星、土星的位置描述的是你的傾向，不是運氣，也不拿來預測哪一年會發生什麼事。

limitations.en: The example uses fixed demonstration placements, not a real person.
limitations.zh: 範例是固定的示範位置，不是真人。

claim.en: “Saturn means bad luck and Jupiter means good luck.”
claim.zh: 「土星代表倒楣，木星代表好運。」

correction.en: Benefic and malefic mean mild versus extreme in nature. When you read these two, look at where you let yourself try and where you prepare first.
correction.zh: 吉星、凶星指的是性質溫和還是極端。讀這兩顆時，看的是你在哪裡放手去試、在哪裡先求準備。

claim.en: “A Jupiter sign shows a person's character.”
claim.zh: 「木星星座可以看出一個人的個性。」

correction.en: Jupiter changes sign about once a year, so most people born in the same year share one. Reading the personal part takes the houses, and houses need a birth time.
correction.zh: 木星大約一年才換一個星座，同年出生的人大多一樣；要讀出個人的部分，再看宮位，而宮位要出生時間。

claim.en: “Where Saturn falls is where I fail.”
claim.zh: 「土星落的地方，就是我做不好的地方。」

correction.en: Saturn shows where you make yourself go slowly and prepare first. Things there often start late, but built up step by step they tend to be the most solid.
correction.zh: 土星看的是你要求自己慢慢來、先準備好的地方。那裡常常起步慢，但一步一步累積下來，往往最扎實。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: do you more often act because you want to try, or because you feel ready?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你比較常因為「想試」而動手，還是因為「準備好了」才動手？

objective.en: By the end you will know which side of you Jupiter and Saturn each describe, why they are easiest to read together, and what their slowness means.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道木星和土星各在講你的哪一面、為什麼兩顆一起看最好懂，以及它們走得慢代表什麼。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: these two only show up when you hold them against real experience.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：這兩顆要對照真實經驗才看得出來。

personalSteps.en: Find your Jupiter and Saturn signs.
personalSteps.zh: 找到你的木星和土星星座。

personalSteps.en: Think of something you just went ahead and tried, and something you keep waiting to be ready for.
personalSteps.zh: 想一件你放手去試過的事，和一件你一直在等「準備好」的事。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: which of the two is more like your usual self?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：這兩件事裡，哪一邊比較像平常的你？

reason.en: Yes — one reaches out, one holds in, and together they keep things moving.
reason.zh: 對，一邊往外擴、一邊收住，兩邊搭配事情才走得動。

text.en: Where you dare to try, and where you prepare first
text.zh: 你在哪裡敢放手去試、在哪裡要先準備好

reason.en: The two describe your tendencies, as a way to know your own pace.
reason.zh: 這兩顆描述的是你的傾向，用來認識自己做事的節奏。

text.en: Which year will bring good luck
text.zh: 哪一年會走好運

reason.en: That is what Mercury describes.
reason.zh: 那是水星在講的。

text.en: How you think and talk
text.zh: 你怎麼想、怎麼說

prompt.en: What do you read when you look at Jupiter and Saturn together?
prompt.zh: 把木星和土星一起看，看的是什麼？

reason.en: From the NASA figures: about a year a sign for Jupiter, two and a half for Saturn.
reason.zh: 依 NASA 數值算，木星大約一年一個、土星大約兩年半一個。

text.en: They change sign slowly, so people born around the same time share them
text.zh: 它們換星座很慢，差不多時間出生的人大多是同一個星座

reason.en: A chart records direction; the real reason is how slowly they change sign.
reason.zh: 盤記的是方向；真正的理由是它們換星座的速度。

text.en: Because they are the furthest away
text.zh: 因為它們離地球最遠

reason.en: A few years apart, they differ; only people born around the same time share them.
reason.zh: 差幾年出生就會不同；差不多時間出生的人才會相同。

text.en: Because everyone has the same Jupiter and Saturn
text.zh: 因為每個人的木星、土星都一樣

prompt.en: Why are Jupiter and Saturn said to describe a backdrop a group shares?
prompt.zh: 為什麼說木星和土星講的是一批人共同的背景？

detail.en: Book I ch. 4 gives Jupiter a temperate force because its sphere lies between Saturn's cooling and Mars's burning, heating and humidifying and so producing fertilizing winds; the same chapter gives Saturn chiefly cooling and moderately drying, probably through being furthest from the Sun's heat. Ch. 5 counts Jupiter beneficent and Saturn maleficent on tempered versus extreme nature. Pairing them as expansion and limit, and reading them as opportunity and duty, are later usage and labelled as such.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 4 章說木星作用溫和，因軌道位在土星的冷與火星的燒之間，既熱又濕、產生助長生長的風；同章說土星主要使冷、稍微使乾，推測因離太陽的熱最遠。第 5 章把木星列為吉星、土星列為凶星，依據是性質溫和或極端。「擴張與收斂」的配對、「機會」與「責任」的讀法都是後世說法，課文已分開標示。

title.zh: NASA NSSDCA, Saturn Fact Sheet（2025-03-18 更新）

summary.en: Jupiter and Saturn move slowly; Jupiter shows where you reach out, Saturn where you set limits.
summary.zh: 木星和土星走得很慢；木星看你往外擴的地方，土星看你設下限度的地方。

title.en: Jupiter and Saturn: Expansion and Limit
title.zh: 木星與土星：擴張與收斂

kicker.en: Your chart has ten bodies; the outer three were found with telescopes.
kicker.zh: 盤上有十顆星，最外面的三顆是用望遠鏡才找到的。

text.en: All three were found only once there were telescopes (NASA): Uranus was discovered in 1781 by William Herschel, the first planet found with a telescope; Neptune was discovered in 1846; Pluto was discovered in 1930 and reclassified as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union in 2006. So your chart holds ten bodies in all: the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn, which the eye can see, plus these three outer planets.
text.zh: 這三顆都是有了望遠鏡才找到的（依 NASA）：天王星在一七八一年由 William Herschel 用望遠鏡發現，是第一顆靠望遠鏡找到的行星；海王星在一八四六年發現；冥王星在一九三〇年發現，二〇〇六年被國際天文聯合會重新分類為矮行星。所以你的盤上一共有十顆星：太陽、月亮、水星、金星、火星、木星、土星這七顆肉眼看得到，再加上這三顆外行星。

text.en: The outer planets are slow and far away, so read them as the backdrop: the first seven describe how you yourself think, love and push, and the outer three describe what the times you live in are pushing for.
text.zh: 外行星走得慢、離得遠，讀的時候先把它們當成背景：前面七顆講的是你個人怎麼想、怎麼愛、怎麼出力，後面三顆講的是你身處的時代在推動什麼。

text.en: Open your chart and count: read the first seven to see yourself clearly, then come back to where the outer three fall and think about what your generation has been through together.
text.zh: 打開你的盤數一數：先讀前七顆，看清楚你個人的樣子；再回頭看後三顆落在哪裡，想想你這一代人一起經歷過什麼。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy sets out each planet’s nature one by one and names seven — Sun, Moon, Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus and Mercury. Ch. 5 sorts the same seven into beneficent and maleficent. These seven are all the planets visible to the eye.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 4 章一顆一顆寫出行星的性質，列的是太陽、月亮、土星、火星、木星、金星、水星，共七顆；第 5 章分吉凶時也是這七顆。這七顆就是肉眼看得到的全部行星。

heading.en: Slow enough to mean a generation

kicker.en: An outer planet takes seven to twenty years to change sign.
kicker.zh: 外行星換一個星座，要七到二十年。

text.en: From NASA figures, Uranus goes round the Sun in about 30,685.400 days, Neptune in about 60,189.018 days and Pluto in about 90,560 days. Shared across twelve signs, that is roughly seven, fourteen and twenty years a sign. NASA also records that the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006.
text.zh: 依 NASA 數值，天王星繞太陽一圈約 30,685.400 天，海王星約 60,189.018 天，冥王星約 90,560 天。平均分給十二個星座，每個星座大約分別待七年、十四年、二十年。NASA 也記載，國際天文聯合會在 2006 年把冥王星重新分類為矮行星。

text.en: At that pace, one sign holds a whole generation. So an outer planet’s sign describes the times a generation shares: Uranus in a given sign, for instance, describes the mood shared by everyone born in those years. Getting down to you takes the house it fell in on your chart, and houses need a birth time.
text.zh: 走這麼慢，代表同一個星座裡會塞進一整批人。所以外行星的星座，講的是一整代人共同的時代背景：比如天王星在某個星座，描述的是那幾年出生的整批人共有的時代氣氛。要落到你個人，再看它在你盤上的哪一宮，而宮位需要出生時間。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy’s planets end at Saturn; Book I ch. 4 of the Tetrabiblos calls Saturn the one furthest from the Sun’s heat.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密的行星排到土星為止；《四書》第一卷第 4 章說，土星是離太陽的熱最遠的那一顆。

kicker.en: Read the outer planets as your generation’s backdrop.
kicker.zh: 把外行星當成你這一代的時代背景來讀。

text.en: Uranus is about breaking with convention, Neptune about things with blurred edges (imagination, and self-deception too), and Pluto about thorough change. Take Uranus: ask which convention your generation is most used to breaking.
text.zh: 天王星看的是打破慣例，海王星看的是界線模糊的事（想像，也包括自我欺騙），冥王星看的是一段徹底的改變。拿天王星來說，可以問：我這一代人最習慣打破的，是哪一種慣例？

text.en: A useful way to read them is as the questions your generation faced together, and then look at how you yourself answered.
text.zh: 好用的讀法，是把它們當成「你這一代共同面對的題目」，再看你自己是怎麼回應的。

text.en: This app computes the positions of all three and shows them on your chart as they are, so you can see where your generation falls.
text.zh: 本 App 會照實算出這三顆的位置，照實顯示在你的盤上，讓你看見自己這一代落在哪裡。

text.en: What the old texts say: when Book I ch. 5 of the Tetrabiblos sorts beneficent from maleficent, it too uses the seven planets visible to the eye.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 5 章分吉凶時，用的也是那七顆肉眼看得到的行星。

caveat.en: An illustration of how people of one generation each answer the same times.
caveat.zh: 這是說明用的對照，用來示範同一代人怎麼各自回應同一個時代。

lines.en: Two people a year apart almost certainly share all three outer signs.
lines.zh: 兩個差一歲的人，外行星星座幾乎一定一樣。

lines.en: Yet the youngest child and the eldest answer the same era’s questions in completely different ways.
lines.zh: 可是一個是家裡最小的、一個是老大，面對同一個時代的題目，反應完全不同。

lines.en: So the outer planets set the question; what makes each person different shows up elsewhere.
lines.zh: 所以外行星講的是題目，每個人的不同要從別的地方看。

limitations.en: Outer-planet placements describe a generation’s backdrop; they do not predict events or years and are no verdict on your life.
limitations.zh: 外行星的位置描述的是一代人的時代背景，不拿來預測事件或年份，也不是對你人生的宣判。

limitations.en: The example is an illustration, not a real case, and uses no real birth data.
limitations.zh: 範例是說明用的對照，不是真人案例，也沒有用任何真實出生資料。

claim.en: “Your Pluto placement is your fate.”
claim.zh: 「冥王星的位置代表你的宿命。」

correction.en: Pluto changes sign about every twenty years, so a placement is shared by a whole generation and describes that generation’s backdrop.
correction.zh: 冥王星大約二十年才換一個星座，同一個位置是一整代人共用的，描述的是那一代的時代背景。

claim.en: “Uranus is in that sign, so I am rebellious.”
claim.zh: 「天王星在那個星座，所以我很叛逆。」

correction.en: One Uranus sign is shared by a whole generation and describes the question that generation faces; how you yourself answer shows in the first seven bodies and in the house it falls in on your chart.
correction.zh: 同一個天王星星座是一整代人共用的，講的是那一代共同面對的題目；你個人怎麼回應，要看前面七顆，以及它落在你盤上的哪一宮。

claim.en: “Pluto was demoted, so ignore it.”
claim.zh: 「冥王星被降級了，所以不用看。」

correction.en: The 2006 reclassification is about how astronomy sorts things. Its position is shown as computed, and you read it the same way as the other two: as a generation’s backdrop.
correction.zh: 2006 年的重新分類，是天文學怎麼分類的問題。盤上照實顯示它的位置，讀它的方式跟另外兩顆外行星一樣：當成時代背景。

detail.en: Book I ch. 4 sets out the natures of seven planets — Sun, Moon, Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Mercury — and ch. 5 sorts the same seven into beneficent and maleficent. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto do not appear in the Tetrabiblos, which is the basis for saying their readings have no classical source.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 4 章逐顆寫出七顆行星（太陽、月亮、土星、火星、木星、金星、水星）的性質，第 5 章以同樣七顆分吉凶。天王星、海王星、冥王星在《四書》中未出現，本課即以此說明外行星的解讀沒有古典出處。

label.en: Book I ch. 4 (the power of the planets)

title.zh: 外行星：世代的背景音

kicker.en: Signs need only a date; houses need the moment.
kicker.zh: 星座只要日期，宮位要出生那一刻。

text.en: An easy way to hold it: signs are the sky's own divisions, there all year and the same for everyone; houses only exist when you look out from the moment and place you were born. Picture the two as layers: the outer ring divides the sky, the inner ring divides the view from the ground where you stand.
text.zh: 可以這樣記：星座是天空自己的分段，一整年都在那裡，誰看都一樣；宮位是從你出生那一刻、那個地點看出去，才有的分段。把兩層疊在一起看：外圈是天空的分段，內圈是你所在的地面看出去的分段。

text.en: So two people born the same day at different hours share almost every sign and can share no houses at all. That is why a birthday alone cannot tell two people apart.
text.zh: 所以同一天出生、不同時間的兩個人，星座幾乎一樣，宮位卻可以完全不同。這也是為什麼只看生日，分不出兩個人的差別。

text.en: Finding the houses on a chart: start at the line marked ASC and count downward, anticlockwise — house one, house two, and on round to house twelve. Each house looks at one area of life: house one is how you come across, house four is home, house seven is partners and the people you work with, house ten is your work and public standing. The sign says how a planet acts; the house says where in life it acts.
text.zh: 在盤上找宮位：從標著 ASC 的那條線開始，往下逆時針數，第一宮、第二宮……一路數到第十二宮。每一宮看的是一塊生活場景：第一宮是你給人的樣子，第四宮是家，第七宮是伴侶和合作的人，第十宮是工作和外面的名聲。星座說一顆星「用什麼方式」表現，宮位說它「在生活哪一塊」表現。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy takes the degree on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth as the chart's starting point. William Lilly's Christian Astrology of 1647, in “Of the Twelve Houses,” goes house by house through what each one covers; the first is life, stature and form.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密在《四書》第三卷第 2 章，用出生那一刻東方地平線上的度數，當作整張盤的起點。William Lilly 一六四七年的《Christian Astrology》在〈Of the Twelve Houses〉一宮一宮寫出各宮管的事，第一宮管生命、身材和樣貌。

kicker.en: The Earth keeps turning; two hours out and every house shifts.
kicker.zh: 地球一直在轉，差兩小時，宮位就整組移位。

text.en: The Earth turns once in about 23.9345 hours (NASA figure), and in that time the twelve signs take turns crossing the eastern horizon, roughly two hours each. Two hours out moves the starting point by a sign, and the whole set of houses shifts with it.
text.zh: 地球自轉一圈大約 23.9345 小時（依 NASA 數值），這段時間裡十二個星座輪流經過東方地平線，平均大約兩小時換一個。差兩小時，起點就換一個星座，整組宮位跟著移位。

text.en: So the twelve houses appear on your chart once you enter a birth time. Until then the house layer stays empty, and the signs your planets are in still show. The more exact the time, the more exact the Ascendant and houses; if a birth certificate or a family memory gives a time, start with that.
text.zh: 所以填好出生時間，命盤上才會出現十二宮。還沒有時間時，宮位這一層會空著，行星落在哪個星座照樣看得到。出生時間越準，上升和宮位就越準；手邊有出生證明或家人記得的時刻，就先填那個。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos is entirely about how to fix the rising degree for the moment of birth. The text is plain: the starting point comes from the moment.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第三卷第 2 章整章都在講「出生那一刻的上升度數怎麼定」。原文說得很清楚：起點來自時刻。

kicker.en: There is more than one way to divide houses, so sites often differ.
kicker.zh: 分宮的方法不只一種，網站之間不同多半是方法不同。

text.en: This app divides houses with Placidus by default. Very far north or south, Placidus has no answer, so the app switches to whole sign houses and says on screen that it switched and why, so you always know where the houses in front of you came from.
text.zh: 本 App 預設用 Placidus 分宮。在緯度非常高的地方，Placidus 會算不出來，這時會改用整宮制（whole sign），並在畫面上寫明換了方法和原因，讓你清楚知道眼前的宮位是怎麼來的。

text.en: There have always been several ways to divide houses. If another site shows you different houses, it has usually used a different method. Check which one you are reading, and the two can sit side by side.
text.zh: 分宮的方法本來就有好幾種。如果你在別的網站看到的宮位跟這裡不一樣，多半是用了不同的分宮方法。先看清楚自己看的是哪一種，兩邊就能放在一起對照。

text.en: What the old texts say: in “Of the Twelve Houses,” Lilly goes house by house through what each one covers; the first, for example, is life, stature and form.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 在〈Of the Twelve Houses〉一宮一宮寫出各宮管什麼事，例如第一宮管生命、身材和樣貌。

alt.en: Diagram: a double ring. The outer ring is divided into twelve parts for the signs, the inner ring stands for the houses, and a horizontal line on the left is labelled ASC, where the houses are counted from. A concept figure with no real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個雙層圓環，外圈分成十二等分代表十二星座，內圈代表十二宮，左側有一條水平線標著 ASC，代表宮位的起算點。概念圖，沒有真實度數。

caption.en: Signs on the outer ring, houses on the inner ring; the starting point on the left comes from the moment of birth.
caption.zh: 外圈是星座，內圈是宮位，左邊的起算點來自出生時刻。

caveat.en: A made-up comparison for explanation, built on imagined birth data.
caveat.zh: 這是為了說明而虛構的對照，用的是假想的出生資料。

lines.en: Two people born the same day four hours apart: nearly the same Sun and Moon signs.
lines.zh: 同一天出生、差四小時的兩個人：太陽、月亮星座幾乎一樣。

lines.en: But their Ascendants are two signs apart, and every house shifts with it.
lines.zh: 但上升差了兩個星座，整組宮位跟著移位。

lines.en: The same Sun in a different house points at a different part of life.
lines.zh: 同一個太陽，落在不同宮，講的生活場景就不一樣。

limitations.en: Without a birth time there is no Ascendant and no houses; that layer stays empty until you enter a real birth time.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間就沒有上升和宮位，命盤上這一層會空著，等你填入真正的出生時間再算。

claim.en: “Houses and signs are the same thing.”
claim.zh: 「宮位和星座是同一件事。」

correction.en: Signs need only a date; houses need the moment and the place. People born the same day at different hours share signs and can share no houses.
correction.zh: 星座只要日期；宮位要出生的時刻和地點。同一天不同時間出生的人，星座幾乎一樣，宮位可以完全不同。

claim.en: “Different sites show different houses, so someone is wrong.”
claim.zh: 「不同網站宮位不一樣，一定有人算錯。」

correction.en: Usually the method differs. This app uses Placidus by default and says so when it switches to whole sign at extreme latitudes.
correction.zh: 多半是分宮方法不同。本 App 預設 Placidus，高緯度算不出來時改用整宮制，並寫明。

claim.en: “No time? Just use noon.”
claim.zh: 「不知道時間，用中午算一下就好。」

correction.en: The Ascendant changes sign about every two hours, so noon makes up a starting point. This app keeps the layer blank until there is a real birth time.
correction.zh: 上升平均兩小時就換一個星座，用中午等於自己編一個起點。本 App 會讓這一層留白，等有真正的出生時間再算。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: if houses are parts of life, which one do you most want to look at first?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：如果宮位是生活場景，你最想先看哪一個？

objective.en: By the end you will know how houses differ from signs, why houses need a birth time, and why different methods give different houses.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道宮位跟星座差在哪、為什麼宮位一定要出生時間，以及為什麼不同算法會算出不同的宮位。

personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：先確認你的盤上有沒有宮位這一層。

personalSteps.en: If it does, note which method it used and whether it says it switched.
personalSteps.zh: 有的話，看一下用的是哪一種分宮，有沒有寫著換過方法。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: which house is your Sun in, and is that part of life familiar?

reason.en: Yes — Book III ch. 2 is about exactly that starting point.

detail.zh: 〈Of the Twelve Houses〉逐宮列出各宮主管的事項，第一宮管生命、身材與樣貌。原文沒有規定分宮算法，也沒有把宮位稱為「生活場景」。
