summary.en: Signs divide the sky; houses divide what you see from where you were born.
summary.zh: 星座是天空的分段，宮位是你從出生地看出去的分段。

title.zh: 宮位是什麼

kicker.en: House one is about you; house two is about what you own.
kicker.zh: 第一宮講你本人，第二宮講你擁有的東西。

text.en: House one looks at how you show up and the first impression you give: the air people sense when they first meet you, what you do first when you walk into an unfamiliar room. A planet in house one is often read as the side of you people see the moment you arrive.
text.zh: 第一宮看你出場的樣子、你給人的第一印象：別人第一次見到你時感覺到的氣質，你走進一個陌生場合時先做什麼。落在第一宮的星，常被讀成你一出場就讓人看見的那一面。

text.en: House two can be read in two layers. The concrete layer is money, belongings, what you lend and get back; the inner layer is self-worth: what you think you are worth and what keeps you steady. The two often run together — some people feel not good enough the moment money runs short.
text.zh: 第二宮可以分兩層看。具體的一層是錢、東西、借出去和收回來的帳；往內的一層是自我價值：你覺得自己值多少、靠什麼站得穩。兩層常常連在一起，例如有人一缺錢就覺得自己不夠好。

text.en: Ask yourself: does the first impression people have of you match the you inside? What do you spend on most gladly? Which thing, if taken away, would unsettle you most?
text.zh: 拿來問自己：別人對你的第一印象，和你心裡的自己一樣嗎？你花錢最捨得花在哪裡？哪一樣東西被拿走，會讓你最不安？

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly's “Of the Twelve Houses” gives house one the life, stature, colour, complexion, form and shape of the person; house two the estate or fortune, wealth or poverty, all movable goods, money lent, and profit or loss.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 的〈Of the Twelve Houses〉寫，第一宮管「生命、身材、顏色、面貌與樣貌」；第二宮管財產和運氣、有錢或貧窮、所有可移動的財物、借出去的錢、賺或賠。

kicker.en: House three is the people around you; house four is your roots.
kicker.zh: 第三宮講你身邊的往來，第四宮講你的根。

text.en: House three looks at the circle you talk with every day: brothers and sisters, neighbours, classmates, the people you message most, and the short trips of school, work and errands. A planet here is often read as how you chat and how you pick up news.
text.zh: 第三宮看你每天說話往來的圈子：兄弟姊妹、鄰居、同學、常傳訊息的人，還有你上學上班、跑腿辦事這種短程的移動。落在這裡的星，常被讀成你平常怎麼聊天、怎麼打聽消息。

text.en: House four looks at your roots: where you grew up, the habits of your home, the people and things that make you feel you are back home. It is also often used for how something finally turns out — when a relationship or a job comes to its end, where you return and how you close it.
text.zh: 第四宮看你的根：你長大的地方、家裡的習慣、讓你覺得「回到家」的人和事。它也常用來看一件事最後怎麼收場——一段關係、一份工作走到尾聲時，你回到哪裡、靠什麼收尾。

text.en: Ask yourself: who are the five people you contact most? What sentence did you hear most at home as a child? When you are tired, where do you most want to go back to?
text.zh: 拿來問自己：你最常聯絡的五個人是誰？小時候家裡最常聽到哪一句話？累的時候，你最想回到哪裡？

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly gives house three brothers, sisters, cousins or kin, neighbours, short or inland journeys, frequent moves, letters, rumours and messengers; house four fathers, lands and houses, inheritances, hidden treasure, and the end of a matter.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 寫第三宮管兄弟姊妹、表親或親戚、鄰居、短程或國內的旅行、常常搬動、書信、消息和傳話的人；第四宮管父親、土地和房子、繼承、藏起來的財物，以及一件事的結尾。

kicker.en: Start with a house that has a body in it, then see what it covers.
kicker.zh: 先找有星體落進去的那一宮，再看它管什麼。

text.en: The easiest way in: see whether your Sun or Moon is in one of these four houses, and if so, read what that house covers. An empty house simply has no body in it; what the house covers can still be read.
text.zh: 最簡單的入口：看你的太陽、月亮有沒有落在這四宮裡，有的話，再回去看那一宮管什麼。空的宮只是說那裡沒有星體，那一宮管的事一樣可以拿來讀。

text.en: Houses are worked out from the birth time. If you have one, the “your turn” part lists the sign and the bodies in each of these four houses; if not, that part tells you they appear once a birth time is added. Until then, hold what each house covers up against these four parts of your own life.
text.zh: 宮位要靠出生時間才算得出來。有時間的人，「換你自己」那一段會列出你這四宮的星座和落進去的星體；還沒有時間的人，那一段會提醒你補上出生時間後才看得到。在那之前，可以先拿上面各宮管什麼，對照自己生活裡的這四塊。

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly lists what each house covers, one by one; real judgment also reads the bodies in the house and the house's ruler — a whole set of rules read together.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 是一宮一宮列出各管什麼；真的要判斷時，還要看落在宮裡的星體和這一宮的主星，放在一起看的一整套規則。

alt.en: Table: house one is life, stature and form; house two estate, movable goods, money lent, profit and loss; house three brethren and kindred, neighbours, short journeys, letters and rumours; house four fathers, lands and houses, inheritance and the end of a matter. All from Lilly's own text.
alt.zh: 對照表：第一宮是生命、身材與樣貌；第二宮是財產、可移動的財物、借出的錢與損益；第三宮是兄弟姊妹、親族、鄰居、短程往來、書信與消息；第四宮是父親、土地房產、繼承與一件事的結尾。皆為 Lilly 原文項目。

caption.en: Houses one to four and the parts of life each one covers.
caption.zh: 第一到第四宮，各自管生活裡的哪些事。

caveat.en: Fixed placements made up for explanation; your own houses are worked out once there is a birth time.
caveat.zh: 這是為了說明而固定的示範位置；你自己的宮位要有出生時間才算得出來。

lines.en: Sun in house one: the energy goes into showing up in person.
lines.zh: 太陽在第一宮：力氣用在「自己出面」這件事上。

lines.en: Moon in house four: what settles them has to do with home and roots.
lines.zh: 月亮在第四宮：讓人安心的，跟家、跟根有關。

lines.en: Nothing in houses two or three: those houses simply hold no bodies, and money and the people around can still be read.
lines.zh: 第二、三宮沒有星體：那裡只是沒有星體，錢和身邊的往來一樣可以讀。

limitations.en: Without a birth time there are no houses; these four appear on your chart once you enter a real birth time.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間就沒有宮位；填入真正的出生時間後，這四宮才會出現在你的盤上。

limitations.en: Houses describe areas of life — a language for knowing yourself, not a forecast. An empty house only means no body sits there; that part of life is still in yours.
limitations.zh: 宮位描述的是生活的範圍，是認識自己的語言，不是預測；空宮只代表那裡沒有星體，那一宮的事照樣在你的生活裡。

claim.en: “An empty house means that part of life is missing.”
claim.zh: 「空宮代表那件事我一輩子都沒有。」

correction.en: An empty house only means no body sits there. Ten bodies across twelve houses always leaves some empty.
correction.zh: 空宮只代表沒有星體落在那裡。十個星體分到十二宮，本來就一定有空的。

claim.en: “House four is about your father.”
claim.zh: 「第四宮就是看父親。」

correction.en: House four looks at your roots: where you grew up, what home was like, the people who steady you. When reading your own chart, include everyone who raised you and gave you a sense of home.
correction.zh: 第四宮看的是你的根：你長大的地方、家的樣子、讓你安定的人。讀自己的盤時，把帶你長大、給你家的感覺的人都放進來一起看。

claim.en: “House two tells me whether I'll be rich.”
claim.zh: 「第二宮就是看我會不會有錢。」

correction.en: House two looks at how you relate to money and belongings: how you earn, spend, lend and save, and what makes you feel secure. It describes your habits with resources.
correction.zh: 第二宮看的是你和錢、東西的關係：怎麼賺、怎麼花、怎麼借、怎麼存，以及哪些東西讓你覺得踏實。它描述你處理資源的習慣。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: of these four, which one are you really dealing with right now?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：一到四宮這四件事裡，哪一件是你最近真的在處理的？

objective.en: By the end you will know which area of life houses one to four each look at, how to find them on your own chart, and what questions to ask yourself.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道第一到第四宮各看生活的哪一塊，以及怎麼在自己的盤上找到它們、拿來問自己問題。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: if your chart has houses, start with these four.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：如果你的盤有宮位，從這四宮開始看。

personalSteps.en: Check whether your Sun or Moon is in houses one to four.
personalSteps.zh: 看你的太陽、月亮有沒有落在第一到第四宮。

personalSteps.en: If so, match it to the area that house looks at: yourself, what you own, the people around you, or your roots.
personalSteps.zh: 有的話，對照那一宮看的是生活哪一塊：你自己、擁有的、身邊往來，還是根。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: has what that house covers come up in your life lately?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：那一宮講的事，最近有沒有出現在你的生活裡？

reason.en: Yes — that is the list in “Of the Twelve Houses.”
reason.zh: 對，〈Of the Twelve Houses〉就是這樣列的。

text.en: Brothers and sisters, neighbours, short journeys, letters and rumours
text.zh: 兄弟姊妹、鄰居、短程往來、書信和消息

reason.en: Those belong to house four.
reason.zh: 那是第四宮。

text.en: Lands and inheritance
text.zh: 土地和繼承

reason.en: Those belong to house two.
reason.zh: 那是第二宮。

text.en: Movable goods and money lent
text.zh: 可移動的財物和借出去的錢

prompt.en: What does Lilly give house three?
prompt.zh: Lilly 寫第三宮管什麼？

reason.en: Ten bodies across twelve houses must leave some empty.
reason.zh: 十個星體分到十二宮，一定會有空的。

text.en: Only that no body sits there
text.zh: 只代表沒有星體落在那裡

reason.en: An empty house means only that no body sits there.
reason.zh: 空宮的意思只是那裡沒有星體。

text.en: That part of life will not happen to you
text.zh: 那件事不會發生在你身上

reason.en: An empty house is a normal result; some of the twelve are always empty.
reason.zh: 空宮是正常的結果，十二宮本來就會有幾宮空著。

text.zh: 那一宮算錯了

prompt.en: What does a house with no bodies mean?
prompt.zh: 宮裡沒有星體，代表什麼？

detail.en: “Of the Twelve Houses” gives: the first house the life, stature, colour, complexion, form and shape; the second the estate or fortune, wealth or poverty, movable goods, money lent, profit or loss; the third brethren, sisters, cousins or kindred, neighbours, short or inland journeys, frequent moves, letters, rumours and messengers; the fourth fathers, lands and houses, inheritances, hidden treasure and the end of a matter. Reading them as how you enter, self-worth, or home and settling is later usage, and reading the fourth as roots instead of fathers is this lesson's change — all labelled as such.
detail.zh: 〈Of the Twelve Houses〉原文列出：第一宮為生命、身材、顏色、面貌與樣貌；第二宮為財產與運氣、財富或貧窮、可移動的財物、借出的錢、利得或損失；第三宮為兄弟姊妹、親族、鄰居、短程或境內旅行、經常搬動、書信、消息與傳話者；第四宮為父親、土地與房產、繼承、藏起的財物與一件事的結尾。「入場方式」「自我價值」「家與安身」等讀法是後世說法；第四宮改讀為根與成長地是本課的改寫，皆已分開標示。

summary.en: Houses one to four: yourself, what you own, the people around you, your roots.
summary.zh: 一到四宮：你自己、你擁有的、你身邊的往來、你的根。

title.zh: 一到四宮：自己與根

kicker.en: House five is what you put out; house six is what you look after daily.
kicker.zh: 第五宮講你拿出去的，第六宮講你每天顧著的。

text.en: Astrology today often reads house five as what you make and are willing to show, and house six as what you keep up every day — work habits and the state of your body. House five is also often read as play and delight — anything that makes you feel “I made this, and I love it”; house six is the small unseen things that keep the days holding up.
text.zh: 現在的占星常把第五宮讀成「你願意做出來、也願意拿給人看的東西」，第六宮讀成「你每天在維持的事——工作習慣和身體狀況」。第五宮也常被讀成玩樂和心動：一切讓你覺得「這是我做的，好開心」的事；第六宮則是那些沒人看見、卻讓日子撐得住的小事。

text.en: Ask yourself: what have you made lately that you really wanted to show someone? On an ordinary workday, how do you arrange getting up, eating and working? Which small habit, once broken, throws the whole day off? How your body is doing is for a doctor and your own sense to judge.
text.zh: 拿來問自己：你最近做了什麼，是很想拿給別人看的？一個普通的工作日，你怎麼安排起床、吃飯、做事？哪個小習慣一斷掉，整天就亂掉？身體的狀況，交給醫生和你自己的感覺來判斷。

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly's “Of the Twelve Houses” gives house five children, ambassadors, the state of a woman with child, banquets, taverns and plays, and the father's wealth; house six servants, smaller cattle and the profit or loss from them, sickness with its quality and cause, whether it can be cured, how long it lasts, and day labourers.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 的〈Of the Twelve Houses〉寫，第五宮管子女、使節、懷孕婦人的狀況、宴席、酒館、戲劇，以及父親的財富；第六宮管僕役、較小的家畜和從牠們來的賺賠、疾病的性質和原因、能不能治好、病多久，還有按日計酬的工人。

kicker.en: House seven is the person opposite you; house eight is what you share.
kicker.zh: 第七宮講站在你對面的人，第八宮講你和別人共有的東西。

text.en: Astrology today often reads house seven as how you deal with an equal — a partner, someone you work with, and an opponent too — and house eight as what you hold jointly with others and what has to end completely before you can move on. House seven sits directly opposite house one on the chart: house one is you, house seven the person standing across from you; house eight is where two people come to share money, responsibility and trust.
text.zh: 現在的占星常把第七宮讀成「你怎麼跟一個對等的人相處」——伴侶、合作的人，也包括對手；第八宮讀成「你和別人共有的東西，以及要徹底結束才能往下走的事」。第七宮在盤上正對著第一宮：第一宮是你，第七宮就是站在你對面的那個人；第八宮則是兩個人之間開始有了共同的錢、責任和信任。

text.en: Ask yourself: with a partner or someone you work with, do you tend to give way or hold firm? Who do you share an account, a home, a duty or a secret with? When a relationship comes to its end, do you cut it off cleanly or let go slowly?
text.zh: 拿來問自己：和伴侶或合作的人相處時，你習慣讓步還是堅持？你和誰有共同的帳戶、房子、責任或秘密？一段關係走到尾聲時，你通常一刀兩斷，還是慢慢放手？

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly gives house seven marriage and the description of the person asked about, all love questions, public enemies, the defendant in a lawsuit, the other side in a war, and quarrels and duels; house eight the estate of the dead, death and its nature, wills and legacies, and the wife's dowry.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 寫第七宮管婚姻，並描述被問到的那個人，也管所有感情問題、公開的敵人、官司裡的被告、戰爭的另一方、爭吵和決鬥；第八宮管死者的財產、死亡和它的性質、遺囑和遺產，以及妻子的嫁妝。

kicker.en: Treat these four as a line running from you out to other people.
kicker.zh: 把這四宮當成一條從你自己走向別人的線。

text.en: An easy order to remember: house five is what you put out, house six what you keep up daily, house seven is an equal standing opposite you, and house eight is what the two of you come to share. Follow the line with questions: is anyone receiving what I put out? Do my daily habits leave room for the people close to me?
text.zh: 一個好記的順序：五宮是你主動拿出去的，六宮是你每天維持的，七宮是有一個對等的人站在你對面，八宮是你們之間開始有了共同的東西。讀的時候順著這條線問：我拿出去的東西，有人接住嗎？每天的習慣，有沒有替我和別人的關係留出空間？

text.en: In many charts these four houses are empty. An empty house simply has no body in it; partners, work and shared property can still be read from these houses. Houses are worked out from the birth time; until you have one, read this lesson as knowledge and learn what the four houses mean.
text.zh: 很多人的盤，這四宮是空的。空宮只是那裡沒有星體，伴侶、工作、共同財產這些事，一樣可以拿這幾宮來讀。宮位要靠出生時間才算得出來；還沒有時間時，可以先把這一堂當知識讀，把四宮的意思記起來。

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly lists each house's matters in turn; real judgment reads the bodies in a house and the house's ruler.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 是一宮一宮列出各宮的事項；真的要判斷時，要看宮裡的星體和這一宮的主星。

alt.en: Diagram: a double ring. The outer ring is divided into twelve parts for the signs, the inner ring stands for the houses, and a horizontal line on the left is labelled ASC, where the houses are counted from. A concept figure with no real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個雙層圓環，外圈分成十二等分代表十二星座，內圈代表十二宮，左側水平線標著 ASC，是宮位的起算點。概念圖，沒有真實度數。

caption.en: Houses run in order from the starting point at birth; this lesson looks at the fifth through the eighth.
caption.zh: 宮位是從出生時刻的起算點依序排下來的；本堂看的是其中第五到第八宮。

caveat.en: Fixed placements made up for explanation; your own houses are worked out once there is a birth time.
caveat.zh: 這是為了說明而固定的示範位置；你自己的宮位要有出生時間才算得出來。

lines.en: Venus in house five: what they enjoy leans towards making things and sharing them.
lines.zh: 金星在第五宮：喜歡的方式偏向做東西、拿出來分享。

lines.en: Mars in house six: the effort goes into daily upkeep, keeping each day in order.
lines.zh: 火星在第六宮：力氣花在日常維持，把每天的事顧好。

lines.en: Houses seven and eight empty: those houses simply hold no bodies, and partners and shared things can still be read.
lines.zh: 七、八宮都空：那裡只是沒有星體，伴侶和共有的事一樣可以讀。

limitations.en: House six looks at daily habits, not at your health; if you are unwell, see a doctor.
limitations.zh: 第六宮看的是作息習慣，不是健康診斷；身體不舒服請找醫生。

limitations.en: House eight describes sharing and closure and is never used to guess at lifespan or danger; astrology is a language for describing yourself, not a forecast.
limitations.zh: 第八宮描述的是共有與收尾，不用來推測壽命或危險；占星是描述自己的語言，不是預測。

limitations.en: With no birth time there are no houses.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間就沒有宮位。

claim.en: “House eight shows how I'll die.”
claim.zh: 「第八宮代表我會怎麼死。」

correction.en: House eight looks at what you share and carry together with others, and how a chapter closes. It describes how you meet these things, such as how you split money and responsibility with someone.
correction.zh: 第八宮看的是你和別人共有、一起承擔的東西，以及一段事情怎麼收尾。它描述你怎麼面對這些事，例如你怎麼和人分錢、分責任。

claim.en: “My house seven is empty, so no partner for me.”
claim.zh: 「第七宮空的，所以我不會有伴侶。」

correction.en: An empty house only means no body sits there; ten bodies across twelve houses always leaves some empty.
correction.zh: 空宮只代表沒有星體落在那裡；十個星體分到十二宮，本來就一定有空的。

claim.en: “House six can tell me what illness I have.”
claim.zh: 「第六宮可以看出我生什麼病。」

correction.en: House six is good for looking at how you keep up your daily routine — whether you eat and sleep at set times or forget everything once you are busy. If you are unwell, see a doctor.
correction.zh: 第六宮適合拿來看你怎麼照顧每天的作息，例如你是固定時間吃飯睡覺的人，還是一忙起來就全忘了。身體不舒服請去看醫生。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: what pattern shows up most when you deal with the person opposite you?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你跟「對面那個人」相處時，最常出現的模式是什麼？

objective.en: By the end you will know which area of life houses five to eight each look at, and how to use them to look at what you make, your daily habits, your partners and what you share.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道第五到第八宮各看生活的哪一塊，以及怎麼用它們看自己做的事、每天的習慣、身邊的伴侶和共有的東西。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: see whether any body sits in these four houses.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：看看這四宮裡有沒有星體。

personalSteps.en: Find which bodies sit in houses five to eight — maybe none.
personalSteps.zh: 找出第五到第八宮裡有哪些星體（也可能一顆都沒有）。

personalSteps.en: If any do, match it to the area that house looks at: what you put out, what you keep up, the person opposite, or what you share.
personalSteps.zh: 有的話，對照那一宮看的是哪一塊：拿出去的、每天顧著的、對面的人，還是共有的。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: which of these four takes up most of your time lately?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：這四件事裡，哪一件最近最佔你的時間？

reason.en: Yes — the old text puts partner and opponent in one house; both are the person opposite.
reason.zh: 對，古書把伴侶和對手放在同一宮，都是「對面的人」。

text.en: Marriage, love questions, public enemies and the other side in a lawsuit
text.zh: 婚姻、感情問題、公開的敵人和官司的另一方

reason.en: Those belong to house five.
reason.zh: 那是第五宮。

text.en: Children and banquets
text.zh: 子女和宴席

reason.en: Those belong to house eight.
reason.zh: 那是第八宮。

text.en: Wills and legacies
text.zh: 遺囑和遺產

prompt.en: What does Lilly give house seven?
prompt.zh: Lilly 寫第七宮管什麼？

reason.en: Yes — house six looks at the habits you keep up daily: how work, meals and sleep are arranged.
reason.zh: 對，第六宮看的是每天維持的習慣：工作、吃飯、睡覺怎麼排。

text.en: How you arrange your days and look after yourself
text.zh: 你每天怎麼安排作息、照顧自己

reason.en: Your health is for a doctor to judge; house six looks at your daily habits.
reason.zh: 身體的狀況交給醫生判斷；第六宮看的是你的日常習慣。

text.en: What illness you have
text.zh: 你生了什麼病

reason.en: That is house seven, the person opposite you.
reason.zh: 那是第七宮，站在你對面的人。

text.en: How you get along with a partner
text.zh: 你和伴侶怎麼相處

prompt.en: What is house six best used to look at?
prompt.zh: 第六宮最適合拿來看什麼？

detail.en: “Of the Twelve Houses” gives: the fifth house children, ambassadors, the state of a woman with child, banquets, taverns, plays and the father's wealth; the sixth servants, lesser cattle and the profit or loss from them, sickness with its quality and cause, whether curable, whether short or long, and day labourers; the seventh marriage, the description of the person asked about, love questions, public enemies, the defendant, the opposing party in war, quarrels and duels; the eighth the estate of the deceased, death with its quality and nature, wills and legacies, and the wife's dowry. Reading them as making and showing, daily upkeep, equal relationships, and sharing and ending are later summaries; the servants, slaves, cattle, medical diagnosis and dowry framing are not carried over, as the lesson states.
detail.zh: 〈Of the Twelve Houses〉原文列出：第五宮為子女、使節、懷孕婦人的狀況、宴席、酒館、戲劇與父親的財富；第六宮為僕役、較小家畜及其損益、疾病的性質與成因、能否治癒、病程長短與日工；第七宮為婚姻、對被問者的描述、感情問題、公開的敵人、訴訟被告、戰爭中的對方、爭執與決鬥；第八宮為亡者財產、死亡及其性質、遺囑與遺產、妻子的嫁妝。「創造並展示」「日常維持」「對等關係」「共有與結束」等讀法為後世概括；僕役、奴隸、家畜、疾病診斷與嫁妝框架本課不沿用，皆已在課文說明。

rights.en: The 1647 text is in the public domain; the transcribing site's layout and notes are not cited.
rights.zh: 一六四七年原文屬公共領域；轉錄網站的編排與註解不在引用範圍。

title.zh: William Lilly, Christian Astrology（1647）

detail.en: Book III ch. 2 takes the rising degree at birth as the point the houses run from; with no birth time there are no houses.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 2 章以出生時刻的上升度數為起算點，宮位由此依序排下；沒有出生時間就沒有宮位。

label.zh: 第三卷第 2 章（上升度數）

rights.en: The Robbins translation is in the public domain, as the University of Chicago LacusCurtius copyright page records. The transcriber's own notes and layout are not cited.
rights.zh: Robbins 英譯本已進入公共領域，芝加哥大學 LacusCurtius 版權說明頁如此記載。轉錄者自己的註解與編排不在引用範圍。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Houses five to eight: what you put out, what you look after daily, the person opposite you, and what you share with others.
summary.zh: 五到八宮：你拿出去的、你每天顧著的、站在你對面的人、你和別人共有的。

title.zh: 五到八宮：關係與共享

kicker.en: House nine is what you reach out for; house ten is how the world sees you.
kicker.zh: 第九宮講你往外追求什麼，第十宮講你在外面被看見的樣子。

text.en: Astrology today often reads house nine as how far you will go to understand something — study, going abroad, what you believe — and house ten as how you are known in public and the direction of your work. House nine is like the edge of your map: the books you have read, the places you have been and the ideas you hold all push that map outward.
text.zh: 現在的占星常把第九宮讀成「為了弄懂一件事，你願意走多遠」——念書、出國、相信什麼；第十宮讀成「你在公開場合被認出來的樣子，和你的工作方向」。第九宮就像你的地圖邊界：你讀過的書、去過的地方、信的道理，都在把這張地圖往外推。

text.en: House ten sits at the top of the chart, its most visible spot. It looks at public standing and the direction of your work: how people out there introduce you, where your work is heading, and what you want to be remembered for.
text.zh: 第十宮在盤的最上方，是整張盤最「被看見」的位置。它看的是公開身分和工作方向：別人在外面怎麼介紹你、你的工作往哪裡走、你想被記得是什麼樣的人。

text.en: Ask yourself: is there something lately you badly want to read about, ask about or go and see? If a colleague or client summed you up in one line, what would they say — and is that what you want?
text.zh: 拿來問自己：最近有沒有一件事，讓你很想去讀、去問、去看看？如果同事或客戶用一句話介紹你，他們會怎麼說？那是你想要的說法嗎？

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly's “Of the Twelve Houses” gives house nine long voyages over the sea, religious people and clergy of every kind, dreams and visions, foreign countries, books and learning; house ten kings, princes, judges and everyone in authority, mothers, honour, promotion, office, and the profession or trade a person follows.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 的〈Of the Twelve Houses〉寫，第九宮管出海的長途旅行、宗教人士和各種神職、夢和異象、外國、書本和學問；第十宮管國王、王公、法官和各種有權位的人、母親、榮譽、升遷、官職，以及一個人做的專業或行業。

kicker.en: House eleven is the people with you; house twelve is how you trip yourself up.
kicker.zh: 第十一宮講你的同伴，第十二宮講你怎麼絆住自己。

text.en: Astrology today often reads house eleven as the people with you and the groups you want to join, and house twelve as the side of yourself you would rather not look at and what you can only deal with alone. The most useful reading of house twelve is “self-undoing”: what blocks you is usually not an outside enemy but your own habits. House eleven looks at the people around you and the hopes you hold for the future.
text.zh: 現在的占星常把第十一宮讀成「你的同伴、你想加入的群體」，第十二宮讀成「你自己也不太想看的那一面，以及要一個人靜下來才處理得了的事」。第十二宮最好用的讀法是「自己害自己」（self-undoing）：擋住你的往往不是外面的敵人，而是你自己的習慣。第十一宮則看你身邊的同伴，以及你對未來抱著什麼希望。

text.en: Ask yourself: where do you tend to hold yourself back — putting things off, saying yes and not following through, refusing to stop when you are worn out? What only becomes clear when you are quiet and alone? Is there a group around you where you feel you belong?
text.zh: 拿來問自己：你在哪些地方習慣拖住自己——拖延、說好卻做不到、明明累了還不肯停？哪些事要一個人靜下來才看得清楚？你身邊有沒有一群人，讓你覺得「我屬於這裡」？

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly gives house eleven, by nature, friends and friendship, hope, trust, the praise or blame a person gets, and whether friends are faithful; house twelve private enemies, witches, sorrow, trouble, imprisonment, every kind of affliction, self-undoing, and those who secretly scheme against their neighbours.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 寫第十一宮天生代表朋友和友誼、希望、信任、別人對你的稱讚或批評、朋友忠不忠實；第十二宮管暗中的敵人、巫者、憂傷、患難、監禁、各種苦難，以及「自己害自己」（self-undoing），還有暗中算計鄰居的人。

kicker.en: The twelve houses are twelve subjects for you to read for yourself.
kicker.zh: 十二宮是十二個題目，答案要你自己去讀。

text.en: The twelve houses are best held as twelve subjects. Where a body falls, that subject has more going on in your life; a house with no bodies still has its subject — it just stays quiet in the chart.
text.zh: 十二宮最好當成十二個題目。星體落在哪一宮，代表那個題目在你身上比較有戲；沒有星體的宮，題目一樣存在，只是在盤上不出聲。

text.en: You have now been through two layers, signs and houses. Try joining them in one sentence: “My ___ (planet) works in the ___ (sign) way, in the ___ (house) part of my life.” The next lesson starts the third: the angles between bodies, called aspects. Without a birth time you can still read the sign and aspect layers.
text.zh: 到這裡，你已經看完星座和宮位兩層。試著把兩層連起來讀成一句話：「我的＿＿（星體）用＿＿（星座）的方式，在＿＿（宮位）這塊生活裡出力。」下一堂開始看第三層：星體之間的角度，也就是相位。沒有出生時間的人，一樣可以讀星座和相位這兩層。

text.en: What the old texts say: Lilly lists what each house covers, then judges from the bodies in it and the house's ruler; the text always weighs several things together before it concludes.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：Lilly 先一宮一宮列出各管什麼，再看落進去的星體和這一宮的主星來判斷；原文總是把幾樣東西放在一起看，才下結論。

alt.en: Diagram: a double ring. The outer ring is divided into twelve parts for the signs, the inner ring stands for the houses, and a horizontal line on the left is labelled ASC, where the houses are counted from. A concept figure with no real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個雙層圓環，外圈分成十二等分代表十二星座，內圈代表十二宮，左側水平線標著 ASC，是宮位的起算點。概念圖，沒有真實度數。

caption.en: The twelve houses run once around from the starting point on the left; this lesson looks at the last four.
caption.zh: 十二宮從左邊的起算點依序排一圈；本堂看的是最後四宮。

caveat.en: Fixed placements made up for explanation; your own houses are worked out once there is a birth time.
caveat.zh: 這是為了說明而固定的示範位置；你自己的宮位要有出生時間才算得出來。

lines.en: Jupiter in house nine: willing to go a long way to understand something.
lines.zh: 木星在第九宮：為了弄懂一件事，願意跑很遠。

lines.en: Saturn in house ten: strict about their own work, building slowly.
lines.zh: 土星在第十宮：對自己的工作要求很嚴，慢慢累積。

lines.en: Houses eleven and twelve empty: friends and time alone still matter — the chart is just quiet about them.
lines.zh: 十一、十二宮空：朋友和獨處的題目一樣存在，只是盤上不出聲。

limitations.en: Astrology is a language for describing yourself, not a forecast; no house means prison, a lawsuit or any event is bound to happen.
limitations.zh: 占星是描述自己的語言，不是預測；任何宮位都不代表坐牢、官司或某件事一定會發生。

limitations.en: Without a birth time the house layer stays empty.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，宮位這一層會一直空著。

claim.en: “House twelve means bad luck and prison.”
claim.zh: 「第十二宮代表倒楣和坐牢。」

correction.en: The most useful reading of house twelve is self-undoing: where you hold yourself back and what only becomes clear alone. It describes habits, not fate.
correction.zh: 第十二宮最好用的讀法是「自己害自己」（self-undoing）：看你在哪裡拖住自己、哪些事要獨處才看得清。它描述習慣，不是命運。

claim.en: “House ten is about your mother.”
claim.zh: 「第十宮就是看母親。」

correction.en: House ten looks at public standing and the direction of your work: how people out there know you and where your work is heading. Home and the people who raised you are read in house four.
correction.zh: 第十宮看的是公開身分和工作方向：別人在外面怎麼認識你、你的工作往哪裡走。家和帶你長大的人，放到第四宮去看。

claim.en: “A house with more bodies matters more.”
claim.zh: 「星體多的宮比較重要。」

correction.en: A house is read from its bodies and its ruler together, as a whole; an empty house still has its subject — it is just quiet in the chart.
correction.zh: 讀一宮要把宮裡的星體和這一宮的主星一起看，看的是整體；空宮的題目也一樣存在，只是在盤上不出聲。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: what is your most common way of tripping yourself up?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你最常用什麼方式絆住自己？

objective.en: By the end you will know which area of life houses nine to twelve each look at, how to use house ten to look at where your work is heading, and house twelve to see where you trip yourself up.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道第九到第十二宮各看生活的哪一塊，怎麼用第十宮看你的工作方向，怎麼用第十二宮看你在哪裡絆住自己。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: finish the last four and you have been all the way round.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：把最後四宮看完，十二宮就繞完一圈了。

personalSteps.en: Find which bodies sit in houses nine to twelve — maybe none.
personalSteps.zh: 找出第九到第十二宮裡有哪些星體（也可能一顆都沒有）。

personalSteps.en: Match it to the area that house looks at: what you reach for, how you are seen, the people with you, or where you trip yourself up.
personalSteps.zh: 對照那一宮看的是哪一塊：往外追求的、被看見的樣子、同伴，還是絆住自己的地方。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: of the twelve subjects, which do you most want to understand now?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：十二個題目裡，你現在最想弄懂哪一個？

reason.en: Yes — self-undoing is the most useful of these: it shows how you trip yourself up.
reason.zh: 對，self-undoing 這個詞最好用：看你怎麼絆住自己。

text.en: Private enemies, sorrow and trouble, and self-undoing
text.zh: 暗中的敵人、憂傷患難，以及「自己害自己」

reason.en: Those belong to house eleven.
reason.zh: 那是第十一宮。

text.en: Friends and friendship
text.zh: 朋友和友誼

reason.en: Those belong to house nine.
reason.zh: 那是第九宮。

text.en: Long voyages and books
text.zh: 長途旅行和書本

prompt.en: What does Lilly give house twelve?
prompt.zh: Lilly 寫第十二宮管什麼？

reason.en: Yes — where a body falls, that subject has more going on; the answer is yours to read.
reason.zh: 對，星體落在哪一宮，那個題目就比較有戲；答案要你自己去讀。

text.en: Twelve subjects, not twelve answers
text.zh: 十二個題目，不是十二個答案

reason.en: A house is a subject for watching yourself.
reason.zh: 宮位是讓你拿來觀察自己的題目。

text.en: Twelve fixed life outcomes
text.zh: 十二個註定的人生結果

reason.en: An empty house still has its subject; the chart is just quiet about it.
reason.zh: 空宮的題目一樣存在，只是盤上不出聲。

text.en: Only houses with bodies in them count
text.zh: 只有有星體的宮才算數

prompt.en: How are the twelve houses best understood?
prompt.zh: 十二宮最好怎麼理解？

detail.en: “Of the Twelve Houses” gives: the ninth house long voyages beyond seas, religious men and clergy, dreams and visions, foreign countries, books and learning; the tenth kings and princes, judges and officers in authority, mothers, honour, preferment, office and the profession followed; the eleventh friends and friendship, hope, trust, praise or dispraise and the faithfulness of friends; the twelfth private enemies, witches, sorrow, tribulation, imprisonment, affliction and self-undoing. Reading them as how far you go to understand, public standing and work, company and groups, and what is dealt with alone are later summaries; the assignment of mothers, and the witches and imprisonment material, are not carried over, as the lesson states.
detail.zh: 〈Of the Twelve Houses〉原文列出：第九宮為海外長途旅行、宗教人士與神職、夢與異象、外國、書籍與學問；第十宮為君王公侯、法官與有權位者、母親、榮譽、晉升、職位與所從事的專業；第十一宮為朋友與友誼、希望、信任、稱讚或非議、朋友是否忠實；第十二宮為暗中的敵人、巫者、憂傷、患難、監禁、各種苦難與 self-undoing。「為理解走多遠」「公開身分與職業」「同伴與群體」「獨處才處理得了的事」為後世概括；母親的宮位指定、巫者與監禁等項目本課不沿用，已在課文說明。

rights.en: The 1647 text is in the public domain; the transcribing site's layout and notes are not cited.
rights.zh: 一六四七年原文屬公共領域；轉錄網站的編排與註解不在引用範圍。

title.zh: William Lilly, Christian Astrology（1647）

summary.en: Houses nine to twelve: what you reach for, how you are seen, the people with you, and where you trip yourself up.
summary.zh: 九到十二宮：你往外追求的、你被看見的樣子、你的同伴、你自己絆住自己的地方。

title.zh: 九到十二宮：世界與內在

kicker.en: The four main aspects: 180, 120, 90 and 60 degrees.

text.en: An aspect is simply how many degrees apart two positions are — something you can read by measuring an angle. The usual reading treats an aspect as a conversation between two planets: 180 degrees apart is face to face, 90 is catching on each other, 120 and 60 are going along with each other.
text.zh: 相位就是兩個位置之間差了幾度，用量角度的方式就能看懂。常見的說法是把相位當成兩顆星之間的對話：差 180 度是面對面，差 90 度是卡著彼此，差 120 度和 60 度是順著彼此。

text.en: A quick way to estimate: count how many signs lie between the two. Six apart is roughly an opposition, four a trine, three a square, two a sextile. Sun in Aries and Moon in Leo are four signs apart, so start by guessing a trine.
text.zh: 有個快速估算的方法：先數兩顆星隔了幾個星座。隔六個大約是對分相，隔四個是三分相，隔三個是四分相，隔兩個是六分相。例如太陽在牡羊、月亮在獅子，隔四個星座，就先猜是三分相。

text.en: Then check the actual degrees. This app measures the real degrees, and the aspects listed on the chart page are already worked out, so you can check your guess against them.
text.zh: 猜完再看實際度數確認。本 App 照實際度數計算，命盤頁列出的相位都已經算好，可以直接拿來對照你的估算。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 13 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, “Of the Aspects of the Signs,” is precise — opposition spans two right angles, six signs, 180 degrees; trine one and a third right angles, four signs, 120 degrees; square one right angle, three signs, 90 degrees; sextile two-thirds of a right angle, two signs, 60 degrees.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 13 章〈星座的相位〉寫得很具體——對分相隔兩個直角、六個星座、180 度；三分相隔一又三分之一個直角、四個星座、120 度；四分相隔一個直角、三個星座、90 度；六分相隔三分之二個直角、兩個星座、60 度。

kicker.en: The four aspects cut the circle into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.
kicker.zh: 四個相位剛好把一圈切成二、三、四、六等份。

text.en: A circle is 360 degrees. 180 is a half, 120 a third, 90 a quarter and 60 a sixth. Held this way, the four aspects are easy to remember, and you can tell which one a figure is at a glance.
text.zh: 一圈是 360 度。180 度是一半，120 度是三分之一，90 度是四分之一，60 度是六分之一。這樣記，四個相位一下就背起來，看到度數也能馬上認出是哪一個。

text.en: This app computes exactly these four, plus the conjunction: two bodies bunched together, 0 degrees apart. The chart page lists all five together.
text.zh: 本 App 算的就是這四個，再加上合相：兩顆星擠在一起，差 0 度。命盤頁會把五種一起列出來。

text.en: Astrology today often reads them like this: a conjunction blends two forces; an opposition is a tug of war that asks for balance; a square catches and pushes you to act; a trine runs easily, without effort; a sextile is an opening you have to reach for.
text.zh: 現在的占星常這樣讀：合相是兩股力氣混在一起；對分相是拉鋸，要找平衡；四分相是卡住，逼你動起來；三分相是順手，用起來不費力；六分相是機會，要伸手才拿得到。

text.en: What the old texts say: the same chapter gives the reason. Opposition is the obvious one, because the two places sit on one straight line. The rest come from applying the most important musical ratios to the right angle: a half and a third applied to opposition give the square, the sextile and the trine. The text adds that trine and sextile are called harmonious because they join signs of the same kind, all masculine or all feminine, while square and opposition are not.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：同一章接著講理由。對分相最明顯，因為兩個位置在同一條直線上。其他的，是把音樂裡最重要的比例套到直角上：把二分之一和三分之一用在對分相上，就得出四分相、六分相和三分相。原文還說，三分相和六分相叫做和諧，因為它們連起同一類的星座（全是陽性或全是陰性）；四分相和對分相則不和諧。

kicker.en: It need not be exactly 120; a table decides how far off still counts.
kicker.zh: 不是剛好 120 度才算，差一點也算，差多少由一張表決定。

text.en: Two bodies are rarely an exact round angle apart, so you need a range for how far off still counts, called the orb. This app uses a common modern table: in a birth chart, 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, 4 for sextile; transits are read more tightly, 1 degree in general and 2 for the Sun and Moon. Every report records which version of the table it used.
text.zh: 兩顆星體很少剛好差整數的角度，所以需要一個「差多少還算」的範圍，叫容許度。本 App 用的是現在常用的簡表：本命盤的合相和對分相容許 8 度、四分相和三分相 6 度、六分相 4 度；看行運時收得更緊，一般 1 度，太陽和月亮放寬到 2 度。每一份報告都會記下用的是哪一版表。

text.en: So if another source shows you different aspects, usually the orbs are set differently. When reading your own chart, start with the aspects closest to exact; they are usually the ones most worth reading first.
text.zh: 所以如果你在別的地方看到的相位跟這裡不同，多半是容許度設得不一樣。讀自己的盤時，先看差得最少、最接近整數角度的那幾個相位，它們通常最值得先讀。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 13 gives exact angles: opposition 180, trine 120, square 90, sextile 60 degrees.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 13 章給的是準確的角度：對分相 180 度、三分相 120 度、四分相 90 度、六分相 60 度。

alt.en: Diagram: a circle with four chords drawn from the top, for the 180-degree opposition, the 120-degree trine, the 90-degree square and the 60-degree sextile, beside a table saying the same in words. A concept figure, not a real chart.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個圓圈，從頂端畫出四條弦，分別對應 180 度的對分相、120 度的三分相、90 度的四分相與 60 度的六分相。旁邊附同樣內容的文字對照表。概念圖，不是真實星盤。

caption.en: The four aspect angles, after Ptolemy Book I ch. 13.
caption.zh: 四個相位的角度，依托勒密第一卷第 13 章。

caveat.en: These degrees were made up to show how orbs work.
caveat.zh: 這組度數是為了說明容許度而編的例子。

lines.en: Sun at 10 degrees Libra, Moon at 12 degrees Aries: 178 degrees apart.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤座 10 度、月亮在牡羊座 12 度：差 178 度。

lines.en: Opposition is 180; 2 degrees off is inside the 8-degree orb, so it counts.
lines.zh: 對分相是 180 度，差 2 度還在 8 度的容許範圍內，所以算對分相。

lines.en: At 175 degrees — 5 off — it still counts here; 9 off would not.
lines.zh: 如果是 175 度（差 5 度），照本 App 的表還算；差 9 度就不算了。

limitations.en: The orb figures are this app's modern conventional table: in a birth chart 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, 4 for sextile; 1 degree for transits, 2 for the Sun and Moon. Other sites may use different figures.
limitations.zh: 容許度的數字是本 App 採用的現代常用表：本命合相和對分相 8 度、四分相和三分相 6 度、六分相 4 度，行運 1 度、太陽月亮 2 度；別的網站可能用不同的數字。

limitations.en: An aspect describes how two forces get along; it is not good or bad and says nothing about luck. Astrology is a language for describing yourself, not a forecast.
limitations.zh: 相位描述兩股力氣怎麼相處，不分好壞，也不代表運氣；占星是描述自己的語言，不是預測。

claim.en: “Squares are bad aspects and trines are good ones.”
claim.zh: 「四分相是壞相位，三分相是好相位。」

correction.en: A square is a force that catches and pushes you to act; a trine is one that runs easily. Both are useful. Reading an aspect means asking how smoothly the two forces run together.
correction.zh: 四分相是卡住、逼你動起來的力氣，三分相是順手、不費力的力氣，兩種都有用處。讀相位時，看的是這兩股力氣順不順、怎麼相處。

claim.en: “If it is not exact it does not count.”
claim.zh: 「沒有剛好那個度數就不算相位。」

correction.en: In practice you need a range. In a birth chart this app allows 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine and 4 for sextile, and records the version.
correction.zh: 實際上需要容許範圍。本 App 的本命容許度是合相和對分相 8 度、四分相和三分相 6 度、六分相 4 度，並記下版本。

claim.en: “More aspects means a stronger chart.”
claim.zh: 「相位越多的盤越厲害。」

correction.en: Every chart is read the same way: see which two forces each aspect joins, and how they get along.
correction.zh: 每張盤都用同樣的方式讀：看每個相位連起哪兩股力氣，它們怎麼相處。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: the closest aspect in your chart joins two forces — how do they get along in you?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你盤上差得最少的那個相位，連起的兩股力氣在你身上怎麼相處？

objective.en: By the end you will know what an aspect is, how many degrees each of the four main aspects spans, how to find them on your own chart, and how far off still counts.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道相位是什麼、四個主要相位各差幾度、怎麼在自己的盤上找到它們，以及差幾度還算數。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: aspects need no birth time, so you can read them without one.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：相位不需要出生時間，沒有時間也看得到。

personalSteps.en: Look at the listed aspects and find the one that is closest to exact.
personalSteps.zh: 看命盤頁列出的相位，找出差得最少的那一個（最接近整數角度）。

personalSteps.en: See which two bodies it joins, and recall what earlier lessons said each one is about.
personalSteps.zh: 看它連的是哪兩顆星體，回想前面幾堂說它們各講什麼。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: do those two forces work together in you, or pull against each other?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：這兩股力氣在你身上是合作，還是互相拉扯？

reason.en: Yes — a half, a third, a quarter and a sixth of the circle.
reason.zh: 對，剛好是一圈的一半、三分之一、四分之一和六分之一。

text.en: 180, 120, 90 and 60 degrees

reason.en: The four main aspects are 180, 120, 90 and 60, cutting the circle into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.
reason.zh: 四個主要相位是 180、120、90、60 度，把一圈切成二、三、四、六等份。

text.en: 180, 150, 90 and 45 degrees

reason.en: There are four main aspects; the conjunction, 0 degrees apart, is one more on top.
reason.zh: 主要相位有四個；合相（差 0 度）是另外再加的一種。

text.en: Only conjunction and opposition
text.zh: 只有合相和對分相

prompt.en: How many degrees do the four main aspects span?
prompt.zh: 四個主要相位各差幾度？

reason.en: Yes — the two signs they join are both masculine or both feminine, the same kind.
reason.zh: 對，它們連起的兩個星座都是陽性，或都是陰性，屬於同一類。

text.en: Because they join signs of the same kind, all masculine or all feminine
text.zh: 因為它們連起同一類的星座（全陽性或全陰性）

reason.en: Harmony here comes from how the signs are sorted: they join signs of the same kind.
reason.zh: 和諧的依據是星座的分類：它們連起同一類星座。

text.en: Because they bring good luck
text.zh: 因為它們會帶來好運

reason.en: A square at 90 is smaller than a trine at 120, so that is not the reason.
reason.zh: 四分相 90 度比三分相 120 度還小，所以不是這個原因。

text.en: Because their angles are smaller
text.zh: 因為它們的角度比較小

prompt.en: Why are trine and sextile called harmonious?
prompt.zh: 三分相和六分相為什麼被叫做和諧？

detail.en: Book I ch. 13 gives the four aspects as right-angle ratios, sign intervals and degrees — opposition 180, trine 120, quartile 90, sextile 60 — explains from musical ratios why only these are taken, and says trine and sextile are called harmonious because they join signs of the same kind while quartile and opposition are disharmonious; the masculine/feminine classification is ch. 12. That chapter treats aspects between signs, while this app measures actual degrees, and modern additions such as 150 and 45 degrees have no classical source and are not used.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 13 章寫出四個相位的直角比例、相隔星座數與度數（對分相 180 度、三分相 120 度、四分相 90 度、六分相 60 度），並以音樂比例解釋為何只取這些，另說三分相與六分相因連接同類星座而稱和諧、四分相與對分相為不和諧；陰陽分類見第 12 章。原文該章談的是星座之間的相位，本 App 按實際度數計算；150 度、45 度等現代相位無古典出處，本 App 不使用。

label.zh: 第一卷第 12 章（星座分陰陽）

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: An aspect is how many degrees apart two bodies are; the four main ones are 180, 120, 90 and 60 degrees.
summary.zh: 相位就是兩顆星體之間差幾度；主要的有四個：180、120、90、60 度。

title.zh: 相位是什麼

kicker.en: A conjunction is two bodies in one place, two forces blended together.
kicker.zh: 合相是兩顆星體湊在同一個位置，兩股力氣混在一起。

text.en: A conjunction is two bodies in the same place, with almost no angle between them. Astrology today reads it as two forces blended and hard to pull apart: with the Sun conjunct Mercury, say, your thinking and you as a person are almost stuck together, and others find it hard to separate what you say from who you are.
text.zh: 合相是兩顆星體湊在同一個位置，幾乎沒有角度差。現在的占星把它讀成「兩股力氣混在一起、分不開」：例如太陽和水星合相，你的想法和你這個人幾乎黏在一起，別人很難把你說的話和你本人分開看。

text.en: What this app does: conjunctions are computed and listed as they are, with an 8-degree orb in a birth chart. This app compares longitude: where each body has reached along the ecliptic, and how many degrees lie between them.
text.zh: 本 App 的做法：合相照實算、照實列，本命盤容許 8 度。本 App 比的是黃經差：看兩顆星體沿著黃道各走到哪裡，再算它們差了幾度。

text.en: Ask yourself: do the two bodies in a conjunction always show up together in you — feelings riding on every word, say, or a sense of duty the moment you start something? Write the two forces' names side by side and see what kind of you they make together.
text.zh: 拿來問自己：合相的兩顆星，在你身上是不是總是一起出現？例如一開口就帶著情緒，或一做事就想到責任？把那兩股力氣的名字寫在一起，看看它們合起來像什麼樣的你。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 24 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, “Of Applications and Separations,” says that when two places are not far apart, the one in front is said to apply to the one behind, and the one behind to separate — whether by bodily conjunction or through one of the traditional aspects. The text adds a detail: for a bodily conjunction, look at latitude too and count only passages on the same side of the ecliptic; for aspects that is not needed, because the rays all meet at the centre of the earth.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 24 章〈趨近與分離〉說，兩個位置隔得不遠時，前面那個算是「趨近」後面的，後面那個算是「分離」；這種關係可以發生在「身體相合」（bodily conjunction），也可以透過傳統的相位發生。原文還補了一點：身體相合要看黃緯，只算兩者在黃道同一側的情況；相位就不用，因為光線都匯到地球中心。

heading.en: Opposition: two ends of a line
heading.zh: 對分相：一條直線的兩端

kicker.en: An opposition is two bodies 180 degrees apart, at the two ends of a line.
kicker.zh: 對分相是兩顆隔 180 度，站在一條直線的兩端。

text.en: Astrology today often reads an opposition as wanting both sides and struggling to have them at once. A more useful question than “conflict” is: do these two forces tend to take turns rather than show up together?
text.zh: 現在的占星常把對分相讀成「兩邊都想要，卻很難同時要」。比起只說「衝突」，更有用的問法是：這兩股力氣是不是常常輪流出現，而不是同時出現？

text.en: The two bodies in an opposition sit in signs directly across the chart from each other, such as Aries and Libra, or Cancer and Capricorn. The usual reading is one side looking after yourself and the other after others, or one after home and the other after work. When you read it, put the weight on how the two forces share the space and take turns, finding balance like a seesaw.
text.zh: 對分相的兩顆星，落在盤上正對面的兩個星座，例如牡羊和天秤、巨蟹和摩羯。常見的讀法是一邊顧自己、一邊顧別人，或一邊顧家、一邊顧工作。讀的時候，重點放在這兩股力氣怎麼分配、怎麼輪流，像蹺蹺板一樣找平衡。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 13 gives opposition two right angles, six signs and 180 degrees, and says it is the most obvious because the two places lie on one straight line. The same chapter puts it among the ones that are not harmonious, because it joins signs of different kinds.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 13 章說對分相隔兩個直角、六個星座、180 度，它最明顯，是因為兩個位置落在同一條直線上。同一章把對分相歸在不和諧的那一類，理由是它連起不同類的星座。

kicker.en: An aspect can be drawing near or moving away, which matters most for transits.
kicker.zh: 相位分「正在靠近」和「已經走開」，看行運時最有用。

text.en: This is especially useful for transits: two degrees before and two degrees after do not feel the same. The transit reports in this app mark the phase: whether the moving body is still closing in on the exact angle or has already passed it.
text.zh: 這一點在看行運時特別實用：同樣是差兩度，正在靠近和已經走過，感覺不一樣。本 App 的行運報告會標出階段，告訴你行運的星是正往準確的角度靠近，還是已經過了準確的角度。

text.en: A birth chart is one still photo of the angles at the moment of birth. In a birth chart, note drawing near or moving away as part of that moment; what actually moves and passes through phases is the transits.
text.zh: 本命盤則是一張靜止的照片，記的是出生那一刻的角度。讀本命盤時，靠近或走開就當成那一刻的樣子記下來；真正會動、會分階段的，是行運。

text.en: What the old texts say: the point of Book I ch. 24 is direction — when two places are not far apart, the one in front applies and the one behind separates. So the old text already tells drawing near from having passed.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 24 章的重點是方向——隔得不遠時，走在前面的叫趨近，走在後面的叫分離。也就是說，古書本來就分「正在靠近」和「已經走開」。

alt.en: Diagram: a circle with a filled dot at the top for a conjunction, two bodies in one place, and a straight line through the centre for the 180-degree opposition, beside a table in words. A concept figure, not a real chart.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個圓圈，頂端有一個實心點代表合相（兩顆落在同一位置），另有一條通過圓心的直線代表 180 度的對分相。旁邊附文字對照。概念圖，不是真實星盤。

caption.en: A conjunction is one point; an opposition is the two ends of a line. Degrees after Tetrabiblos I.13 and I.24.
caption.zh: 合相是同一點，對分相是直線兩端。度數依托勒密第一卷第 13 章與第 24 章。

caveat.en: Fixed placements made up for explanation.
caveat.zh: 這是為了說明而固定的示範位置。

lines.en: Sun conjunct Mercury: what they think and how they come across are nearly one thing.
lines.zh: 太陽和水星合相：想的和表現出來的幾乎是同一件事，很難分開看。

lines.en: Moon opposite Saturn: the need to rest and the demand to be responsible take turns.
lines.zh: 月亮和土星對分相：想休息的需要，和要負責的要求，輪流出現。

lines.en: Both are about how two forces take their turn and get along.
lines.zh: 兩個講的都是這兩股力氣怎麼排隊、怎麼相處。

limitations.en: An aspect describes how two forces get along, not good or bad; drawing near or moving away in a birth chart records that one moment. Astrology is a language for describing yourself, not a forecast.
limitations.zh: 相位描述兩股力氣怎麼相處，不分好壞；本命盤裡的靠近或走開，記的是出生那一刻的樣子。占星是描述自己的語言，不是預測。

claim.en: “Conjunction is one of the four classical aspects.”
claim.zh: 「合相是古書四個相位之一。」

correction.en: The four main aspects are 180, 120, 90 and 60 degrees; a conjunction is two bodies in one place, a different relation — a bodily meeting. The chart page lists it together with the four.
correction.zh: 四個主要相位是 180、120、90、60 度；合相是兩顆星湊在同一個位置，是另一種關係——身體相合。命盤頁會把它和四個相位一起列出來。

claim.en: “An opposition means trouble.”
claim.zh: 「對分相代表這件事會出問題。」

correction.en: An opposition describes two forces pulling against each other and taking turns, like the wish to rest and the duty to be responsible. It shows you which two things need balancing.
correction.zh: 對分相描述兩股力氣在拉鋸、輪流出現，例如想休息和要負責輪流冒出來。它告訴你哪兩件事需要找平衡。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: which two things do you want at once but struggle to do at once?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你身上有哪兩件事，是「都想要，卻很難同時做」的？

objective.en: By the end you will know what a conjunction and an opposition are, how to read them, and how drawing near differs from moving away.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道合相和對分相是什麼、怎麼讀它們，以及「正在靠近」和「已經走開」差在哪。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: start with conjunctions and oppositions — they are the easiest to spot.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：先找合相和對分相，它們最容易看出來。

personalSteps.en: Find any conjunctions and oppositions in the aspect list.
personalSteps.zh: 在相位清單裡找出合相和對分相（如果有的話）。

personalSteps.en: See which two bodies each one joins, and recall what earlier lessons said they are about.
personalSteps.zh: 看它連的是哪兩顆星體，回想前面幾堂說它們各講什麼。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: are those two forces blended in you, or do they take turns?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：那兩股力氣在你身上是混在一起，還是輪流出現？

reason.en: Yes — almost no angle between them; in a birth chart, within 8 degrees counts.
reason.zh: 對，幾乎沒有角度差；本命盤差 8 度以內都算。

text.en: Two bodies in the same place
text.zh: 兩顆星體湊在同一個位置

reason.en: That is an opposition, the two ends of a line.
reason.zh: 那是對分相，站在一條直線的兩端。

text.en: Two bodies 180 degrees apart
text.zh: 兩顆星體隔 180 度

reason.en: That is a square, one right angle.
reason.zh: 那是四分相，一個直角。

text.en: Two bodies 90 degrees apart
text.zh: 兩顆星體隔 90 度

prompt.en: What is a conjunction?
prompt.zh: 合相是什麼？

reason.en: Yes; this app compares longitude — where each body has reached along the ecliptic.
reason.zh: 對；本 App 比的是黃經差，也就是兩顆星沿著黃道各走到哪裡。

text.en: Look at latitude, and count only passages on the same side of the ecliptic
text.zh: 要看黃緯，只算兩者在黃道同一側的情況

reason.en: A chart records the direction of each body in the sky.
reason.zh: 星盤記的是每顆星體在天空中的方向。

text.en: Check how far apart the two bodies are in space
text.zh: 要看兩顆在太空裡離多遠

reason.en: It is houses that need the birth time; aspects can be read without one.
reason.zh: 要出生時間的是宮位；相位沒有時間也看得到。

text.en: You need the birth time
text.zh: 要知道出生時間

prompt.en: What extra condition does the old text set for a bodily meeting?
prompt.zh: 古書談身體相合時，多要求了哪一件事？

detail.en: Book I ch. 13 gives opposition as two right angles, six signs and 180 degrees, calls it the most obvious because the places meet on one straight line, and counts it disharmonious; Book I ch. 24 says that when the interval is not great the preceding place applies and the following separates, that this holds by bodily conjunction or through the traditional aspects, and that bodily conjunction also asks for latitude to be observed, accepting only passages on the same side of the ecliptic. Fusion and taking turns are later readings, and this app uses longitude only without the latitude condition, as the lesson states.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 13 章給出對分相為兩個直角、六個星座、180 度，並說它最明顯是因為兩個位置落在同一條直線上，同時把它歸為不和諧；第一卷第 24 章說相隔不遠時前者趨近、後者分離，且此關係可透過「身體相合」或傳統相位發生，並要求談身體相合時另看黃緯、只採黃道同一側者。「兩股力氣混在一起」「輪流出現」為後世讀法；本 App 只用黃經差、不套用黃緯條件，課文已照實說明。

label.en: Book I ch. 13 (the aspects of the signs)
label.zh: 第一卷第 13 章（星座的相位）
第一卷第 24 章（趨近與分離）

rights.en: The Robbins translation is in the public domain, as the University of Chicago LacusCurtius copyright page records. The transcriber's own notes and layout are not cited.
rights.zh: Robbins 英譯本已進入公共領域，芝加哥大學 LacusCurtius 版權說明頁如此記載。轉錄者自己的註解與編排不在引用範圍。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: In a conjunction two bodies sit together; in an opposition they face each other across the chart.
summary.zh: 合相是兩顆疊在一起，對分相是兩顆隔著整張盤面對面。

title.zh: 合相與對分相

kicker.en: A trine is 120 degrees apart and joins signs of the same group.
kicker.zh: 三分相差 120 度，連起的是同一組星座。

text.en: A trine joins signs in the same triangle, that is, the same element group: fire is Aries, Leo and Sagittarius; earth is Taurus, Virgo and Capricorn; air is Gemini, Libra and Aquarius; water is Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces. Each pair within a group is four signs, 120 degrees, apart.
text.zh: 三分相連起來的，是同一個三角裡的星座，也就是同一組元素：火象的牡羊、獅子、射手；土象的金牛、處女、摩羯；風象的雙子、天秤、水瓶；水象的巨蟹、天蠍、雙魚。同一組裡的星座兩兩相隔四個星座、120 度。

text.en: Astrology today often reads it as two forces that get on naturally, with no effort. With the Moon trine Venus, for example, how you look after yourself and what you enjoy fit well, so when you relax you are naturally doing something you like.
text.zh: 現在的占星常把它讀成「這兩股力氣天生合得來、不費力」。例如月亮和金星三分相，照顧自己的方式和喜歡的東西很合拍，放鬆的時候自然就做著喜歡的事。

text.en: A more useful question than “smooth”: are these two forces so easy together that you have never practised the other way?
text.zh: 比起「很順」，更有用的問法是：這兩股力氣是不是太順了，順到你從來沒練過另一種做法？

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 13 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos gives the trine one and a third right angles, four signs and 120 degrees, and calls trine and sextile harmonious because they join signs of the same kind — all masculine or all feminine. Ch. 18 adds that the zodiac is split into four equal-sided triangles, the first through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius — exactly four signs apart from each other.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 13 章說三分相隔一又三分之一個直角、四個星座、120 度；並說三分相和六分相是和諧的，因為它們連起同一類的星座（全是陽性或全是陰性）。第 18 章又說，黃道分成四個等邊三角，第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手——剛好彼此隔四個星座。

kicker.en: A square is 90 degrees apart and joins signs of different kinds.
kicker.zh: 四分相差 90 度，連起的是不同類的星座。

text.en: Astrology today often reads a square as needing effort to make two things work together. Take Aries (fire) square Cancer (water): one wants to charge ahead, the other to look after feelings first; both want to lead, so they take turns giving way or find a new way through.
text.zh: 現在的占星常把四分相讀成「要花力氣才能協調」。例如牡羊（火）和巨蟹（水）四分相：一個想往前衝，一個想先顧好感受，兩邊都想做主，只好輪流讓步或找出新的做法。

text.en: A practical view: a square is often where a person really builds a skill, because it pushes them to handle two different approaches. The longer it catches, the more solid the skill it tends to build.
text.zh: 一個實用的看法：四分相常常是一個人真正練出本事的地方，因為它逼你同時處理兩種不同做法。卡得越久，練出來的功夫往往越紮實。

text.en: Ask yourself: in you, is it a place worth practising? Is there something that felt awkward at first and later became one of your strengths?
text.zh: 拿來問自己：在你身上，它是不是一個值得練習的地方？有沒有哪件事你一開始做得很卡，後來反而成了你的強項？

text.en: What the old texts say: the same chapter gives the square one right angle, three signs and 90 degrees, and puts it with opposition among the ones that are not harmonious, again because the signs it joins are of different kinds. The text also explains the angles with musical ratios: apply a half to opposition and you get the square.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：同一章說四分相隔一個直角、三個星座、90 度，和對分相一起歸在不和諧那一類，理由一樣是連起的星座不同類。原文也用音樂比例解釋角度怎麼來：把二分之一用在對分相上，就得到四分相。

heading.en: Harmony and tension are two categories
heading.zh: 和諧與緊張是兩種分類

kicker.en: Harmonious or not is a way of sorting, by what kind of signs are joined.
kicker.zh: 和諧、不和諧是一種分類，看的是星座屬於哪一類。

text.en: Any aspect can be read with two questions: do the two forces run smoothly, and have you ever practised the other way? For a trine the first answer is usually “smoothly,” so watch the second; for a square the first is usually “it catches,” but the answer to the second is often where your skill lies.
text.zh: 讀任何一個相位，都可以問兩個問題：這兩股力氣順不順？你有沒有練過另一種做法？三分相第一題通常答「順」，要留意第二題；四分相第一題通常答「卡」，但第二題的答案，常常就是你的本事所在。

text.en: What this app does: aspects are computed and listed as they are, each shown the same way, so you can hold them up to these two questions yourself.
text.zh: 本 App 的做法：相位照實算、照實列，每一個相位都用同樣的方式呈現，讓你拿這兩個問題自己對照。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 13 is clear about what harmonious and not harmonious rest on — whether the signs joined are of the same kind, using the masculine and feminine sorting of ch. 12. Trine and sextile are harmonious; square and opposition are not.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 13 章把和諧、不和諧的依據寫得很清楚——連起的星座是不是同一類（用第 12 章的陰陽分類）。和諧的是三分相和六分相，不和諧的是四分相和對分相。

alt.en: Diagram: a circle with two chords from the top, one for the 120-degree trine and one for the 90-degree square, beside a table saying that a trine joins one element group and a square joins unlike kinds. A concept figure, not a real chart.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個圓圈，從頂端畫出兩條弦，一條對應 120 度的三分相、一條對應 90 度的四分相，旁邊附文字對照，說明三分相連同一組元素、四分相連不同類的星座。概念圖，不是真實星盤。

caption.en: Trine at 120 and square at 90, degrees after Tetrabiblos I.13.
caption.zh: 三分相 120 度、四分相 90 度，度數依托勒密第一卷第 13 章。

caveat.en: Fixed placements made up for explanation. Real aspects are measured in exact degrees.
caveat.zh: 這是為了說明而固定的示範位置；實際算相位時，看的是精確的度數。

lines.en: Sun in Libra, Jupiter in Gemini: four signs apart, a trine, both air.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤座、木星在雙子座：隔四個星座，三分相，都是風。

lines.en: Moon in Aries, Saturn in Capricorn: three signs apart, a square, different kinds.
lines.zh: 月亮在牡羊座、土星在摩羯座：隔三個星座，四分相，不同類。

lines.en: The first runs without thinking, the second needs arranging — two different ways of working.
lines.zh: 前一個順到不用想，後一個要刻意安排——是兩種不同的做法。

limitations.en: An aspect describes how two forces get along; it is not good or bad and says nothing about luck. Astrology is a language for describing yourself, not a forecast.
limitations.zh: 相位描述兩股力氣怎麼相處，不分好壞，也不代表運氣；占星是描述自己的語言，不是預測。

claim.en: “Trines are good and squares are bad.”
claim.zh: 「三分相是好相位，四分相是壞相位。」

correction.en: A trine is a force that comes easily and a square one that takes practice; both are useful. Read an aspect by asking how smoothly the forces run and whether you have practised the other way.
correction.zh: 三分相是順手的力氣，四分相是要練的力氣，兩種都有用。讀相位時問：這兩股力氣順不順、你有沒有練過另一種做法。

claim.en: “More squares means a harder life.”
claim.zh: 「四分相多的人比較倒楣。」

correction.en: A square describes two different approaches that have to be handled together, often where a person builds real skill. Each square can be read as a place worth practising.
correction.zh: 四分相描述兩種不同做法要一起處理，常常就是一個人練出本事的地方；每一個四分相，都可以當成一個值得練習的地方來讀。

claim.en: “A trine is always within one element.”
claim.zh: 「三分相一定是同一個元素。」

correction.en: Counting by signs, yes; but measured in degrees, a position near a border can fall in the next sign, where the element is different. This app measures degrees, so now and then you will see a trine across elements.
correction.zh: 照隔幾個星座來算是這樣；但用實際度數算時，靠近交界的位置可能跨到隔壁星座，元素就不同了。本 App 照實際度數算，所以偶爾會看到跨元素的三分相。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: which of your abilities came easily, and which did you have to build?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你哪一項能力是「天生就順」，哪一項是「練出來的」？

objective.en: By the end you will know how many degrees a trine and a square are, how to spot them on a chart, and how to read the two kinds of force: one comes easily, one takes practice.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道三分相和四分相各差幾度、怎麼在盤上認出它們，以及怎麼讀這兩種力氣：一種順手，一種要練。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: find one trine and one square and compare them.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：找一個三分相、一個四分相，對照看看。

personalSteps.en: Find a trine and a square in the aspect list — you may have only one kind.
personalSteps.zh: 在相位清單裡找出三分相和四分相（可能只有其中一種）。

personalSteps.en: Look at the trine's two bodies: is that something you have always done naturally?
personalSteps.zh: 看三分相連的兩顆：那件事是不是你一直做得很自然？

personalSteps.en: Then the square's two: is that something you can only do because you practised?
personalSteps.zh: 再看四分相連的兩顆：那件事是不是你練過才會的？

reason.en: Yes — the basis is the masculine and feminine sorting in ch. 12.
reason.zh: 對，依據是第 12 章的陰陽分類。

text.en: Because the signs it joins are of different kinds
text.zh: 因為它連起的星座不是同一類

reason.en: Not harmonious rests on how the signs are sorted: the signs joined are of different kinds.
reason.zh: 不和諧的依據是星座的分類：連起的星座不同類。

text.en: Because it brings obstacles
text.zh: 因為它會帶來阻礙

reason.en: The reason is that the signs joined are of different kinds, one masculine and one feminine.
reason.zh: 理由是連起的星座屬於不同類，一個陽性、一個陰性。

text.en: Because 90 degrees is hardest to compute
text.zh: 因為 90 度最難算

prompt.en: Why is the square counted among the ones that are not harmonious?
prompt.zh: 四分相為什麼被歸在不和諧？

reason.en: Yes — four signs apart lands in the same triangle, the same element group.
reason.zh: 對，隔四個星座剛好落在同一個三角、同一組元素。

text.en: Four signs, 120 degrees
text.zh: 四個星座、120 度

reason.en: That is the square.
reason.zh: 那是四分相。

text.en: Three signs, 90 degrees
text.zh: 三個星座、90 度

reason.en: That is the sextile, covered in the next lesson.
reason.zh: 那是六分相，下一堂會講。

text.en: Two signs, 60 degrees
text.zh: 兩個星座、60 度

prompt.en: How many signs and degrees apart is a trine?
prompt.zh: 三分相隔幾個星座、幾度？

detail.en: Book I ch. 13 gives the trine one and one-third right angles, four signs and 120 degrees, and the quartile one right angle, three signs and 90 degrees, derives the angles from musical ratios, and calls trine and sextile harmonious because they join signs of the same kind while quartile and opposition are disharmonious; the masculine/feminine classification is ch. 12 and the four equilateral triangles, the first through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius, are ch. 18. Reading them as natural ease, required effort or built skill is later or this lesson's own wording, and is labelled as such.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 13 章給出三分相為一又三分之一直角、四個星座、120 度，四分相為一個直角、三個星座、90 度，並以音樂比例解釋角度來源，另說三分相與六分相因連接同類星座而稱和諧、四分相與對分相為不和諧；陰陽分類見第 12 章；四個等邊三角（第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手）見第 18 章。「天生合得來」「要花力氣」「練出本事」為後世或本課的讀法，課文已分開標示。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: A trine joins one element group, like an easy gift; a square joins different kinds, like homework to practise.
summary.zh: 三分相連起同一組元素，像順手的天分；四分相連起不同類，像要練的功課。

title.zh: 三分相與四分相

kicker.en: A sextile is two planets 60 degrees apart, two signs away.
kicker.zh: 六分相是兩顆星相隔 60 度，也就是隔兩個星座。

text.en: How to spot a sextile: count two signs forward or back from the sign a planet is in, and that is where a sextile points. Two signs forward from Aries is Gemini, two back is Aquarius; 10 degrees Aries and 10 degrees Gemini are exactly 60 degrees apart.
text.zh: 六分相怎麼認：從一顆星所在的星座往前或往後數兩個星座，就是六分相的方向。例如牡羊座往前數兩個是雙子座，往後數兩個是水瓶座；牡羊座 10 度和雙子座 10 度，正好相差 60 度。

text.en: A sextile is often read as “an opening, but you have to act”: lighter than a trine, and it does not happen by itself. What the two planets stand for can help each other, but the ease shows up once you speak first or make the first move.
text.zh: 六分相常被讀成「有機會，但要你自己動手」：比三分相淡一點，不會自己發生。兩顆星代表的事彼此幫得上忙，但要你先開口、先去做，那份順手才會出現。

text.en: When you find a sextile in your own chart, ask yourself: do the things these two planets stand for go especially smoothly when I take the first step? If you always wait for it to happen, you may never have noticed it.
text.zh: 看到自己盤上的六分相，可以問自己：這兩顆星代表的事，是不是在我主動去做的時候特別順？如果總是等它自己發生，可能就一直沒感覺到它。

text.en: In this app's aspect list the sextile has the smallest orb (4 degrees in a birth chart), so it is also the one most easily “just off, so it doesn't count.” The next section is about how far off still counts.
text.zh: 在這個 App 的相位清單裡，六分相的容許度最小（本命 4 度），所以它也最容易「差一點就不算」。下一段就講差幾度還算。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, Book I ch. 13, gives the sextile two-thirds of a right angle, two signs and 60 degrees, and counts it with the trine as harmonious because it joins signs of the same kind.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 13 章寫，六分相相隔三分之二直角、兩個星座、60 度，和三分相一起算「和諧」，理由是它連起同一類的星座。

kicker.en: Two planets need not be exactly 60 degrees apart; how far off still counts is called the orb.
kicker.zh: 兩顆星不必剛好 60 度，差一點也算；差多少還算，就叫容許度。

text.en: The orb is the range for how far off still counts. Two planets 63 degrees apart are 3 off a sextile; as long as those 3 degrees are inside the orb, the sextile counts. The less it is off, the “tighter” the aspect; near the limit, it is “looser.”
text.zh: 容許度就是「差幾度還算」的範圍。兩顆星相隔 63 度，離 60 度差 3 度；只要這 3 度在容許度裡面，這條六分相就算數。差得越少，這條相位就越「緊」；差到接近上限，就比較「鬆」。

text.en: Books and websites use wider or tighter orbs, so the same chart can list a different number of aspects. When you see someone's list of aspects, you can ask first: what orb was this worked out with?
text.zh: 不同的書和網站，容許度有寬有緊，所以同一張盤列出來的相位數量可能不一樣。看到別人列的相位時，可以先問一句：這是用幾度的容許度算的？

text.en: When you read your own aspect list, look at how far off each one is too: 0 to 1 degree is tight, close to the limit is loose. Start comparing yourself with the tightest few, then move on to the looser ones.
text.zh: 看自己的相位清單時，把「差幾度」也一起看：差 0 到 1 度的很緊，差到接近上限的比較鬆。先從最緊的那幾條開始對照自己，再看比較鬆的。

text.en: What the old texts say: Tetrabiblos Book I ch. 24 says that when two places are “not far apart,” the one in front is applying and the one behind is separating. So when two places are close, the relation already holds.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 24 章寫，兩個位置「相隔不遠」時，前面的算靠近、後面的算離開。也就是說，兩個位置相隔不遠時，關係就已經成立。

heading.zh: 這個 App 用的數字

kicker.en: Birth chart: 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, 4 for sextile.
kicker.zh: 本命盤：合相、對分相 8 度，四分相、三分相 6 度，六分相 4 度。

text.en: Birth chart: 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, 4 for sextile. Transits are read more tightly: 1 degree in general, 2 for the Sun and Moon, and “exact” means within 0.1 of a degree. These numbers are kept in one table with a version number, and every report records which version it used.
text.zh: 本命盤：合相和對分相 8 度、四分相和三分相 6 度、六分相 4 度。看行運時收得更緊：一般 1 度，太陽和月亮放寬到 2 度；差 0.1 度以內叫「正好」。這些數字寫在同一份表裡並標了版本號，每份報告都會記下用的是哪一版。

text.en: So the same chart may show a few more or fewer aspects somewhere else, and the difference usually comes from how wide the orbs are. Remember which table you are reading and comparisons stay clear.
text.zh: 所以同一張盤，換到別的地方可能多幾條或少幾條相位，差別通常來自容許度的寬緊。記得自己看的是哪一套，拿去比較就不會亂。

text.en: Try it: pick one aspect in your list, work out how far it is from the exact angle, then compare that with the numbers above to see how far it is from the limit. The further from the limit, the tighter the aspect.
text.zh: 練習一下：在相位清單裡挑一條，算出它離整數角度差幾度，再對照上面的數字，看它離上限還有多遠。離上限越遠，代表這條相位越緊。

alt.en: Diagram: a circle with a solid chord from the top for the 60-degree sextile and a dashed chord on either side at 56 and 64 degrees, showing this app's 4-degree tolerance, beside a note of the natal and transit orbs. A concept figure, not a real chart.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個圓圈，從頂端畫出一條實線代表 60 度的六分相，兩側各有一條虛線代表 56 度與 64 度，表示本 App 的 4 度容許範圍。旁邊附文字說明本命與行運的容許度數字。概念圖，不是真實星盤。

caption.en: A sextile is 60°, plus the 4° natal orb this app uses; the dashed lines mark the orb.
caption.zh: 六分相 60 度，加上本 App 用的 4 度本命容許度；虛線標出容許範圍。

caveat.en: These degrees were made up to show how orbs work; you can work through your own chart the same way.
caveat.zh: 這組度數是為了說明容許度而編的示範，換成你自己的盤也能照同樣方法算。

lines.en: Venus at 2 degrees Libra, Mars at 5 degrees Sagittarius: 63 degrees apart.
lines.zh: 金星在天秤座 2 度、火星在射手座 5 度：相差 63 度。

lines.en: A sextile is 60; 3 off is still inside 4 degrees, so it counts.
lines.zh: 六分相是 60 度，差 3 度，還在 4 度以內，所以算。

lines.en: At 5 off it would not — and a looser table elsewhere would list it.
lines.zh: 差到 5 度就不算了——換一套比較寬的表，就會多出這一條。

limitations.en: The orb numbers are this app's table; other books or websites may use different numbers and list different aspects.
limitations.zh: 容許度的數字是這個 App 用的表；別的書或網站可能用不同的數字，列出的相位也會不同。

claim.en: “An aspect only counts at the exact angle.”
claim.zh: 「相位一定要剛好整數角度才算。」

correction.en: When two places are “not far apart” the relation already holds; how far off still counts is the orb. In this app a birth-chart sextile counts within 4 degrees.
correction.zh: 兩個位置「相隔不遠」，關係就已經成立；差幾度還算，看容許度。在這個 App 裡，本命的六分相差 4 度以內都算。

claim.en: “A wider orb reads more accurately.”
claim.zh: 「容許度越寬，看得越準。」

correction.en: Widening lets more pairs in, so the list gets longer. The less an aspect is off, the tighter it is, and you can start reading from the tight ones.
correction.zh: 放寬是讓更多組合算進來，清單變長。差得越少的相位越緊，讀的時候可以先從緊的開始。

claim.en: “Sextiles are weak, so ignore them.”
claim.zh: 「六分相沒什麼用，可以忽略。」

correction.en: The old text lists the sextile side by side with the trine as harmonious. It is often missed because its orb is the smallest, so a little off and it drops out of the list.
correction.zh: 古書把六分相和三分相並列為和諧的相位。它常被漏掉，是因為它的容許度最小，差一點就不在清單上。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: which is the tightest aspect in your chart, and does its description sound like you?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你盤上最緊的一條相位是哪一條？它的描述像不像你？

objective.en: By the end you will recognise a sextile, work out how far off still counts, and use the orb to pick out the tightest aspects in your own list.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會認得六分相、會算「差幾度還算」，也會在自己的相位清單裡用容許度挑出最緊的那幾條。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: this time look not at the aspects but at how far off each one is.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：這次不看相位本身，看它「差了幾度」。

personalSteps.en: In the aspect list, find the one that is furthest off exact.
personalSteps.zh: 在相位清單裡，找出差最多度的那一條。

personalSteps.en: Think: tighten the orb by two degrees and it disappears.
personalSteps.zh: 想一想：容許度再收緊兩度，它就不見了。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: does that aspect's description sound like you or not?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：那條相位的描述，像你還是不像你？

reason.en: Yes — 3 off is still inside the sextile's 4-degree orb.
reason.zh: 對，差 3 度還在六分相的 4 度容許度裡。

text.en: Yes: 63 degrees apart is 3 off 60, inside 4 degrees
text.zh: 算：相差 63 度，離 60 度差 3 度，在 4 度以內

reason.en: A little off still counts, as long as it is inside the orb.
reason.zh: 差一點也算，只要在容許度以內。

text.en: No: it must be exactly 60 degrees
text.zh: 不算：一定要剛好 60 度

reason.en: A trine is 120 degrees; 63 is far from it and closest to the sextile's 60.
reason.zh: 三分相是 120 度，63 度離它很遠，離六分相的 60 度最近。

text.en: No: 63 degrees is closer to a trine
text.zh: 不算：63 度比較接近三分相

prompt.en: Venus at 2 Libra, Mars at 5 Sagittarius: with this app's birth-chart orbs, is it a sextile?
prompt.zh: 金星在天秤座 2 度、火星在射手座 5 度，用這個 App 的本命容許度，算不算六分相？

reason.en: Birth chart: 8 for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, 4 for sextile.
reason.zh: 本命：合相和對分相 8 度、四分相和三分相 6 度、六分相 4 度。

text.en: 4 degrees
text.zh: 4 度

reason.en: 8 is for conjunction and opposition.
reason.zh: 8 度是合相和對分相。

text.en: 8 degrees
text.zh: 8 度

reason.en: 1 degree is the general transit orb; a birth-chart sextile uses 4.
reason.zh: 1 度是看行運時的一般容許度；本命的六分相用 4 度。

text.en: 1 degree
text.zh: 1 度

prompt.en: What orb does this app use for a sextile in a birth chart?
prompt.zh: 這個 App 在本命盤上，六分相的容許度是多少？

detail.en: Book I ch. 13 gives the sextile two-thirds of a right angle, two signs and 60 degrees and lists it with the trine as harmonious, on joining signs of the same kind; Book I ch. 24 says that when the interval between two places is not great the preceding applies and the following separates, without giving any general orb figure. Reading a sextile as an opening that needs action is later usage, and this app's orb figures are a modern conventional table approved by Michael on 2026-09-30, printed in the lesson as they are.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 13 章給出六分相為三分之二直角、兩個星座、60 度，並與三分相同列為和諧（依連接同類星座）；第一卷第 24 章說兩個位置「相隔不遠」時前者趨近、後者分離，但未給出通用容許度數字。「有機會但要主動」為後世讀法；本 App 的容許度數字為現代慣用簡表，2026-09-30 經 Michael 核定，課文已照實列出。
