title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: A sextile is two planets 60 degrees apart; the orb decides how far off still counts, and this app uses 4 degrees for a birth-chart sextile.
summary.zh: 六分相是兩顆星相隔 60 度；容許度決定差幾度還算，這個 App 本命盤的六分相用 4 度。

title.zh: 六分相與容許度

kicker.en: Every sign has one way of moving: starting, holding or shifting.
kicker.zh: 每個星座都屬於一種動靜：開場、守成或轉換。

text.en: The three ways of moving are called cardinal (starting), fixed (holding) and mutable (shifting). Starting signs are good at beginning things, holding signs at keeping them going, and shifting signs at adjusting, wrapping up and handing on to the next stage.
text.zh: 星座的三種動靜叫做基本（開場）、固定（守成）、變動（轉換）。開場的星座擅長起頭，守成的擅長把事情撐下去，轉換的擅長調整、收尾，把事情接到下一段。

text.en: Starting: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn. Holding: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius. Shifting: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. An easy way to remember: the sign that opens each season is starting, the one in the middle is holding, and the one at the end, as the season turns, is shifting.
text.zh: 開場是牡羊、巨蟹、天秤、摩羯；守成是金牛、獅子、天蠍、水瓶；轉換是雙子、處女、射手、雙魚。好記的方法：每個季節開頭的星座是開場，季節中間的是守成，季節快結束、要換季的是轉換。

text.en: Some books call the starting signs solstitial and equinoctial, the holding signs solid, and the shifting signs bicorporeal. When you meet those names, match them straight back to these three groups: they are the same signs.
text.zh: 有些書把開場的星座叫「至點座、分點座」，守成的叫「固定座」，轉換的叫「雙體座」。看到這些名字時，直接對回這三組就好，說的是同一批星座。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, Book I ch. 11, splits the twelve signs into four classes and names each sign. Solstitial: Cancer and Capricorn, where the Sun turns and brings summer and winter. Equinoctial: Aries and Libra, where the Sun makes night and day equal. Solid: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius, which follow those. Bicorporeal: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces, which follow the solid ones and share in the seasons on either side. Every reason comes from the seasons and the Sun's position.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 11 章把十二星座分成四類，一個一個點名：至點座是巨蟹和摩羯（太陽在這裡轉向，帶來夏天和冬天）；分點座是牡羊和天秤（太陽在這裡讓日夜一樣長）；固定座是金牛、獅子、天蠍、水瓶（跟在至點座和分點座後面）；雙體座是雙子、處女、射手、雙魚（跟在固定座後面，帶有前後兩個季節的性質）。取名的理由全部來自季節和太陽的位置。

kicker.en: Four elements times three ways of moving makes twelve cells, one sign each.
kicker.zh: 四個元素乘三種動靜，剛好十二格，一格一個星座。

text.en: Cross the two groupings and four times three gives twelve: one sign per cell, nothing repeated and nothing missing.
text.zh: 把兩種分法交叉起來，四乘三剛好等於十二，每格正好一個星座，沒有重複也沒有空格。

text.en: How to read the table: find the row (element) first, then the column (way of moving). Leo sits in the fire row and the holding column, so it is fire plus holding; Pisces sits in the water row and the shifting column, so it is water plus shifting.
text.zh: 讀表的方法：先找行（元素），再找列（動靜）。獅子座在火那一行、守成那一列，就是「火＋守成」；雙魚座在水那一行、轉換那一列，就是「水＋轉換」。

text.en: Two words per sign are the easiest way to remember them: Aries is fire plus starting, Capricorn is earth plus starting. That is far easier than memorising twelve paragraphs of character.
text.zh: 用兩個詞描述一個星座最好記：牡羊是「火＋開場」、摩羯是「土＋開場」。這樣比背十二段性格描述輕鬆多了。

text.en: The table is a sorting tool. The four starting signs act very differently because their elements differ, and to read a person you put the two words together with a planet and a house.
text.zh: 這張表是一個分類工具。同樣是「開場」的四個星座，因為元素不同，表現差很多；要讀一個人，還要把這兩個詞配上行星和宮位一起看。

text.en: What the old texts say: Tetrabiblos Book I ch. 18 divides the zodiac into four equal-sided triangles, the first through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius; ch. 11 is the other grouping, into three ways of moving.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 18 章把黃道分成四個等邊三角，第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手；第 11 章是另一種分法（三類動靜）。

kicker.en: Look at where things cluster, not at one cell.
kicker.zh: 看整體擠在哪裡，不要只看一格。

text.en: Drop the placements you are sure of into the table and see whether they crowd into one row or one column. Start with the Sun and Moon, then Mercury, Venus and Mars, then the other planets, counting one at a time.
text.zh: 把你盤上能確定的位置填進這張表，看看是不是擠在同一行或同一列。可以先填太陽和月亮，再填水星、金星、火星，最後加上其他行星，一顆一顆數。

text.en: A crowded row (one element) often suggests you keep reaching for the same kind of attention; a crowded column (one way of moving) often suggests you favour starting, holding or shifting.
text.zh: 擠在同一行（同元素），常代表你習慣用同一種注意力；擠在同一列（同動靜），常代表你在「起步、維持、轉換」裡特別偏好其中一種。

text.en: If nothing crowds together, that is an answer too: you probably adjust to the situation and switch between ways of doing things. Every spread is a clue for looking back at yourself.
text.zh: 什麼都沒擠在一起，也是一種答案：你可能比較看場合，會換著用不同的做法。每一種分布，都是讓你回頭看看自己的一條線索。

text.en: What the old texts say: the text uses these groupings as material for later rules, used together with the other rules.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：原文把這些分類當成後面判斷規則的材料，和其他規則合在一起使用。

alt.en: Table of four groups of three: fire is starting Aries, holding Leo, shifting Sagittarius; earth is starting Capricorn, holding Taurus, shifting Virgo; air is starting Libra, holding Aquarius, shifting Gemini; water is starting Cancer, holding Scorpio, shifting Pisces.
alt.zh: 對照表，四組各三個：火是開場牡羊、守成獅子、轉換射手；土是開場摩羯、守成金牛、轉換處女；風是開場天秤、守成水瓶、轉換雙子；水是開場巨蟹、守成天蠍、轉換雙魚。

caption.en: Four element groups by three ways of moving. The groupings come from Tetrabiblos I.11 and I.18, with the modern names alongside.
caption.zh: 四個元素組 × 三種動靜。分組來自托勒密第一卷第 11 與第 18 章，名稱對照現代用法。

caveat.en: Fixed demonstration placements. The grouping is a sorting tool that helps you organise what you notice.
caveat.zh: 固定的示範位置。分組是分類工具，用來幫你整理觀察。

lines.en: Sun in Libra: air plus starting. Moon in Aries: fire plus starting.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤座：風＋開場。月亮在牡羊座：火＋開場。

lines.en: Both in the starting column: quick to begin, keeping going takes practice.
lines.zh: 兩個都在「開場」那一列：起步快，撐下去要刻意練。

lines.en: But one air, one fire: one talks first, one moves first — not the same start.
lines.zh: 但一個風一個火：一個先開口，一個先衝，不是同一種開場。

limitations.en: The spread of elements and ways of moving is a clue for describing yourself; it cannot decide anyone's character on its own.
limitations.zh: 元素和動靜的分布是描述自己的線索，不能單獨決定一個人的性格。

claim.en: “Signs in the same column act the same.”
claim.zh: 「同一列的星座，表現都一樣。」

correction.en: Two starting signs act very differently when their elements differ: Aries (fire) moves first, Libra (air) talks first. Read a sign with both words together.
correction.zh: 同樣是開場，元素不同，表現就差很多：牡羊（火）先衝，天秤（風）先開口。讀一個星座，兩個詞要一起看。

claim.en: “Most of my chart is fire, so I'm a fire person.”
claim.zh: 「我盤上火最多，所以我是火象的人。」

correction.en: A spread is a hint that shows you where to look — and an element needs a planet before you know where that energy goes.
correction.zh: 分布是觀察的提示，幫你找出值得留意的地方；元素也要配上行星，才知道那股力氣用在哪裡。

claim.en: “An even spread means no character.”
claim.zh: 「分布平均的人沒有特色。」

correction.en: An even spread is an answer too: you adjust to the situation and can switch between ways.
correction.zh: 平均也是一種答案：你可能比較看場合，能換著用不同的方式。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: do you lean to starting, holding or shifting? Give one recent example.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你比較偏「開場、守成、轉換」哪一種？舉一件最近的事。

objective.en: By the end you can lay the twelve signs out in one “element by way of moving” table, know what starting, holding and shifting look like, and see which row or column your own chart crowds into.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你能把十二星座排成一張「元素 × 動靜」的表，知道開場、守成、轉換各是什麼樣子，也看得出自己的盤擠在哪一行、哪一列。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: drop the placements you are sure of into the table.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：把能確定的位置填進那張表。

personalSteps.en: Count elements first: which row has the most?
personalSteps.zh: 先數元素：哪一行最多？

personalSteps.en: Then count ways of moving: which column has the most?
personalSteps.zh: 再數動靜：哪一列最多？

personalSteps.en: Write one line: does the fullest row or column match how you actually work?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：最多的那一行或那一列，像不像你平常做事的方式？

reason.en: Yes — the Sun turns there, bringing summer and winter.
reason.zh: 對，太陽在這兩個星座轉向，帶來夏天和冬天。

text.en: Cancer and Capricorn
text.zh: 巨蟹座和摩羯座

reason.en: Those are the equinoctial signs, where night and day are equal.
reason.zh: 那兩個是分點座，太陽在那裡讓日夜一樣長。

text.en: Aries and Libra
text.zh: 牡羊座和天秤座

reason.en: Those are two of the solid signs, in the holding group.
reason.zh: 那是固定座裡的兩個，屬於守成那一組。

text.en: Taurus and Leo
text.zh: 金牛座和獅子座

prompt.en: Which two signs does Book I ch. 11 call solstitial?
prompt.zh: 古書第一卷第 11 章把哪兩個星座叫做至點座？

reason.en: Yes — each element has three signs, exactly one starting, one holding and one shifting.
reason.zh: 對，每個元素各有三個星座，正好開場、守成、轉換各一個。

text.en: Four elements crossed with three ways of moving give one sign per cell
text.zh: 四個元素和三種動靜交叉，一格剛好一個星座

reason.en: Houses are a separate system; the same number is a coincidence.
reason.zh: 宮位是另一套系統，數字一樣是巧合。

text.en: Because there are also twelve houses
text.zh: 因為十二宮也是十二個

reason.en: The split is regular: every element has one starting, one holding and one shifting sign.
reason.zh: 分法很有規律：每個元素都有一個開場、一個守成、一個轉換。

text.en: Because the signs were split at random and happened to fill it
text.zh: 因為星座是隨便分的，剛好湊滿

prompt.en: Why does four by three fit the twelve signs exactly?
prompt.zh: 為什麼四乘三剛好排得下十二個星座？

detail.en: Book I ch. 11 names them: Cancer and Capricorn solstitial, Aries and Libra equinoctial, Taurus, Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius solid, and Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces bicorporeal, with every reason drawn from the seasons and the Sun's position; ch. 18 divides the zodiac into four equilateral triangles, the first through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius. The cardinal/fixed/mutable and fire/earth/air/water names and the crossing of the two divisions into one grid are later arrangements, labelled as such.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 11 章逐一指名：至點座為巨蟹與摩羯、分點座為牡羊與天秤、固定座為金牛、獅子、天蠍、水瓶、雙體座為雙子、處女、射手、雙魚，並說明命名理由全部來自季節與太陽位置；第 18 章把黃道分成四個等邊三角，第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手。基本／固定／變動與火土風水的名稱、以及把兩種分法交叉成一張表，都是後世的整理方式，課文已分開標示。

label.en: Book I ch. 11 (solstitial, equinoctial, solid, bicorporeal signs)
label.zh: 第一卷第 11 章（至點、分點、固定、雙體座）
第一卷第 18 章（四個三角）

rights.en: The Robbins translation is in the public domain, as the University of Chicago LacusCurtius copyright page records. The transcriber's own notes and layout are not cited.
rights.zh: Robbins 英譯本已進入公共領域，芝加哥大學 LacusCurtius 版權說明頁如此記載。轉錄者自己的註解與編排不在引用範圍。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Twelve signs are four elements times three ways of moving — one sign per cell.
summary.zh: 十二星座＝四個元素 × 三種動靜，一格剛好一個星座。

title.zh: 元素與性質

kicker.en: Domicile is the sign each planet is given as its own; seven planets share out all twelve signs.
kicker.zh: 守護是每顆行星分到的「自己的星座」，七顆行星剛好分完十二個星座。

text.en: A planet in a sign it rules is often said to be stronger, as if at home: what that planet stands for comes more easily and naturally.
text.zh: 行星落在自己守護的星座，常被說成比較有力，像回到自己家：那顆行星代表的事，做起來比較自在、順手。

text.en: The table holds seven planets: the Sun and Moon take one sign each, and Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn take two each, which uses up all twelve signs.
text.zh: 這份表收了七顆行星：太陽和月亮各拿一個星座，水星、金星、火星、木星、土星各拿兩個，十二個星座剛好分完。

text.en: How to look it up: find which sign your Venus is in, then see that Venus rules Libra and Taurus. If it is in one of them, Venus is in its own sign. Check the other planets the same way, one at a time.
text.zh: 查法：先找你的金星在哪個星座，再看表上金星守護天秤和金牛；落在其中一個，就是金星在自己的星座。其他行星照同樣方法一顆一顆查。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, Book I ch. 17, reasons like this. Cancer and Leo are closest to our zenith and make the most heat, so they go to the two lights: masculine Leo to the Sun, feminine Cancer to the Moon. The half-circle from Leo to Capricorn counts as the Sun's and Aquarius to Cancer as the Moon's, and each of the five planets takes one sign on each side. Saturn, coldest and furthest, takes Capricorn and Aquarius opposite; Jupiter, moderate, the next pair, Sagittarius and Pisces; Mars, dry, Scorpio and Aries; Venus, mild and fertile, Libra and Taurus; and Mercury, never more than one sign from the Sun, the remaining Gemini and Virgo.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 17 章這樣推——巨蟹和獅子最靠近天頂、最生熱，所以分給兩個發光體：陽性的獅子給太陽，陰性的巨蟹給月亮。再把獅子到摩羯這半圈算太陽的、水瓶到巨蟹算月亮的，五顆行星在兩邊各拿一個星座。土星最冷、最遠，拿正對面的摩羯和水瓶；木星溫和，拿接著的射手和雙魚；火星乾燥，拿天蠍和牡羊；金星溫和多產，拿天秤和金牛；水星離太陽不超過一個星座，拿剩下的雙子和處女。

kicker.en: Exaltation is another special place for a planet, and depression sits directly opposite it.
kicker.zh: 擢升是行星另一個特別的位置，失勢就在它的正對面。

text.en: Exaltation is often read as a place where a planet can really show what it does; depression as a place where it works harder and takes more effort.
text.zh: 擢升常被讀成行星特別能發揮的位置；失勢則是比較吃力、要多花一點力氣的位置。

text.en: Depression is always directly opposite exaltation: the Sun is exalted in Aries, so its depression is Libra opposite; the Moon is exalted in Taurus, so its depression is Scorpio opposite. Remember the exaltation and you can work out the depression.
text.zh: 失勢永遠在擢升的正對面：太陽擢升在牡羊，失勢就在對面的天秤；月亮擢升在金牛，失勢就在對面的天蠍。記住擢升，就推得出失勢。

text.en: When someone writes “Venus in Pisces: exalted,” you can trace the reason: Venus is moist, and Pisces is where the moist spring begins. Once you know the reason it is easy to remember, and easier to sense what that placement is about.
text.zh: 看到別人寫「金星在雙魚：擢升」時，可以對回背後的理由：金星偏濕，雙魚是潮濕春天開始的地方。知道理由，記起來就不吃力，也更能體會那個位置想表達的味道。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 19 goes planet by planet. In Aries the Sun turns north, days lengthen and its heat grows, so it is exalted in Aries and depressed in Libra; Saturn, standing opposite the Sun, is exalted in Libra and depressed in Aries. The Moon starts to grow brighter after meeting the Sun in Aries, and is exalted in Taurus, the first sign of her own triangle, with Scorpio opposite as depression. Jupiter reaches furthest north in Cancer and is at full strength, so it is exalted in Cancer and depressed in Capricorn; Mars, fiery by nature and fiercer furthest south in Capricorn, is exalted there and depressed in Cancer; Venus, moist, is strongest in Pisces where the moist spring begins, so exalted there and depressed in Virgo; and Mercury, drier, is the reverse: exalted in Virgo, the dry autumn, and depressed in Pisces.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 19 章一顆一顆說明。太陽到牡羊開始往北、白天變長、熱力變強，所以擢升在牡羊、失勢在天秤；土星要和太陽相對，擢升在天秤、失勢在牡羊。月亮在牡羊和太陽相會後開始變亮，在自己三角的第一個星座金牛擢升，對面的天蠍失勢。木星在巨蟹走到最北、力量最足，擢升巨蟹、失勢摩羯；火星本性火熱，在最南的摩羯更烈，擢升摩羯、失勢巨蟹；金星偏濕，在潮濕春天開始的雙魚最強，擢升雙魚、失勢處女；水星偏乾，反過來擢升在乾燥秋天的處女、失勢在雙魚。

kicker.en: Put the chart page next to this table and you can find which kind of place each planet is in.
kicker.zh: 對照命盤頁和這張表，你自己就查得出每顆行星的位置屬於哪一種。

text.en: The chart page lists the sign each planet is in. Put it next to this lesson's table and you can find for yourself which planets are in domicile and which in exaltation or depression.
text.zh: 命盤頁會列出每顆行星落在哪個星座。把它對照這一堂的表，你自己就能查出哪顆在守護、哪顆在擢升或失勢。

text.en: Once you have found them, ask yourself: does what the planet in its domicile or exaltation stands for come especially easily to me? Does the one in depression take a little more effort, or a longer way round?
text.zh: 查到之後，可以問自己：落在守護或擢升的那顆行星，代表的事是不是我做起來特別自在？落在失勢的那顆，是不是要多花一點力氣、繞一點路？

text.en: One placement is one clue, read together with the rest. Next time another site says “Venus in Pisces: exalted,” you will know where that comes from, and remember to look at that Venus's aspects and the house it falls in as well.
text.zh: 一個位置是一條線索，要和其他條件一起讀。下次看到別的網站寫「金星在雙魚：擢升」，你會知道這句話怎麼來的，也會記得再看看這顆金星和其他行星的相位、它落在哪一宮。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 17 opens by saying a planet's closeness to the signs comes in several kinds, including houses, triangles, exaltations and terms; chs. 20 and 21 then give two different systems of terms, the Egyptian and the Chaldaean, and note that the Egyptian one is not consistent in order or amount. Classical strength is a set of linked rules.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 17 章一開頭就說，行星和星座的親近關係有好幾種，包括守護、三角、擢升、界（terms）等；第 20、21 章還列了兩套不同的界（埃及的和迦勒底的），並指出埃及那套在順序和數量上不一致。也就是說，古典的強弱判斷是一整套互相牽連的規則。

alt.en: Table: the Sun rules Leo, exalted in Aries and depressed in Libra; the Moon rules Cancer, exalted in Taurus, depressed in Scorpio; Mercury rules Gemini and Virgo, exalted in Virgo, depressed in Pisces; Venus rules Libra and Taurus, exalted in Pisces, depressed in Virgo; Mars rules Scorpio and Aries, exalted in Capricorn, depressed in Cancer; Jupiter rules Sagittarius and Pisces, exalted in Cancer, depressed in Capricorn; Saturn rules Capricorn and Aquarius, exalted in Libra, depressed in Aries.
alt.zh: 對照表：太陽守護獅子，擢升牡羊、失勢天秤；月亮守護巨蟹，擢升金牛、失勢天蠍；水星守護雙子與處女，擢升處女、失勢雙魚；金星守護天秤與金牛，擢升雙魚、失勢處女；火星守護天蠍與牡羊，擢升摩羯、失勢巨蟹；木星守護射手與雙魚，擢升巨蟹、失勢摩羯；土星守護摩羯與水瓶，擢升天秤、失勢牡羊。

caption.en: Domicile, exaltation and depression for the seven planets, after Tetrabiblos I.17 and I.19.
caption.zh: 七顆行星的守護與擢升、失勢，依托勒密第一卷第 17 與第 19 章。

caveat.en: The demonstration uses the old text's table, as practice at looking it up.
caveat.zh: 示範用的是古書的分配表，拿來練習查表。

lines.en: Venus in Libra: one of the signs Venus rules.
lines.zh: 金星在天秤座：那是金星守護的星座之一。

lines.en: Venus in Pisces: where Venus is exalted.
lines.zh: 金星在雙魚座：那是金星的擢升位置。

lines.en: Venus in Virgo: opposite Pisces, where Venus is depressed.
lines.zh: 金星在處女座：雙魚的正對面，是金星的失勢位置。

limitations.en: Domicile, exaltation and depression are tools for describing what a planet is like, for getting to know yourself; they do not rank people or charts.
limitations.zh: 守護、擢升、失勢是描述行星性質的工具，用來認識自己，不用來替人或命盤分高下。

claim.en: “A planet in exaltation makes someone superior.”
claim.zh: 「行星在擢升位的人比較優秀。」

correction.en: The reasons for exaltation are seasons, direction and hot, cold, dry and moist: the planet and sign suit each other. It describes how a planet acts and ranks no one.
correction.zh: 擢升的理由是季節、方位和冷熱乾濕，說的是行星和星座的性質配得好；它描述一顆行星怎麼表現，不替人分高下。

claim.en: “A planet in depression is bad.”
claim.zh: 「行星失勢就是壞的。」

correction.en: Depression sits opposite exaltation and is often read as a planet working harder and taking more effort. It describes a way of doing things, not good or bad, and not something you cannot do.
correction.zh: 失勢在擢升的正對面，常被讀成那顆行星做事比較吃力、要多花力氣；它描述的是做事的方式，不是好壞，也不是做不到。

claim.en: “You have to memorise the whole table to use it.”
claim.zh: 「守護和擢升要整張背起來才會用。」

correction.en: Two patterns are enough: domicile spreads out evenly from Leo and Cancer on both sides, and exaltation and depression are always opposite. The rest you can look up.
correction.zh: 抓住兩條規律就好：守護從獅子、巨蟹往兩邊對稱排開；擢升和失勢永遠正對面。其他的看表就查得到。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: how would you now explain the idea of a “strong placement” to a friend?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：「有力位置」這種說法，你現在會怎麼跟朋友解釋？

objective.en: By the end you will recognise domicile, exaltation and depression, be able to look up which of these your own planets are in, and know the seasons and heat behind each placement.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會認得「守護」和「擢升、失勢」，會用表查出自己的行星落在哪一種位置，也知道每個位置背後的季節和冷熱理由。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: put the chart page next to this lesson's table and check one planet at a time.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：拿命盤頁對照這一堂的表，一顆一顆查。

personalSteps.en: Check the table: is any planet in a sign it rules?
personalSteps.zh: 對照表，看你有沒有行星落在自己守護的星座。

personalSteps.en: Then check: is any in its exaltation or depression?
personalSteps.zh: 再看有沒有落在擢升或失勢的位置。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: does what your planet in domicile or exaltation stands for come easily to you?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：落在守護或擢升的那顆行星，代表的事你做起來自在嗎？

reason.en: Yes — Book I ch. 17: masculine Leo to the Sun, feminine Cancer to the Moon.
reason.zh: 對，第一卷第 17 章這樣推：陽性的獅子給太陽、陰性的巨蟹給月亮。

text.en: Because they are closest to our zenith and make the most heat, so they went to the two lights
text.zh: 因為這兩個星座最靠近天頂、最生熱，所以給兩個發光體

reason.en: The reasons are astronomy and seasons: these two signs are nearest the zenith and make the most heat.
reason.zh: 理由是天文和季節：這兩個星座最靠近天頂、最生熱。

text.en: Because Leos are confident
text.zh: 因為獅子座的人比較有自信

reason.en: The reason is nearness to the zenith and heat, not brightness.
reason.zh: 理由是靠近天頂、最生熱，不是亮度。

text.en: Because the Sun and Moon are brightest there
text.zh: 因為太陽和月亮在這兩個星座最亮

prompt.en: Why does the old text give Leo to the Sun and Cancer to the Moon?

detail.en: Book I ch. 17 starts from Cancer and Leo being nearest our zenith and most productive of heat, assigns them to the Moon and the Sun, and then distributes the rest by semicircle, planetary nature, orbital distance and aspect: Saturn Capricorn and Aquarius, Jupiter Sagittarius and Pisces, Mars Scorpio and Aries, Venus Libra and Taurus, Mercury Gemini and Virgo — noting that Mercury never goes more than one sign from the Sun and Venus no more than two. Ch. 19 explains each exaltation and depression with its seasonal reasoning. Ch. 20 notes two systems of terms, Egyptian and Chaldaean, and that the Egyptian one is inconsistent in order and quantity. “Stronger in its own sign” and exaltation as a bonus are later shorthands; outer-planet rulerships have no classical source; and this app implements none of these judgments, for the reason the lesson gives.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 17 章以巨蟹、獅子最近天頂最生熱為起點，分給月亮與太陽，再以半圈與行星性質、軌道遠近、相位關係依序分配：土星得摩羯與水瓶、木星得射手與雙魚、火星得天蠍與牡羊、金星得天秤與金牛、水星得雙子與處女（並說水星離太陽不超過一個星座、金星不超過兩個）。第 19 章逐顆說明擢升與失勢及其季節理由。第 20 章指出界有埃及與迦勒底兩套系統，且埃及那套在順序與數量上不一致。「在自己星座比較有力」「擢升是加分」為後世簡化；外行星守護無古典出處；本 App 不實作這類判斷，課文已說明原因。

summary.en: Domicile is a planet's own sign; exaltation and depression are another pair of opposite places. One table shows them all.
summary.zh: 守護是行星「自己的星座」，擢升和失勢是另一組正對面的位置；一張表就查得到。

title.zh: 守護與旺弱的傳統說法

kicker.en: A planet stops, goes back for a while, then turns again; the moment it stops is called a station.
kicker.zh: 行星會停住、往回走一段，再轉回來；停住的那一刻叫「停留」。

text.en: Most of the time a planet moves forward across the sky, but now and then it slows, stops, travels back for a while, then stops again and goes forward once more. The moment it stops is a “station,” and the stretch where it goes back is “retrograde.”
text.zh: 行星在天上大多是往前走，但有時會慢下來、停住，往回走一段，然後又停住、恢復往前。停住的那一刻叫「停留」，往回走的那一段叫「逆行」。

text.en: So one retrograde has two stations: at the first it starts going back, at the second it turns forward again. Those two moments are where a planet's path gets split into stretches.
text.zh: 所以一次逆行有兩個停留：第一次停留時開始往回走，第二次停留時又轉回往前。這兩個時間點，就是把行星的一段路程切開的地方。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, Book I ch. 8, on the planets and the Sun, uses the terms “first station” and “second station” — moist from rising to the first station, hot to evening rising, dry to the second station, cold to setting. The text treats stations as something everyone knows and uses them to mark out stretches.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 8 章講行星和太陽的關係時，用了「第一次停留」「第二次停留」這些詞——從升起到第一次停留偏濕、到夜間升起偏熱、到第二次停留偏乾、到落下偏冷。原文把「停留」當成大家都知道的現象，直接拿來分段。

heading.zh: 這個 App 怎麼判斷逆行

kicker.en: This app checks one thing: whether the body's degrees are getting smaller.
kicker.zh: 這個 App 只看一件事：那顆星的度數有沒有在變小。

text.en: The method is simple: work out the degree at your moment of birth, then the degree a short moment later, and subtract. If it got smaller, the body is marked retrograde. The Sun and Moon are never marked, because seen from Earth they do not go retrograde.
text.zh: 判斷的方法很直接：先算你出生那一刻的度數，再算稍後一小段時間的度數，兩個相減。變小了，就標成逆行。太陽和月亮一律不標，因為從地球看它們不會逆行。

text.en: So the retrograde mark is a plain fact: at that moment, its degree along the zodiac was going backwards. The planet's sign and aspects are shown as usual, worked out the same way.
text.zh: 所以盤上的逆行記號是一個事實：那一刻，它在黃道上的度數正在往回走。那顆行星的星座和相位照常顯示，算法完全一樣。

text.en: On the chart page, every planet with a retrograde mark beside it was going backwards at your moment of birth. Several, just one or none at all are all common.
text.zh: 看命盤頁時，每顆旁邊有逆行記號的行星，就是你出生那一刻正在往回走的。一張盤上有好幾顆、只有一顆，或一顆都沒有，都很常見。

heading.en: Why it looks like going backwards
heading.zh: 看起來往回走，是怎麼回事

kicker.en: The planet does not really reverse; it is how Earth's own motion makes it look.
kicker.zh: 行星沒有真的倒退，是地球自己在動造成的樣子。

text.en: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day puts it plainly for Mars: Mars did not really reverse the direction of its orbit; its “going back” against the background stars reflects the motion of the Earth itself. Another entry says that about every two years Earth passes Mars on the way round the Sun, that Mars then seems to draw a loop in the sky, going back most clearly as Earth passes it, and that the same can be seen for other planets.
text.zh: NASA 的每日一天文圖講火星逆行時寫得很直接：火星沒有真的把繞行方向倒過來，它在背景星星前「往回走」，反映的是地球自己的運動。另一則說明寫到，大約每兩年，地球會在繞太陽的路上追過火星一次，那段時間火星在天空中看起來畫出一個圈，地球追過它的時候往回走最明顯；其他行星也看得到同樣的現象。

text.en: Think of overtaking on a motorway: you are going faster than the car beside you, and as you pass it, it looks as if it is sliding backwards. So Mars's retrograde also comes round about every two years.
text.zh: 可以把它想成在高速公路上超車：你開得比旁邊的車快，追過它的那一刻，那台車看起來像在往後退。所以火星的逆行，也大約每兩年出現一段。

text.en: A common saying is “don't sign contracts or have talks during Mercury retrograde.” Many people take it as a reminder: before you speak, write or sign, check the details once more.
text.zh: 常見的說法是「水星逆行不要簽約、不要談事情」。很多人把它當成一個提醒：說話、寫字、簽名之前，多看一次細節。

text.en: When you see a retrograde mark in your own chart, read it as a fact: at your moment of birth, that body was going backwards. Read the planet's sign and aspects as usual, and note the mark alongside.
text.zh: 在自己的盤上看到逆行記號，就把它讀成一個事實：出生那一刻，那顆星正在往回走。讀那顆行星時，它的星座、相位照常讀，再把這個記號一起記下來。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 8 uses the stations as points in time that mark out how a planet's qualities change.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 8 章把「停留」當成分段的時間點，用來描述行星性質的變化。

alt.en: Table: the Moon stays in a sign about two days, the Sun about a month, Mars about two months, Jupiter about a year and Saturn about two and a half years. All averages from NASA orbit periods; retrograde motion changes any single pass.
alt.zh: 對照表：月亮一個星座約兩天多，太陽約一個月，火星約兩個月，木星約一年，土星約兩年半。都是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值，逆行會讓實際時間不同。

caption.en: Retrograde motion makes real stays depart from these averages — which is what the note under the table says.
caption.zh: 逆行會讓實際停留時間偏離這些平均值——表格下方那行說明的就是這件事。

caveat.en: This demonstration explains what the mark means.
caveat.zh: 這個示範用來說明記號的意思。

lines.zh: 水星的星座和相位照常顯示、照常讀，旁邊多一個逆行記號。

lines.en: The Sun and Moon never carry the mark.
lines.zh: 太陽和月亮永遠不會有這個記號。

limitations.en: The retrograde mark only describes which way a degree was moving at your birth; it is a language for knowing yourself, not a prediction, and not good or bad.
limitations.zh: 逆行記號只描述出生那一刻的度數方向，是用來認識自己的語言，不是預測，也不代表好壞。

summary.en: Retrograde means “seen from Earth, its degrees are going backwards” — the way Earth's own motion makes it look.
summary.zh: 逆行是「從地球看，它的度數在往回走」，是地球自己在動造成的樣子。

title.zh: 逆行怎麼讀

kicker.en: A phase is how many degrees the Moon is from the Sun.
kicker.zh: 月相看的是月亮離太陽差幾度。

text.en: A phase is the aspect idea from earlier lessons, applied to the Sun and Moon: new moon is a conjunction (around 0 degrees), full moon an opposition (around 180), and the quarters are close to a square (90). The further the Moon moves on from the Sun, the more of it is lit, until it is fully lit when opposite.
text.zh: 月相就是前面學過的相位，用在太陽和月亮這一對上：新月是合相（0 度附近），滿月是對分相（180 度附近），上弦和下弦接近四分相（90 度）。月亮越往前離開太陽，亮的部分就越大，到正對面時整個亮起來。

text.en: By NASA's figures, one full round of phases (the synodic month) takes about 29.53 days, and one orbit of the Moon about 27.3217 days.
text.zh: 依 NASA 的數值：月相走完一輪（朔望月）約 29.53 天，月亮繞行一圈約 27.3217 天。

text.en: The round of phases is a little longer than one orbit because the Sun has moved on as well: when the Moon finishes its orbit the Sun has moved ahead, and the Moon needs a little over two more days to catch up.
text.zh: 月相那一輪比繞一圈長一點，是因為太陽自己也在往前走：月亮繞完一圈時，太陽已經往前移了一段，月亮要再多走兩天多才追得上。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, Book I ch. 8, splits the month into four by phase — moist from new moon to first quarter, hot from first quarter to full, dry from full to last quarter, cold from last quarter until the Moon disappears. The text uses phase as a relation between where the Sun and Moon are. Book III ch. 2 also uses the word syzygy for a new or full moon.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 8 章用月相把一個月分成四段——新月到上弦偏濕、上弦到滿月偏熱、滿月到下弦偏乾、下弦到隱沒偏冷。原文把月相當成太陽和月亮的位置關係來用。第三卷第 2 章也用「朔望」（syzygy）這個詞指新月或滿月。

kicker.en: A new moon is the Sun and Moon meeting, a full moon them facing each other; the old text used them as reference points for correcting a birth time.
kicker.zh: 新月是日月相會，滿月是日月相對；古書拿它們當校正出生時刻的參考點。

text.en: A new moon is often read as a time for beginnings, and a full moon as a time for seeing results and letting go. Many people write down what they want to start at a new moon, then look back at the full moon to see how far it has come.
text.zh: 新月常被讀成「開始」的時機，滿月常被讀成「看見結果、放下」的時機。很多人會在新月寫下想開始的事，到滿月再回頭看看走到哪裡。

text.en: Spotting them is easy: Sun and Moon in or near the same sign is the new-moon stretch; the Moon in the sign opposite the Sun is the full-moon stretch. With the Sun in Libra, for example, the Moon reaching Aries is close to full.
text.zh: 認新月滿月很簡單：太陽和月亮在同一個星座附近，就是新月那一帶；月亮在太陽正對面的星座，就是滿月那一帶。例如太陽在天秤座時，月亮走到牡羊座就接近滿月。

text.en: The chart page shows the Sun and Moon at your moment of birth and the aspect between them; from that aspect you can tell whether you were born at a new moon, a full moon, or somewhere in between.
text.zh: 命盤頁會顯示你出生那一刻的太陽、月亮，以及它們之間的相位；從這個相位，就看得出你出生在新月、滿月，還是兩者之間的哪一段。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 2 first notes that birth times taken from water clocks and sundials often err. To fix the degree of the birth moment, take the syzygy — new or full moon — just before the birth, work out its degree exactly (both lights at a new moon, the one above the horizon at a full moon), then see which stars rule that place at the birth. So in the old texts new and full moons are reference points for a calculation.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第三卷第 2 章先說，用水鐘、日晷記下的出生時刻常有誤差；要定出生時刻那一度，就取出生前最近的一次朔望——新月或滿月——把度數算準（新月取兩個發光體的度數，滿月取在地平線上的那一個），再看出生時哪些星主管那個位置。所以在古書裡，新月滿月是計算用的參考點。

heading.en: Reading your own Sun and Moon
heading.zh: 怎麼看自己的日月距離

kicker.en: What you look at is how far apart your Sun and Moon are.
kicker.zh: 看的是太陽和月亮隔多遠。

text.en: The birth phase is often read as “how far your inner needs sit from the way you come across”: near a new moon the two point the same way, so what you want and what you show are close; near a full moon they face each other, and you often look for a balance between the two.
text.zh: 出生月相常被讀成「你的內在需求和對外表現離多遠」——新月附近的人，兩者幾乎同一個方向，想要的和表現出來的差不多；滿月附近的人，兩者正對面，常在兩邊之間來回找平衡。

text.en: You can check it yourself: how many signs apart are your Sun and Moon? Zero or one is roughly the new-moon stretch; six is the full-moon stretch; about three is near a quarter. Sun in Leo and Moon in Aquarius, for example, are six apart: the full-moon stretch.
text.zh: 你可以自己檢查：你的太陽和月亮差幾個星座？差 0 到 1 個，大概是新月那一帶；差 6 個，就是滿月那一帶；差 3 個左右，接近上弦或下弦。例如太陽在獅子座、月亮在水瓶座，差 6 個，就是滿月那一帶。

text.en: The Moon moves about 12° a day. So without a birth time the number of signs apart is usually still clear, but the exact angle needs the time.
text.zh: 月亮一天大約走 12 度。所以沒有出生時間時，差幾個星座通常還看得出來，但確切的角度要有出生時間才算得準。

text.en: Without a birth time, this app shows the range of the angle across your whole birth day instead: the two ends of the range are the earliest and latest angles possible that day.
text.zh: 沒有出生時間時，這個 App 會改給出生那一整天的角度範圍：範圍的兩端，就是那天最早和最晚可能的角度。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 8 uses phase to split up qualities, in order moist, hot, dry and cold.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第一卷第 8 章把月相當成性質的分段，依序是偏濕、偏熱、偏乾、偏冷四段。

alt.en: Diagram: four circles shading from light to dark for new moon, first quarter, full and last quarter, with a note that the text calls new to first quarter moist, first quarter to full hot, full to last quarter dry and last quarter to occultation cold. The circles show order only.
alt.zh: 示意圖：四個由淺到深的圓圈，依序代表新月、上弦、滿月、下弦，並附文字說明原文把新月到上弦列為偏濕、上弦到滿月偏熱、滿月到下弦偏乾、下弦到隱沒偏冷。圓圈只表示順序。

caption.en: The four phases of the month, from new moon to full and back.
caption.zh: 一個月裡的四段月相，從新月到滿月再回到新月。

caveat.en: Fixed demonstration placements. This app works in degrees; counting signs is an easy way to explain.
caveat.zh: 固定的示範位置。這個 App 用度數計算，數星座差幾個是方便說明的算法。

lines.en: Sun in Libra, Moon in Aries: six signs apart, near the full-moon stretch.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤座、月亮在牡羊座：差六個星座，接近滿月那一帶。

lines.en: The need to rest and the wish to be seen sit opposite each other.
lines.zh: 想休息的需求，和想被看見的方向，剛好在對面。

lines.en: Put the Moon in Libra instead and it is the new-moon stretch, both pointing the same way.
lines.zh: 如果月亮改在天秤座，就是新月那一帶，兩者幾乎同一個方向。

limitations.en: Without a birth time, the angle between the Sun and Moon is shown as a range across your whole birth day, not a single number.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，日月之間的角度會以出生那一整天的範圍顯示，不是單一個數字。

limitations.en: Reading the phases is a language for describing yourself, not a prediction, and promises no wish will come true.
limitations.zh: 月相的讀法是描述自己的語言，不是預測，也不保證願望會實現。

claim.en: “Wish on a new moon and it will come true.”
claim.zh: 「新月許願，願望就會實現。」

correction.en: A new moon is an angle between the Sun and Moon. Writing down what you want to start at a new moon and looking back at the full moon is a good habit for sorting your thoughts; whether it happens depends on what you do.
correction.zh: 新月是太陽和月亮的一個角度。在新月寫下想開始的事、到滿月回頭看，是幫自己整理心思的好習慣；事情做不做得到，靠的是你自己的行動。

claim.en: “Phases are a separate system.”
claim.zh: 「月相是另一套獨立的系統。」

correction.en: A phase is just the angle between Sun and Moon: new moon a conjunction, full moon an opposition.
correction.zh: 月相就是太陽和月亮之間的角度：新月是合相、滿月是對分相。

claim.en: “One orbit of the Moon is one round of phases.”
claim.zh: 「月亮繞一圈就是一輪月相。」

correction.en: One orbit is about 27.3217 days and one round of phases about 29.53, because the Sun has moved on too.
correction.zh: 繞一圈約 27.3217 天，一輪月相約 29.53 天；差別是因為太陽也在往前走。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: how many signs apart are your Sun and Moon, and does that distance match how you really feel?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你的太陽和月亮差幾個星座？那個距離像不像你真實的感受？

objective.en: By the end you will know that a moon phase is simply the angle between the Sun and Moon, be able to see from your own chart which stretch of the phases you were born in, and recognise a new and a full moon.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道月相就是太陽和月亮之間的角度，會從自己的盤看出你出生在月相的哪一段，也會認得新月和滿月。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: you can do this without a birth time; the exact angle just becomes a range.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：沒有出生時間也能做，只是確切角度會變成一個範圍。

personalSteps.en: Find your Sun and Moon signs and count how many signs apart they are.
personalSteps.zh: 找出你的太陽和月亮星座，數一數差幾個星座。

personalSteps.en: Zero or one is the new-moon stretch, six the full-moon stretch, about three is close to a square.
personalSteps.zh: 差 0 到 1 個是新月那一帶，差 6 個是滿月那一帶，差 3 個左右接近四分相。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: do your inner needs and the way you come across point the same way, or pull against each other?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：你的內在需求和對外表現，是同一個方向，還是對著幹？

reason.en: Yes — a phase is the Sun–Moon angle, and at full moon they face each other.
reason.zh: 對，月相就是日月之間的角度，滿月時兩者正對面。

text.en: An opposition between Sun and Moon, around 180 degrees
text.zh: 太陽和月亮的對分相（約 180 度）

reason.en: That is a new moon.
reason.zh: 那是新月。

text.en: A conjunction of Sun and Moon
text.zh: 太陽和月亮的合相

reason.en: A phase involves only the Sun and Moon.
reason.zh: 月相只看太陽和月亮這兩顆。

text.en: An aspect between the Moon and the Ascendant
text.zh: 月亮和上升的相位

prompt.en: Put in terms of aspects, what is a full moon?
prompt.zh: 用相位的說法，滿月是什麼？

reason.en: Yes — the text first says water clocks and sundials often err, then gives this correction.
reason.zh: 對，原文先說水鐘、日晷常有誤差，再給這個校正方法。

text.en: As a reference point for fixing the degree of the birth moment
text.zh: 當成校正出生時刻那一度的計算參考點

reason.en: This chapter uses the syzygy to correct the birth time.
reason.zh: 這一章是用朔望來校正出生時刻。

text.en: Because it is a good day to make wishes
text.zh: 因為那天適合許願

reason.en: The Moon's sign is calculated directly; this passage is about correcting the time.
reason.zh: 月亮星座直接算就有，這一段是在校正時刻。

text.en: To decide the Moon's sign
text.zh: 為了決定月亮星座

prompt.en: Why does Book III ch. 2 take the syzygy just before the birth?
prompt.zh: 第三卷第 2 章為什麼要取出生前最近的朔望？

detail.en: Book I ch. 8 divides the month by phase — moist from new moon to first quarter, hot to full, dry to last quarter, cold to occultation. Book III ch. 2 first notes that birth times taken from water clocks and sundials often err, then requires taking the syzygy most recently preceding the birth, establishing its degree accurately — both luminaries at a new moon, the one above the earth at a full one — and seeing which stars rule that place. Reading the birth phase as the distance between inner and outer is later usage, and new-moon wishing has no classical source, which the lesson states.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 8 章以月相分段（新月到上弦偏濕、上弦到滿月偏熱、滿月到下弦偏乾、下弦到隱沒偏冷）；第三卷第 2 章先說以水鐘、日晷取得的出生時刻常有誤差，再要求取出生前最近的朔望（新月或滿月）精確求度數，新月取兩個發光體、滿月取在地平線上者，再看何者主管該位置。「出生月相代表內外距離」為後世讀法；「新月許願、滿月釋放」查無古典出處，課文明示不作此主張。

label.en: Book I ch. 8 (the power of the aspects to the Sun)
label.zh: 第一卷第 8 章（行星與太陽的相位）
第三卷第 2 章（上升度數）

summary.en: A moon phase is how far apart the Sun and Moon are: full moon is an opposition, new moon a conjunction.
summary.zh: 月相就是太陽和月亮相隔多遠；滿月是對分相，新月是合相。

title.en: Lunar Phase and the Sun–Moon Pair
title.zh: 月相與日月關係

kicker.en: The Ascendant depends on the birth time; a little off, and it may land in another sign.
kicker.zh: 上升靠出生時間決定，時間差一點，上升就可能換一個星座。

text.en: The Ascendant changes sign about every two hours. So a birth time off by an hour or two may put the Ascendant in another sign, and right at the border between two signs a few minutes can make a difference. When the Ascendant moves, the whole ring of twelve houses turns with it.
text.zh: 上升平均每兩小時換一個星座。所以出生時間差一兩個小時，上升就可能換一個星座；剛好落在兩個星座交界附近時，差幾分鐘也會不一樣。上升一換，十二宮的位置也跟著整圈轉動。

text.en: To find your birth time, look at your birth certificate, hospital records or baby book, or ask your family. If all you remember is “some time in the morning,” leave it blank and add the exact time once you find it, so the Ascendant and houses you see are really yours.
text.zh: 想找回出生時間，可以查出生證明、醫院紀錄或媽媽手冊，也可以問家人。如果只記得「大概早上」，先空著，等查到確切時間再補上，看到的上升和宮位才會是你的。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, Book III ch. 2, opens by admitting that the most important and most troublesome thing is the birth time down to the minute. Only measuring with proper instruments at the birth gets the minute; the other tools most people use often err — sundials when their position or pointer shifts, water clocks when they clog, run unevenly or by plain chance. So he then gives a method that uses the new or full moon just before the birth to work out the degree that should be rising.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 2 章一開頭就承認：最重要也最麻煩的，是出生那一刻精確到分的時間。只有出生當下用觀測儀器實測才準到分；多數人用的其他器具常出錯——日晷會因為位置或指針歪掉而錯，水鐘會因為堵住、流得不均或純粹意外而錯。所以他接著提出一套方法，用出生前最近的一次新月或滿月，推算當時應該上升的度數。

heading.en: What is left without a time

kicker.en: The empty row is itself the answer.
kicker.zh: 空著的那一行，本身就是答案。

text.en: With no birth time, this app takes a position every hour across your day of birth (25 samples, covering the whole local day) and sees which signs each body was in that day. If there was one, it is shown as it is; if there were two, both are listed and marked “unconfirmed.” The Ascendant, Midheaven and houses need a birth time to be calculated, so that layer is left empty.
text.zh: 沒有出生時間時，這個 App 會在你出生那一天每小時取一次位置（共 25 次，涵蓋當地一整天），看每顆星那天出現過哪些星座。只出現一個就照實顯示；出現兩個就兩個都列出來，標成「未確定」。上升、天頂和宮位那一層要有出生時間才算得出來，所以先留空。

text.en: So without a birth time you can still read your Sun, most planets' signs and every aspect. The Moon shows two candidates more often, because it changes sign every couple of days.
text.zh: 所以沒有出生時間，你還是看得到太陽、多數行星的星座，以及全部相位。月亮比較常出現兩個候選，因為它兩天多就換一個星座。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 2 makes the rising degree the starting point of the whole chart; with that starting point, the houses can be laid out.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：第三卷第 2 章把上升度數當成整張盤的起算點；有了這個起點，宮位才排得起來。

heading.en: What an empty row is good for

kicker.en: Leave it empty and you can tell what was calculated from what is still waiting for data.
kicker.zh: 留空，你就分得出哪裡是算出來的、哪裡還在等資料。

text.en: This app works from the data you give it: what can be calculated is shown as it is, and the layer that needs a birth time is left empty until you add one.
text.zh: 這個 App 照你給的資料算：算得出來的照實顯示，需要出生時間才算得出來的那一層就留空，等你補上。

text.en: The good thing about an empty row is that you see at a glance what was calculated and where there is no data yet. Every row it shows was really calculated. If you find the exact time later you can add it any time, and the house layer appears.
text.zh: 留空的好處是：你一眼就知道哪裡是算出來的、哪裡還沒有資料。顯示出來的每一格都是真的算出來的。之後查到確切時間，隨時可以補上，宮位那一層就會出現。

text.en: Without a time, get to know the layers that are certain: the Sun, the planets' signs, every aspect, and the Moon's two candidates — compare the two descriptions and see which sounds more like you. Once you add a time, the Ascendant and houses join in and the same chart gains a layer of detail.
text.zh: 沒有時間的時候，先把確定的那幾層讀熟：太陽、行星星座、全部相位，還有月亮的兩個候選——對照兩段描述，看哪一個比較像你。等補上時間，再加上上升和宮位，同一張盤就多了一層細節。

text.en: What the old texts say: the text's answer is a whole set of rules — domicile, exaltation, terms and aspects — used to work out the degree that should be rising. That is a grounded procedure you can check.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：原文的做法，是用一整套規則（守護、擢升、界、相位）去推算應該上升的度數——那是有根據、可以檢查的程序。

alt.en: Table: the Sun's sign is present, with two candidates on a changeover day; most planetary signs are present, with candidates for the fast ones on a boundary day; the Moon often has two candidates; aspects are present and need no birth time; the Ascendant is absent, its row empty; and the twelve houses are absent, the whole layer missing.
alt.zh: 對照表：太陽星座有（交界日列兩個候選）；多數行星星座有，走得快的在交界日列候選；月亮常有兩個候選；相位有，不需要出生時間；上升沒有，那一格是空的；十二宮沒有，整層不存在。

caption.en: With the birth time unknown: which parts of the chart have data, and which stay blank.
caption.zh: 出生時間不明時，盤上哪幾格有資料、哪幾格留白。

caveat.en: This demonstration shows how things are displayed.
caveat.zh: 這個示範用來說明畫面怎麼顯示。

lines.en: A chart with no time: Sun in Libra, confirmed.
lines.zh: 沒有時間的盤：太陽在天秤座，確定。

lines.en: The Moon is in Aries or Taurus; both are listed for you to compare.
lines.zh: 月亮可能在牡羊座或金牛座，兩個都列出來，讓你自己對照。

lines.en: The Ascendant row is left empty, and the house layer appears once there is a time.
lines.zh: 上升那一行留空，宮位那一層等有了時間才出現。

limitations.en: Without a birth time, the Ascendant, Midheaven and houses are not shown, and a body that changed sign on your birth day is listed with two candidate signs.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，上升、天頂和宮位不會顯示；在出生那天換星座的行星，會列出兩個候選星座。

claim.en: “Without a birth time there is nothing to read.”
claim.zh: 「沒有出生時間，盤就不能看。」

correction.en: The Sun, most planets' signs and every aspect still hold. What waits for a time is the Ascendant and the house layer.
correction.zh: 太陽、多數行星的星座和全部相位都照樣成立；要等有時間才出現的，是上升和宮位那一層。

claim.en: “Just use noon, or midnight.”
claim.zh: 「用中午或出生當天 0 點算一下就好。」

correction.en: The Ascendant changes sign about every two hours, so using noon invents a starting point. This app leaves that layer empty, so everything you see is data that could be calculated.
correction.zh: 上升平均每兩小時換一個星座，用中午算等於編一個起算點。這個 App 會把那一層留空，讓你看到的都是算得出來的資料。

claim.en: “The ancients had reliable times.”
claim.zh: 「古人有時間就一定算得準。」

correction.en: Book III ch. 2 opens by saying sundials shift and water clocks stop — that is why a correction method was needed at all.
correction.zh: 第三卷第 2 章一開頭就說日晷會歪、水鐘會停，所以才需要校正方法。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: would you rather see a blank or a rough guess, and why?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你比較能接受「空著」，還是「填一個大概」？為什麼？

objective.en: By the end you will know what a chart still shows without a birth time, which layer waits for the time, and how to go about finding your birth time.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道沒有出生時間時盤上還看得到什麼、哪一層要等時間才出現，以及怎麼去找回自己的出生時間。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: this lesson matters most if you do not know your birth time.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：不知道出生時間的人，這一堂最重要。

personalSteps.en: See which bodies are marked unconfirmed, with two candidates listed.

detail.en: Book III ch. 2 opens by admitting that the fraction of the hour of birth is the hardest thing to obtain: only instrumental observation at the time gives the minute, while sundials err through a shifted position or gnomon and water clocks through stoppages, uneven flow or chance. It then offers a method for inferring the degree that should be rising from the syzygy most recently preceding the birth, using domicile, exaltation, terms and aspect. This app implements neither that correction nor any default time, for the reason the lesson gives.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 2 章開頭承認出生那一刻的「時的分數」最難取得：只有出生時以觀測儀器實測才能得分，日晷會因位置或指針偏移而錯、水鐘會因阻塞、流速不均或偶然而錯；因此提出以出生前最近朔望推算應上升度數的方法，並用到守護、擢升、界與相位。本 App 未實作該校正方法，也不預設時間，課文已說明原因。

summary.zh: 沒有時間，星座和相位照樣成立；有了時間，才會多出上升和宮位那一層。

title.en: When the Birth Time Is Uncertain
title.zh: 出生時間不確定時

kicker.en: A transit is two tables of positions compared.
kicker.zh: 行運就是兩張位置表拿來比一比。

text.en: Once a day this app works out that day's positions and compares them with the positions at your moment of birth, looking for the angles taught earlier. Any it finds are listed, naming which body has reached which of your placements. With a birth time, transits to the Ascendant and houses are added too.
text.zh: 這個 App 每天算一次當天的星星位置，再跟你出生那一刻的位置比，看有沒有形成前面學過的那幾個角度。有的話就列出來，並寫明是哪一顆走到你的哪一個位置。有出生時間的話，還會多出走到上升和各宮的那些行運。

text.en: So a transit is the result of comparing two sets of degrees. Today's sky is the same for everyone. What differs is your own table from the moment you were born — which is why the same day touches different placements for different people.
text.zh: 所以行運是兩組度數比出來的結果。今天的天空對每個人都一樣，不一樣的是你出生那一刻的位置表——所以同一天，對不同人會碰到不同的位置。

kicker.en: Read a transit by three things: what is moving, what it touches, and the angle.
kicker.zh: 讀行運看三件事：誰在走、碰到你哪裡、成什麼角度。

text.en: To read a transit, look at three things: which body is moving, which of your placements it touches, and what angle it makes. Take “transiting Mars square your Sun”: Mars is moving, your Sun is touched, and the angle is a square.
text.zh: 讀一條行運，看三件事：哪一顆在走、碰到你的哪一個位置、形成哪一種角度。例如「行運火星四分你的太陽」：走的是火星，碰到的是你的太陽，角度是四分相。

text.en: A common reading is that the moving body brings the theme of that stretch of time, and the placement it touches is the part of you that gets stirred. So the same transiting body reads differently on your Sun than on your Moon.
text.zh: 常見的讀法是：走動的那顆星帶來那段時間的主題，被碰到的那個位置，是你身上被牽動的那一塊。所以同一顆行運星，碰到你的太陽和碰到你的月亮，讀起來就不一樣。

text.en: How to compare: write down what those days were actually like, then look back after a while to see which descriptions fit and which did not. Bit by bit you learn which transits show most clearly in you.
text.zh: 對照的方法：把那幾天的實際狀況寫下來，過一陣子回頭看，哪些描述對得上、哪些對不上。這樣你會慢慢知道哪幾種行運在你身上最明顯。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy deals with “when” in Tetrabiblos Book IV ch. 10, “Of the Division of Times.” It divides a life into stages by rule, and says general conditions (such as country of birth) come before particular details: first the wider setting, then the personal details.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密處理「什麼時候」的是《四書》第四卷第 10 章〈時間的劃分〉。那一章照規則把一生分成幾個階段，並明說大方向的條件（例如出生地）要比個別細節優先。也就是先看大環境，再看個人的細節。

kicker.en: A transit counts within 1 degree, or 2 for the Sun and Moon.
kicker.zh: 行運一般只差 1 度內才算，太陽月亮放寬到 2 度。

text.en: For transits the orbs are tighter than for a birth chart: 1 degree in general, 2 for the Sun and Moon, and “exact” means within 0.1 of a degree. The reason is simple: a transit is about “now,” and an 8-degree orb would keep one angle going for weeks, which is no longer now.
text.zh: 看行運時，容許度收得比本命緊：一般 1 度，太陽和月亮放寬到 2 度，差 0.1 度以內才叫「正好」。理由很簡單：行運講的是「現在」，放寬到 8 度會讓一個角度維持好幾週，那就不算現在了。

text.en: Slow bodies — Jupiter, Saturn and the outer planets — stay a while even inside a 1-degree orb, while the Moon is gone in a day. So the difference between “these few days” and “these few years” mostly comes from which body is moving.
text.zh: 走得慢的星（木星、土星和外行星）就算容許度只有 1 度，也會停比較久；月亮則一天就過去了。所以「這幾天」和「這幾年」的差別，多半來自是哪一顆在走。

alt.en: Table: the Moon stays in a sign about two days, the Sun about a month, Mars about two months, Jupiter about a year and Saturn about two and a half years. All averages from NASA orbit periods; retrograde motion changes any single pass.
alt.zh: 對照表：月亮一個星座約兩天多，太陽約一個月，火星約兩個月，木星約一年，土星約兩年半。都是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值，逆行會讓實際時間不同。

caption.en: Which body is moving decides roughly how long a transit lasts. The figures are averages worked out from NASA orbit periods.
caption.zh: 哪一顆在走，決定一次行運大概持續多久。數字是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值。

limitations.en: A transit is a language for comparing with your own days; it predicts no events and gives no warnings.

detail.en: Book IV ch. 10, “Of the Division of Times,” is the text's chapter on when things happen. It divides a life into stretches by rule and requires general conditions such as country of birth to take precedence over particular details; it is not the modern technique of today's positions against a birth chart. That chapter also generalises about peoples in the terms of its era, which this lesson neither cites nor uses. Transits here are a modern technique with this app's own orbs — 1 degree in general, 2 for the lights — as the lesson states.
detail.zh: 第四卷第 10 章〈時間的劃分〉是原文處理「什麼時候」的章節，做法是依規則把一生劃分為階段，並要求一般性條件（如出生地）優先於個別細節；與現代「今日星體對上出生盤」的行運不是同一種技術。該章另含以族群概括人的敘述，屬當年世界觀，本課完全未引用、未使用。本 App 的行運為現代技術，容許度為本 App 自訂（一般 1 度、日月 2 度），課文已照實說明。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: A transit is today's planet positions held up against the positions at your birth.
summary.zh: 行運就是拿「今天的星星位置」去對「你出生那一刻的位置」。

title.zh: 行運是什麼

kicker.en: The man who wrote the system said himself that predictions can fail.
kicker.zh: 寫這套系統的人，自己就說預測會錯。

text.en: Ptolemy admits two things outright: predictions sometimes fail, and what a person turns out like depends on more than the sky — seed, birthplace and upbringing count too.
text.zh: 托勒密在書裡直接承認兩件事：第一，預測有時候會錯；第二，一個人長成什麼樣子，不只看天上，還跟種子（先天）、出生的地方、怎麼被養大有關。

text.en: So by the old texts’ own standard, a chart is one angle to look from, with many other forces at work in a life. Next time someone says “you will definitely …”, remember this, then rephrase it as “you may tend to …” and hold it up against your own recent experience.
text.zh: 所以，照古書自己的標準，星盤是一個參考角度，人生還有許多力量一起作用。下次聽到「你一定會怎樣」，可以先想起這一段，再把那句話換成「你可能比較常……」，拿自己最近的經驗對照看看。

text.en: What the old texts say: the title of Book I ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos is itself “how far knowledge is attainable.” It says the heavenly bodies and the earth never return to exactly the same positions within human experience, “so that for this reason predictions sometimes fail, because of the disparity of the examples on which they are based.” The same chapter says differences of seed, place of birth, and rearing and custom all make a difference, and that those who think everything can be understood from the heavens alone run into much difficulty.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 2 章的標題就是「可知到什麼程度」。書裡說，天體和地球不會在人能經歷的時間裡回到完全一樣的位置，「因此預測有時候會失誤，因為所依據的例子彼此並不相同」。同一章也說，種子的差異、出生地點、養育與習俗都會一起造成差別；以為一切都能單靠天體運行看懂的人，會遇到很大的困難。

kicker.en: Astrology is at its most useful as a language for describing yourself.
kicker.zh: 占星最好用的地方，是當成一套描述自己的語言。

text.en: The most direct way to judge whether a claim holds up is to test it, ideally double-blind: neither the people judging nor the people tested know whose data is whose, so expectations cannot steer the result. The idea that signs or planet positions predict personality, ability or big life events is still waiting for evidence; saying it has been “completely disproved” needs evidence too. So whenever you hear a chart reading, first ask: has anyone tested this?
text.zh: 判斷一個說法靠不靠得住，最直接的方法是拿去測，而且最好是雙盲：做判斷的人和受測的人都不知道哪份資料是誰的，結果才不會被先入為主帶著走。「星座或行星位置能預測性格、能力或人生大事」這個說法，目前還在等證據；說它「已經被完全推翻」，同樣也要拿證據來說。所以聽到任何一句星盤說法，先問：這句話有人測過嗎？

text.en: Where astrology really helps is as a descriptive language two thousand years in use. It hands you ready-made words that give a name to feelings you could not put into words: Venus for what you like and find worthwhile, Saturn for where you demand the most of yourself. With the words, it is easier to stop and see yourself clearly, and easier to explain yourself to others.
text.zh: 占星真正好用的地方，是一套用了兩千年的描述語言。它給你現成的詞，讓說不清楚的感覺有名字：例如用金星講你喜歡什麼、覺得什麼值得，用土星講你在哪裡給自己最多要求。有了詞，你比較容易停下來看清自己，也比較容易跟別人說明白。

text.en: It also gives you angles. A chart works like a list of questions: every placement can become a question you ask yourself, the answers come from your own life, and the decisions are yours. Ask the same chart this year and next and the answers can differ, which is exactly what makes it useful.
text.zh: 它也給你角度。一張盤就像一份問題清單：每一個位置都能變成一個問自己的問題，答案從你的生活裡找，決定由你自己做。同一張盤，今年問和明年問，答案可以不一樣，這正是它好用的地方。

text.en: Someone did test it formally: in 1985 Nature, vol. 318, published Shawn Carlson’s “A double-blind test of astrology.” The public record page says the study ran two double-blind tests of the claim that natal charts can accurately describe personality traits.
text.zh: 有人正式測過這件事：1985 年《Nature》第 318 期刊出 Shawn Carlson 的〈A double-blind test of astrology〉。公開的記錄頁寫著，這份研究做了兩次雙盲測試，檢驗「出生盤能準確描述人格特質」這個說法。

text.en: What the old texts say: Ptolemy’s reasoning was that the heavens change the air and moisture around the Earth (Book I ch. 2) — the natural philosophy of his time.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密的理由是天體會改變地上的空氣和水氣（第一卷第 2 章），那是他那個年代的自然哲學。

kicker.en: Turn every chart reading into a question you ask yourself.
kicker.zh: 把每一句星盤說法，變成一個問自己的問題。

text.en: This app gives you three things: where each body actually is in the chart, what the old texts and later readings say, and steps for observing yourself. The small tag beside each paragraph tells you whether it is the old text, a later reading, an exercise, or a fact the app worked out. Every chart is treated as equal, with no scores and no rankings.
text.zh: 這個 App 給你三樣東西：盤上每一顆星的實際位置、古書和後來的說法、以及觀察自己的步驟。每一段旁邊的小標籤會告訴你，那一段是古書、後人的說法、練習，還是 App 算出來的事實。每一張盤都平等看待，沒有分數，也沒有排名。

text.en: The method is simple: when you read a statement, rewrite it as a question. “Tradition reads the tenth house as your public standing” becomes “in my work and public role, where have I felt pressure lately, and where have I felt satisfied?”; “the Moon shows what you need to feel safe” becomes “what has made me feel safe lately?” Write the answers down, and they are your own observations.
text.zh: 用法很簡單：讀到一句說法，就把它改寫成問題。「傳統把第十宮看成你在外面的身分」可以變成「我在工作和對外的身分上，最近哪裡讓我覺得有壓力、哪裡讓我有成就感？」；「月亮看你需要什麼才安心」可以變成「最近什麼事讓我覺得安心？」答案寫下來，就是你自己的觀察。

text.en: For the decisions that really matter — work, relationships, money, health, moving — decide with the real information you have: talk to the people involved, ask a professional, look at the actual numbers. What the chart does here is help you put your feelings and what you care about into words, so you know better what you want; which road you take is your choice.
text.zh: 真正要做決定的事——工作、感情、錢、健康、搬家——用你手上的真實資訊來決定：跟當事人談、問專業的人、看實際的數字。星盤在這裡的用處，是幫你把自己的感受和在意的事說清楚，讓你更知道自己想要什麼，走哪條路由你自己選。

text.en: What the old texts say: the book also has chapters on health, marriage, children, death and wealth (in Books III and IV, for example). Book I ch. 3 argues that the study is beneficial.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：書裡也有健康、婚姻、子女、死亡、財富這些章節（例如第三卷、第四卷）。第一卷第 3 章主張，這門學問對人有益。

alt.en: Table: the Sun's sign is present, with two candidates on a changeover day; most planetary signs are present, with candidates for the fast ones on a boundary day; the Moon often has two candidates; aspects are present and need no birth time; the Ascendant is absent, its row empty; and the twelve houses are absent, the whole layer missing.
alt.zh: 對照表：太陽星座有（交界日列兩個候選）；多數行星星座有，走得快的在交界日列候選；月亮常有兩個候選；相位有，不需要出生時間；上升沒有，那一格是空的；十二宮沒有，整層不存在。

caption.en: What is known is shown as it is, candidates are both listed, and the rest stays blank. Read your own chart in the same order.
caption.zh: 有資料的照實寫，候選的兩個都列，空著的就留白。讀自己的盤也照這個順序。

caveat.en: Both lines are about the same placement, Saturn in the tenth house. Only the wording differs, and the second one lets you find the answer yourself.
caveat.zh: 兩句講的是同一個位置：土星在第十宮。差別只在說法，第二句讓你自己去找答案。

label.en: Two ways of saying the same thing

lines.en: Announcing an outcome for you: “Saturn is in your tenth, so your career will be delayed.”
lines.zh: 替你宣布結果的寫法：「土星在你第十宮，所以你的事業會延後。」

lines.en: Asking instead: “Tradition reads the tenth as your public standing — look at what is happening there lately.”
lines.zh: 提問的寫法：「傳統把第十宮看成你在外面的身分；你自己看看那一塊最近在發生什麼。」

lines.en: The difference: the first announces an outcome for you, the second hands the looking back to you.
lines.zh: 差別在於：第一句替你宣布結果，第二句把觀察交還給你。

limitations.en: Astrology is a language for describing yourself, not prediction: nothing here predicts events, years, health, lifespan or money, or decides relationships, work or a partner for you.
limitations.zh: 占星是一套描述自己的語言，不是預測：這裡不預測事件、年份、健康、壽命或錢的結果，也不替你決定感情、工作或伴侶。

limitations.en: The two example lines are not anyone’s chart, including yours.
limitations.zh: 示範的兩句例句不是任何人的盤，也不是你的盤。

claim.en: “The ancients believed a chart was destiny.”
claim.zh: 「古人相信星盤就是命中注定。」

correction.en: In Book I ch. 2 Ptolemy writes plainly that predictions sometimes fail, and that seed, birthplace, rearing and custom all make a difference too.
correction.zh: 托勒密在第一卷第 2 章明寫：預測有時會錯，而且種子、出生地、養育與習俗都會一起造成差別。

claim.en: “The more certain a reading sounds, the more accurate it is.”
claim.zh: 「星盤說得越肯定，就越準。」

correction.en: Sounding certain and being accurate are different things. A good reading gives you a direction and a question to hold up against your own experience: keep what fits, let go of what does not.
correction.zh: 說得肯定和說得準是兩回事。好的讀法給你一個方向和一個問題，讓你拿自己的經驗去對照：對得上的留下，對不上的放掉。

claim.en: “With no scientific evidence, there is no point learning it.”
claim.zh: 「既然沒有科學證據，學這個就沒意義。」

correction.en: It is a descriptive language and a way of observing yourself: it helps you find words for your feelings and the right questions to ask yourself. None of that depends on prediction.
correction.zh: 它是一套描述的語言、一種觀察自己的方法：幫你替感受找到詞，替自己找到該問的問題。這些用處不需要靠預測。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: how would you explain to a friend that this is a tool for describing and observing yourself?
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你會怎麼跟朋友解釋「這套東西是用來描述和觀察自己的」？

objective.en: By the end you will know which limits Ptolemy admitted himself, what astrology is best used for, and how to turn a chart reading into a question you ask yourself.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你會知道托勒密自己承認哪些限制、占星最適合拿來做什麼，以及怎麼把一句星盤說法變成一個問自己的問題。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: this lesson looks at how you use your chart.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：這一堂看的是你怎麼使用星盤。

personalSteps.en: Think of an astrology claim you once believed and ask: where did it come from?
personalSteps.zh: 想一個你以前相信過的星座說法，問問看：它有出處嗎？

personalSteps.en: Then ask: did it announce an outcome for you, or just offer an angle?
personalSteps.zh: 再問：它是替你宣布結果，還是只給你一個角度？

personalSteps.en: Write one line: which decisions do you want to make entirely yourself, with the chart only as a reference?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：哪些事你想完全自己決定，只把星盤當成參考？

reason.en: The bodies never return to the same positions within human experience, so no two examples match.
reason.zh: 天體和地球不會在人能經歷的時間裡回到一模一樣的位置，所以沒有完全相同的例子可比。

text.en: They sometimes fail, because the examples compared are never the same
text.zh: 有時會錯，因為拿來比的例子彼此都不一樣

reason.en: The book says predictions sometimes fail.
reason.zh: 書裡寫的是：預測有時會錯。

text.en: Predictions never fail
text.zh: 預測從來不會錯

reason.en: The reason the book gives is that the examples compared differ.
reason.zh: 書裡給的理由是：拿來比的例子彼此不一樣。

text.en: They fail when the astrologer lacks piety
text.zh: 會錯是因為占星師不夠虔誠

prompt.en: What does Ptolemy say in Book I ch. 2 about predictions failing?
prompt.zh: 托勒密在第一卷第 2 章怎麼說預測會錯？

reason.en: The book says leaving these out leads to much difficulty.
reason.zh: 書裡說不把這些一起考慮，就會遇到很大的困難。

text.en: Differences of seed, place of birth, and rearing and custom
text.zh: 種子的差異、出生地點，還有養育與習俗

reason.en: The book says seed, birthplace, rearing and custom make a difference too.
reason.zh: 書裡說種子、出生地、養育與習俗也會造成差別。

text.en: Nothing; the sky is the only cause
text.zh: 沒有，天上是唯一原因

reason.en: The book lists three kinds: seed, place of birth, and rearing and custom.
reason.zh: 書裡列了三類：種子、出生地點，還有養育與習俗。

text.en: Only the place of birth
text.zh: 只有出生地點

prompt.en: Besides the sky, what does the book say makes people different?
prompt.zh: 除了天上，書裡說還有什麼會讓人不一樣？

detail.en: The record page publicly shows the bibliography (Nature 318, 419–425, 1985) and one sentence of purpose: two double-blind tests were made of the thesis that astrological natal charts can be used to describe accurately the personality traits of test subjects. The full text is behind a subscription, so no conclusion of the paper is quoted or paraphrased here.
detail.zh: 記錄頁公開顯示書目（Nature 318 期 419–425 頁，1985）與研究主旨一句：該研究做了兩次雙盲測試，檢驗「出生盤能準確描述受試者人格特質」這個主張。全文需訂閱，本課不引用其結論文字，也不代它下結論。

rights.en: The full text is behind a subscription, so no conclusion of the paper is quoted here — only the bibliographic record and the one sentence of purpose that the record page shows publicly. Copyright rests with the publisher.
rights.zh: 論文全文需訂閱，因此本課不引用其結論文字，只引用記錄頁公開可見的書目與研究主旨一句。著作權屬出版者。

title.en: Shawn Carlson, “A double-blind test of astrology,” Nature vol. 318, pp. 419–425 (1985)
title.zh: Shawn Carlson,「A double-blind test of astrology」，Nature 318 期 419–425 頁（1985）

detail.en: Book I ch. 2 is titled “that knowledge by astronomical means is attainable, and how far” and states that the bodies and the earth do not return to the same positions within human experience, “so that for this reason predictions sometimes fail, because of the disparity of the examples on which they are based”; the same chapter names differences of seed, place of birth, and rearing and custom, and says those who think everything follows from the heavens alone meet much difficulty. Ch. 3 argues the study is beneficial.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 2 章標題為「可知到什麼程度」，內文寫天體與地球不會在人的經驗內回到完全相同位置，「因此預測有時候會失誤，因為所依據的例子彼此並不相同」；同章另列種子差異、出生地點、養育與習俗等因素，並說若不一併考慮，以為一切都能單憑天體運行理解的人會遇到很大困難。第 3 章論這門學問有益。

label.en: Book I ch. 2 (how far knowledge is attainable)
label.zh: 第一卷第 2 章（可知到什麼程度）

label.en: Book I ch. 3 (that it is beneficial)
label.zh: 第一卷第 3 章（是否有益）

rights.en: The Robbins translation is in the public domain, as the University of Chicago LacusCurtius copyright page records. The transcriber's own notes and layout are not cited.
rights.zh: Robbins 英譯本已進入公共領域，芝加哥大學 LacusCurtius 版權說明頁如此記載。轉錄者自己的註解與編排不在引用範圍。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Even Ptolemy wrote that predictions sometimes fail, and that birthplace, upbringing and custom shape a person too. A chart is most useful for giving you words to describe yourself and questions to ask yourself.
summary.zh: 連托勒密都寫過：預測有時會錯，而且一個人也被出生地、養育和習俗塑造。星盤最好用的地方，是給你描述自己的詞，和該問自己的問題。

title.zh: 星象不是預測

kicker.en: The first step is to check what data you have and what is still empty.
kicker.zh: 讀盤第一步，是先清點手上有什麼資料、哪裡還空著。

text.en: Ask yourself: do you have a birth time? If so, the house layer exists; if not, that layer is empty. Then see which bodies are marked “unconfirmed” with two candidates. Seeing this first lets everything you say later rest on data you really have.
text.zh: 先問自己：有沒有出生時間？有的話，宮位那一層才存在；沒有的話，那一層是空的。再看哪幾顆星標了「未確定」、列了兩個候選。先把這些看清楚，後面的描述就能穩穩建立在真的有的資料上。

text.en: This is the step people skip most, and the one that matters most. A lot of “it was inaccurate” comes from reading a layer you do not actually have; checking first avoids that trap.
text.zh: 這一步最常被跳過，卻最影響結果。很多「算得不準」的感覺，來自讀了一層手上其實沒有的資料；先清點，就能避開這個坑。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 13 of the Tetrabiblos, on the quality of the soul, Ptolemy says its impulses vary so much that it cannot be judged simply or offhand, only by many complicated observations together. The old text itself asks for many observations and a careful judgement.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第三卷第 13 章談人的心性時說，心裡的衝動變化很多，所以不能用簡單、隨便的方式判斷，要靠許多複雜的觀察一起進行。古書自己就主張多方觀察、慢慢判斷。

kicker.en: One line each for Sun, Moon and Ascendant: which body, what manner, which area.
kicker.zh: 太陽、月亮、上升各寫一句：哪一顆、什麼方式、哪個場景。

text.en: The steadiest order for a line is: which body, then in what manner, then in which area of life. With no birth time, skip that last part. One line each for Sun, Moon and Ascendant is enough.
text.zh: 照這個順序寫一句話最穩：先說哪一顆星，再說它用什麼方式，最後說在哪個生活場景。沒有出生時間，就跳過最後那一段。太陽、月亮、上升各寫一句就夠了。

text.en: Astrology today usually splits the work like this: the planet is the subject, the sign is the adjective, the house is the setting.
text.zh: 現在的占星常這樣分工：行星是主詞，星座是形容詞，宮位是場景。

text.en: Once you have three lines, leave them side by side. They describe three layers, and side by side is where they are clearest.
text.zh: 寫完三句，就讓三句並排放著。三句話講的是三個層次，並排看最清楚。

text.en: What the old texts say: judgement in the book always starts from a body: where it is and what it is connected to — for example Mercury and the Moon in Book III ch. 13, or Mars, Venus and Mercury in Book IV ch. 4.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：書裡判斷一向從星體出發，看某顆星在哪裡、跟哪些星有關係。例如第三卷第 13 章看水星和月亮，第四卷第 4 章看火星、金星、水星。

kicker.en: Where the three lines don’t match is what is most worth writing down.
kicker.zh: 三句話對不上的地方，才是最值得寫下來的。

text.en: The usual reading: the Sun is the direction you want to be seen in, the Moon is the safety you need, and the Ascendant is the first impression you give.
text.zh: 常見的說法是：太陽是你想被看見的方向，月亮是你需要的安全感，上升是別人對你的第一印象。

text.en: With three lines written, ask three questions. Does the way the Sun wants to be seen point the same way as the safety the Moon needs? Does the Ascendant’s impression match the Sun? In the tightest aspect in the chart, do the two forces work together or take turns? The mismatches are usually more worth writing down than the matches.
text.zh: 三句寫完，問自己三個問題：太陽想被看見的方向，跟月亮要的安全感同方向嗎？上升給人的印象，跟太陽一致嗎？盤上最緊的那個相位，連起來的兩股力氣是合作，還是輪流出場？對不上的地方，通常比對得上的地方更值得寫下來。

text.en: That is one full pass: data, three lines, gaps. The same order works on any question: work, relationships, a stretch of moods. Come back in a few months, reread the three lines, and see which one fits you best now and which you want to change. The sentence about who you are is yours to write, and you can change it any time.
text.zh: 到這裡你已經走完一輪：資料、三句、落差。同樣的順序可以用在任何題目上：工作、關係、一段時間的心情。過幾個月回來重讀這三句，看看哪一句現在最像你、哪一句想改。描述「你是什麼樣的人」的那一句話，由你自己來寫，而且隨時可以改。

text.en: What the old texts say: the book handles the relation between two places through aspects (Book I chs. 13 and 24); the relation itself is material for judgement.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：書裡用相位來處理「兩個位置之間的關係」（第一卷第 13 章、第 24 章），關係本身就是判斷的材料。

alt.en: Diagram: an outer ring labelled Sun, an inner ring labelled Moon, and a point at the bottom labelled Ascendant, stacked on one vertical line to show three different layers rather than real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：外圈標示太陽，中圈標示月亮，底部標示上升 ASC，三者排在同一條垂直線上，代表三個不同層次的位置，不是真實度數。

caption.en: Back to lesson one's picture: three layers, one line each.
caption.zh: 回到第一堂那張圖：三個層次，各寫一句。

caveat.en: These are fixed demonstration placements. When the Moon has two candidates, put both in the line, as the second line does.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置。月亮有兩個候選時，兩個都寫進句子裡，像第二行那樣。

lines.en: Check: birth time known, so houses exist; the Moon is unconfirmed, with two candidates.
lines.zh: 清點：有出生時間，所以有宮位；月亮未確定，有兩個候選。

lines.en: Three lines: Sun in Libra, seventh house; Moon in Aries or Taurus; Ascendant Capricorn.
lines.zh: 三句：太陽在天秤、第七宮；月亮在牡羊或金牛；上升摩羯。

lines.en: The gap: steady and formal on the outside, quick to react inside — that gap is what there is to write about.
lines.zh: 落差：對外穩重正式，情緒卻來得很快——這個落差就是可以寫的東西。

limitations.en: Without a birth time the house layer does not exist, so skip it when reading.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，宮位那一層不存在，讀盤時就跳過它。

limitations.en: Astrology is a language for describing yourself: reading a chart gives a few layered lines of description, not a verdict or a prediction.
limitations.zh: 占星是描述自己的語言：讀盤得到的是幾句有層次的描述，不是一句結論或預測。

limitations.en: The demonstration placements are not a real person’s chart.
limitations.zh: 示範位置不是任何真人的盤。

claim.en: “Reading a chart should give you a conclusion.”
claim.zh: 「讀完一張盤，應該得到一個結論。」

correction.en: Book III ch. 13 says this kind of judgement needs many complicated observations together. What a chart gives you is a few layered lines of description.
correction.zh: 古書第三卷第 13 章就說，這種判斷要靠許多複雜的觀察一起進行。讀完一張盤，你得到的是幾句有層次的描述。

claim.en: “Without a birth time this lesson is useless.”
claim.zh: 「沒有出生時間，這一堂就不用學。」

correction.en: The order still works; you just skip the house part. Checking your data and looking at the gaps need no birth time at all.
correction.zh: 順序照樣能用，只是跳過宮位那一段；清點和看落差都不需要出生時間。

claim.en: “If the lines don’t match, something is wrong with me.”
claim.zh: 「三句對不上，代表我有問題。」

correction.en: The three placements describe different layers, so differences are normal. A gap is exactly the material to observe: it often shows how you switch between settings.
correction.zh: 三個位置講的是不同層次，各自不同很正常。落差正好是可以觀察的材料：它常常說出你在不同場合切換的方式。

notePrompt.en: Write your own three lines, then one on the gap. The note stays with this lesson.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下你自己的三句話，再加一句落差。這份筆記會留在這一堂。

objective.en: By the end you can tie the first twenty-three lessons together and read a whole chart, in a fixed order, as a layered description.
objective.zh: 讀完這一堂，你能把前面二十三堂串起來，照固定順序，把一張盤讀成一段有層次的描述。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: this time, actually write the three lines.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：這一堂請真的把三句話寫出來。

personalSteps.en: Check first: do you have a birth time, and which bodies are unconfirmed?
personalSteps.zh: 先清點：有沒有出生時間、哪幾顆星未確定。

personalSteps.en: Write one line each for Sun, Moon and Ascendant, in the order which body, what manner, which area.
personalSteps.zh: 太陽、月亮、上升各寫一句，照「哪一顆、什麼方式、哪個場景」的順序。

personalSteps.en: Then one line on the gap: which two lines sound least like the same person?
personalSteps.zh: 最後寫一句落差：哪兩句最不像同一個人？

reason.en: Seeing the empty parts first lets your description rest on data you really have.
reason.zh: 先看見空的地方，後面的描述就能建立在真的有的資料上。

text.en: Check what data you have and which layer is empty
text.zh: 清點有什麼資料、哪一層是空的

reason.en: The first step is the check; the Sun sign is only one layer.
reason.zh: 第一步是清點；太陽星座只是其中一層。

text.en: Start with the Sun sign’s personality description
text.zh: 先看太陽星座的性格描述

reason.en: Aspects come third; first you need to know which placements exist.
reason.zh: 相位是第三步，要先知道有哪些位置可以比。

text.en: Start with the tightest aspect
text.zh: 先找最緊的相位

prompt.en: What is the first step in reading a chart?
prompt.zh: 讀一張盤，第一步是什麼？

reason.en: The planet is the subject, the sign the adjective, the house the setting; skip the last part without a time.
reason.zh: 行星是主詞、星座是形容詞、宮位是場景；沒有時間就跳過最後一段。

text.en: Which body, what manner, which area of life
text.zh: 哪一顆、什麼方式、哪個場景

reason.en: The planet is the subject and the sign the adjective, so the planet comes first.
reason.zh: 句子的主詞是行星，星座是形容詞，所以先寫行星。

text.en: Sign, planet, aspect
text.zh: 星座、行星、相位

reason.en: The order is to observe first and describe after; the old text also asks for many observations together.
reason.zh: 順序是先觀察再描述，古書也主張靠許多觀察一起判斷。

text.en: Decide the conclusion, then look for support
text.zh: 先下結論，再找證據

prompt.en: What is the steadiest order for one line of description?
prompt.zh: 寫一句描述，最穩的順序是什麼？

detail.en: Book III ch. 13 says the impulses of the soul vary greatly, that such inquiry cannot be made simply or offhand but by many complicated observations, and reads Mercury and the Moon for it; Book IV ch. 4 reads Mars, Venus and Mercury for the quality of action, showing that judgment starts from bodies rather than signs; and Book I chs. 13 and 24 give the handling of a relation between two places. The order inventory, three lines, gaps is this lesson's arrangement, not the text's structure.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 13 章說靈魂的衝動變化很多，這類探討不能用簡單或隨便的方式，要靠許多複雜的觀察一起進行，並以水星與月亮為判斷依據；第四卷第 4 章以火星、金星、水星判斷行動性質，顯示原文的判斷從星體出發而非從星座出發；第一卷第 13、24 章提供兩個位置之間關係的處理方式。「清點、三句、落差」這個閱讀順序是本課的編排，不是原文結構。

label.zh: 第一卷第 13 章（星座的相位）
第一卷第 24 章（趨近與分離）

label.en: Book III ch. 13 (quality of the soul)
label.zh: 第三卷第 13 章（靈魂的性質）

label.en: Book IV ch. 4 (the quality of action)
label.zh: 第四卷第 4 章（行動的性質）

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Read a chart in order: first what data you have, then three key lines, then where they disagree.
summary.zh: 讀盤照順序來：先看有什麼資料，再寫三句重點，最後看哪裡不一樣。

title.en: Reading a Whole Chart as a Person
title.zh: 把一張盤讀成一個人

kicker.en: Date, time, place and time zone each change your chart.
kicker.zh: 日期、時間、地點、時區，每一格都會改變你的盤。

text.en: The date fixes which sign the Sun and most planets are in. The time fixes the Ascendant, the Midheaven and the twelve houses; fill it in and that layer appears. The place plus the time zone fix what the clock said where you were at that moment.
text.zh: 日期決定太陽和大部分行星落在哪個星座。時間決定上升、天頂和十二宮；填了時間，這一層才會出現。地點加上時區，決定「那一刻在你那裡是幾點」。

text.en: One time zone out moves the whole chart an hour earlier or later. So a wrong time zone matters as much as a wrong birth time.
text.zh: 差一個時區，就等於整張盤往前或往後挪一小時。所以時區填錯，影響跟出生時間填錯一樣大。

text.en: This app’s city search brings the time zone with it, which is safer than typing one in yourself.
text.zh: 這個 App 的城市搜尋會把時區一起帶出來，用搜尋比自己手填安全。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy takes the degree rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth as the chart’s starting point, so both the moment and the place are needed.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 2 章，用出生那一刻東方地平線上的度數當整張盤的起點，所以出生的時刻和地點都少不了。

heading.en: Three checks once it is set up

kicker.en: Once the chart is set up, check your typing, the blanks and the candidates, then start reading.
kicker.zh: 建好盤後，先檢查打字、空格和候選，再開始讀。

text.en: Once the chart exists, check three things. First, go back over the date, time and place you typed. Second, look at the Ascendant row. Third, see whether any body is marked “unconfirmed” with two candidates.
text.zh: 建好盤之後，檢查三件事：第一，回頭對一次你輸入的日期、時間、地點有沒有打錯。第二，看上升那一行。第三，看有沒有星標了「未確定」、列出兩個候選。

text.en: If you entered no time, the Ascendant row stays empty, which is exactly the correct result. A body marked “unconfirmed” changed sign on the day you were born. You can edit your data in settings at any time, and the whole chart is worked out again.
text.zh: 如果你沒填時間，上升那一行會留空，這正是正確的結果。標了「未確定」的星，表示它在你出生那天換過星座。資料隨時可以回設定頁改，改完整張盤會重新算。

text.en: The two most common typing slips are mixing up morning and afternoon (2:30 and 14:30 are twelve hours apart) and swapping month and day (4 March entered as 3 April). With those three checked, your chart is solid material to work with.
text.zh: 最常見的打錯有兩種：上午下午搞反（2:30 和 14:30 差了十二小時），還有月和日對調（3 月 4 日打成 4 月 3 日）。這三件事確認過，你手上的盤就是可靠的材料。

alt.en: Diagram: a double ring. The outer ring is divided into twelve parts for the signs, the inner ring stands for the houses, and a horizontal line on the left is labelled ASC, the starting point. A concept figure with no real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個雙層圓環，外圈分成十二等分代表十二星座，內圈代表十二宮，左側有一條水平線標著 ASC，代表起算點。概念圖，沒有真實度數。

caption.en: The time you enter sets the starting point on the left, and with it the twelve houses on the inner ring.
caption.zh: 你輸入的時間決定左邊的起算點，也決定內圈的十二宮。

caveat.en: Fixed demonstration data: same day, same place, changing only the time or the time zone shows what each field does.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範資料：同一天、同一個地點，只改時間或時區，就看得出每一格的作用。

lines.en: Enter 1990-03-21, Taipei, time unknown: the Sun is Pisces or Aries, two candidates.
lines.zh: 輸入 1990-03-21、台北、不知道時間：太陽在雙魚或牡羊，有兩個候選。

lines.en: Add 14:30 to the same day: the Sun settles on one sign, and the Ascendant and houses appear.
lines.zh: 同一天補上 14:30：太陽確定是一個，上升和宮位也一起出現。

lines.en: Set the time zone to Tokyo by mistake and the chart moves an hour; the Ascendant may change sign.
lines.zh: 如果時區不小心填成東京，整張盤往前挪一小時，上升可能換一個星座。

limitations.en: Without a birth time the Ascendant, Midheaven and houses stay empty until you add a time.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間，上升、天頂和十二宮會空著，等你補上時間才會出現。

limitations.en: The name is not used in any calculation, and you do not type the time zone yourself.
limitations.zh: 姓名不參與任何計算；時區不需要你手填。

limitations.en: The demonstration data is not a real person and not a model answer.
limitations.zh: 示範資料不是真人，也不是標準答案。

claim.en: “The time zone hardly matters — it is the same day either way.”
claim.zh: 「時區不重要，反正是同一天。」

correction.en: One zone out is an hour out. The Ascendant changes sign roughly every two hours, and the whole set of houses moves with it.
correction.zh: 差一個時區就差一小時。上升平均每兩小時換一個星座，宮位會整組跟著移。

claim.en: “An empty Ascendant row means the app is broken.”
claim.zh: 「上升那一行是空的，代表 App 壞了。」

correction.en: With no birth time, empty is the correct result; once you add a time, the Ascendant and houses appear.
correction.zh: 沒填出生時間時，空的就是正確結果；等你補上時間，上升和宮位就會出現。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: which piece of your data were you least sure of, and how did you check it?
notePrompt.zh: 記下來：建盤時你最不確定的是哪一項資料？後來怎麼確認的？

objective.en: By the end your own chart is set up in this app, and you know what each field you filled in actually changes.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你的盤就建好在這個 App 裡，而且你知道每個欄位會影響什麼。

personalIntro.en: Now actually do it: set up or check your own chart.
personalIntro.zh: 現在真的動手做一次：建好或檢查你自己的盤。

personalSteps.en: In settings, confirm your birth date, time, place and time zone.
personalSteps.zh: 到設定頁，確認你的出生日期、時間、地點和時區。

personalSteps.en: Back on the chart page, check the Ascendant row: filled if it should be, empty if it should be.
personalSteps.zh: 回到命盤頁，確認上升那一行：該有值就有值，該空就空。

personalSteps.en: Note which bodies are marked “unconfirmed”; later lessons use this.
personalSteps.zh: 記下哪幾顆星標了「未確定」，後面幾堂會用到。

reason.en: The chart starts from the degree rising in the east at that moment.
reason.zh: 盤的起點，是出生那一刻東方地平線上的度數。

text.en: The birth time, together with place and time zone
text.zh: 出生時間（再加上地點和時區）

reason.en: The date fixes the Sun and most planets’ signs; the houses come from the time.
reason.zh: 日期決定的是太陽和大部分行星的星座；宮位要靠時間。

text.en: The birth date
text.zh: 出生日期

reason.en: The name is only for display; the calculation uses date, time, place and time zone.
reason.zh: 姓名只用來顯示；計算用的是日期、時間、地點和時區。

text.en: Your name
text.zh: 姓名

prompt.en: Which field fixes the Ascendant and the twelve houses?
prompt.zh: 哪個欄位決定上升和十二宮？

reason.en: A city’s time-zone rules can change over the years, so the date is part of the answer.
reason.zh: 同一個城市在不同年代，時區規則可能不一樣，所以要連日期一起算。

text.en: The app works out that place’s zone on that date
text.zh: App 依出生地點和出生日期，帶出當時的時區

reason.en: The birth moment needs the birthplace’s zone at the time; your phone’s zone today can be hours off.
reason.zh: 出生時刻要用出生地當時的時區；手機現在的時區可能差好幾小時。

text.en: Your phone’s current time zone
text.zh: 用你手機現在的時區

reason.en: The city search brings the zone in for you, which is the safest way to avoid a mistake.
reason.zh: 時區由城市搜尋自動帶出，這樣最不容易出錯。

text.en: You type it in by hand
text.zh: 你自己手動輸入

prompt.en: Once you pick a city in the search, where does the time zone come from?
prompt.zh: 用城市搜尋選好地點後，時區是怎麼來的？

detail.en: Book III ch. 2 takes the degree rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth as the chart's starting point, so the moment and place are required. The breakdown of what each field affects is this lesson's arrangement, and the city search carrying the time zone is this app's behaviour.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 2 章以出生時刻東方地平線上的度數為整張盤的起算點，因此時刻與地點為必要條件。四個欄位各自影響什麼的整理方式為本課編排；「城市搜尋會一併帶出時區」為本 App 的行為。

label.zh: 第三卷第 2 章（上升度數）
