rights.zh: Robbins 英譯本已進入公共領域，芝加哥大學 LacusCurtius 版權說明頁如此記載。轉錄者自己的註解與編排不在引用範圍。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Task: set up your own chart and find out what each field changes.
summary.zh: 任務：建好自己的盤，弄清楚每個欄位影響什麼。

title.zh: 建立你的第一張盤

kicker.en: Copy down your Sun, Moon and Ascendant exactly as shown, candidates included.
kicker.zh: 先把太陽、月亮、上升原樣抄下來，連候選一起抄。

text.en: Start with the Sun, the Moon and the Ascendant: they are the placements most often used to describe a person, and the steadiest place to begin reading. Find all three and you have the material for three lines.
text.zh: 先找太陽、月亮、上升這三個位置，因為它們最常被拿來描述一個人，也是讀盤最穩的起點。三個都找到，你就有了三句話的材料。

text.en: On the chart page the Sun and the Moon each have a row, with a sign and perhaps a house. The Ascendant has its own row, which shows its sign when you have a birth time.
text.zh: 在命盤頁上，太陽和月亮各占一列，有星座，可能也有宮位；上升自己一行，有出生時間時會顯示它的星座。

text.en: Copy the three down before doing anything else, including any “unconfirmed” mark and both candidates. A candidate is what this chart truly looks like, and worth noting as it is.
text.zh: 先把三個位置抄下來，再做下一步。抄的時候，「未確定」和兩個候選也一起抄。候選就是這張盤真實的樣子，值得照實記下。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book III ch. 12 of the Tetrabiblos, listing parts of the body, Ptolemy gives the Sun sight, the brain and the heart; ch. 13 gives the Moon the sensory, non-rational part; and ch. 2 takes the rising degree as the chart’s starting point.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 12 章列身體部位時，把視覺、腦、心臟歸給太陽；第 13 章把感受的、非理性的部分歸給月亮；第 2 章用上升的度數當整張盤的起點。

kicker.en: The planet is the subject of the sentence; the sign describes it.
kicker.zh: 句子的主角是行星，星座用來形容它。

text.en: Write “my Moon is in Scorpio, so under pressure I go quiet first,” with the planet as the subject. If you have a house, add the area of life; if not, two parts make the whole sentence. “My Moon is in Scorpio” is more accurate than “I am a Scorpio”: a sign describes one body, not the whole person.
text.zh: 寫成「我的月亮在天蠍，所以壓力大時我會先沉默」，讓行星當句子的主角。有宮位的，再加一段場景；沒有宮位的，兩段就是完整的一句。寫「我的月亮在天蠍」，比寫「我是天蠍座的人」更準：星座形容的是某一顆星，不是整個人。

text.en: A common reading: the Moon shows what you need to feel safe, and Scorpio gives it a deep, held-in, watch-first manner, so under pressure it goes quiet first. Keep the sentence shape, change the body or the sign, and you have a different line.
text.zh: 常見的說法是：月亮看你需要什麼才有安全感，天蠍給它的方式是深、收、先觀察，所以壓力大時會先沉默。同樣的句型，換一顆星、換一個星座，就是另一句話。

text.en: Once the three lines are written, keep them separate. Kept apart, the gaps between them stay visible — and the gaps are often the most useful part: a steady-looking Ascendant with a quick-reacting Moon, for instance, is a clue worth noting.
text.zh: 三句寫完，先讓它們各自獨立。分開放著，落差才看得清楚——而落差常常才是最有用的部分：例如上升看起來穩重、月亮卻反應很快，這就是一條值得記下的線索。

text.en: What the old texts say: the book judges a body first and then the sign it is in — for example Book IV ch. 4 reads Mars, Venus and Mercury and the signs they are passing through.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：書裡判斷是先看星體，再看它落在哪個星座。例如第四卷第 4 章看火星、金星、水星，也看它們經過的星座。

alt.en: Diagram: an outer ring labelled Sun, an inner ring labelled Moon, and a point at the bottom labelled Ascendant, stacked on one vertical line to show three different layers rather than real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：外圈標示太陽，中圈標示月亮，底部標示上升 ASC，三者排在同一條垂直線上，代表三個不同層次的位置，不是真實度數。

caption.en: Three placements, three layers, each saying one thing.
caption.zh: 三個位置是三個層次，各說一件事。

caveat.en: These are fixed demonstration placements. The Moon in the second line has two candidates: writing both into the line is the right way.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置。第二句的月亮有兩個候選：兩個都寫進句子裡，就是正確的寫法。

lines.en: Sun in Libra, seventh house: the energy goes into keeping relationships smooth.
lines.zh: 太陽在天秤、第七宮：力氣花在把關係擺平這件事上。

lines.en: Moon in Aries or Taurus (two candidates): how it reacts under pressure is not settled yet, so note both.
lines.zh: 月亮在牡羊或金牛（兩個候選）：壓力下怎麼反應還不確定，兩種都先記著。

lines.en: Ascendant in Capricorn: at first meeting, steady and a bit formal.
lines.zh: 上升在摩羯：第一次見面看起來穩重、有點正式。

limitations.en: Without a birth time the Ascendant row is empty and the Sun and Moon lines are the whole answer; with two candidates, note both.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，上升那一行是空的，太陽和月亮兩句就是完整的答案；有兩個候選時，兩個都記下來。

limitations.en: The demonstration placements are not a real person’s chart.
limitations.zh: 示範位置不是任何真人的盤。

claim.en: “The three lines should sound like the same person.”
claim.zh: 「三句話應該要像同一個人。」

correction.en: The three describe different layers, so differences are normal — and that gap is one of the most useful clues in a chart.
correction.zh: 三個位置講的是不同層次，各自不同很正常；這個落差正好是讀盤最有用的線索。

claim.en: “With two candidates, just pick one to make it easier.”
claim.zh: 「有兩個候選，就先挑一個比較好寫。」

correction.en: Keeping both is the accurate record; if you find your birth time later, it settles on its own.
correction.zh: 兩個都留著，才是照實記錄；以後查到出生時間，自然會只剩一個。

notePrompt.en: Write your three lines here. Later lessons come back and revise them.
notePrompt.zh: 把你的三句話寫在這裡。之後幾堂會回來修改它。

objective.en: By the end you can find your Sun, Moon and Ascendant and write one line for each with the planet as its subject.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你能在自己的盤上找到太陽、月亮、上升，並各寫一句以行星為主角的描述。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: three lines, in this lesson’s note.
personalIntro.zh: 換你的盤：三句話，寫在這一堂的筆記裡。

personalSteps.en: Copy your Sun, Moon and Ascendant, with any “unconfirmed” mark and candidates.
personalSteps.zh: 抄下你的太陽、月亮、上升，「未確定」和候選也一起抄。

personalSteps.en: Write one line each with the planet as the subject and the sign describing it.
personalSteps.zh: 各寫一句，主角是行星，星座用來形容它。

personalSteps.en: No Ascendant? The Sun and Moon lines are the whole answer.
personalSteps.zh: 沒有上升的人，太陽和月亮兩句就是完整的答案。

reason.en: A sign is an adjective; without the planet the sentence has no subject.
reason.zh: 星座是形容詞，少了行星，句子就沒有主角。

text.en: The planet
text.zh: 行星

reason.en: The sign is the adjective that describes the planet’s manner.
reason.zh: 星座是形容詞，用來形容行星的方式。

text.en: The sign
text.zh: 星座

reason.en: A house is the setting, and it appears only with a birth time.
reason.zh: 宮位是場景，有出生時間時才會出現。

text.en: The house
text.zh: 宮位

prompt.en: What should the subject of the sentence be?
prompt.zh: 一句描述的主角應該是什麼？

reason.en: The Ascendant needs a birth time; the Sun and Moon lines use only real data.
reason.zh: 上升要靠出生時間；寫太陽和月亮兩句，用到的全是真的資料。

text.en: Write just the Sun and Moon lines
text.zh: 只寫太陽和月亮兩句

reason.en: Houses need a real birth time; an assumed time produces a whole set of houses nobody can check.
reason.zh: 宮位要用真實的出生時間來算；假設的時間會連帶算出一整組無法查證的宮位。

text.en: Assume you were born at noon and write all three
text.zh: 先當作中午十二點出生，再寫三句

reason.en: Two lines still let you practise; the point is how you write.
reason.zh: 兩句一樣能練，這一堂的重點是怎麼寫。

text.en: Skip the lesson
text.zh: 跳過這一堂

prompt.en: What should you do in this lesson if the Ascendant row is empty?
prompt.zh: 上升那一行是空的，這一堂該怎麼做？

detail.en: Book III ch. 12 gives the Sun sight, the brain and the heart in its list of body parts; ch. 13 gives the Moon the sensory, non-rational part and Mercury the rational; ch. 2 takes the rising degree as the starting point; and Book IV ch. 4 shows judgment starting from a body and its sign. The body-manner-area sentence order is this lesson's arrangement.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 12 章列身體部位時把視覺、腦、心臟歸太陽；第 13 章把感受的、非理性的部分歸月亮、理性歸水星；第 2 章以上升度數為起算點；第四卷第 4 章顯示判斷從星體出發並看其所在星座。「哪一顆、什麼方式、哪個場景」的寫句順序為本課編排。

label.zh: 第三卷第 2 章（上升度數）
第三卷第 12 章（身體部位）

label.zh: 第三卷第 13 章（靈魂的性質）

label.zh: 第四卷第 4 章（行動的性質）

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Task: find the three key placements and write one line for each.
summary.zh: 任務：找到三個重點位置，各寫一句。

title.zh: 找出三大重點位置

kicker.en: Match each body’s sign to the table and count how many land in each group.
kicker.zh: 把每顆星的星座對到表上，數一數每組有幾個。

text.en: Match every body’s sign to the table and count how many fall in each element and each way of moving. For a body marked “unconfirmed” with two candidates, leave it out of the total and note which ones they are; then try each candidate in turn and see whether your conclusion changes — if it does, the spread itself is not settled yet.
text.zh: 把盤上每一顆星的星座對到表上，數出每個元素、每種動靜各有幾個。標了「未確定」、有兩個候選的星，先不算進總數，另外記下是哪幾顆；再把兩個候選各代入一次，看結論會不會因此改變——會的話，代表這個分布本身也還不確定。

text.en: A spread is material to observe, and everyone’s mix is different. Its use is to show whether you keep reaching for the same approach.
text.zh: 分布是一份觀察材料，每個人的組合都不一樣。它的用處，是讓你看出自己是不是一直重複用同一種方式。

text.en: Each grouping has names: the elements are fire, earth, air and water, and the ways of moving are starting, holding and shifting; crossed, they fill a table of twelve. A common reading: fire for action, earth for practical matters, air for thinking and exchange, water for feeling; starting begins things, holding keeps them going, shifting adjusts them.
text.zh: 兩種分法各有名字：元素是火、土、風、水，動靜是開場、守成、轉換，交叉起來剛好排成一張十二格的表。常見的讀法是：火看行動、土看實際、風看思考和交流、水看感受；開場是起頭，守成是撐住，轉換是調整。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 18 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy divides the zodiac into four equilateral triangles (the first through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius); ch. 11 sorts the signs into solstitial, equinoctial, solid and bicorporeal.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 18 章把黃道分成四個等邊三角形（第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手）；第 11 章把星座分成至點、分點、固定、雙體四類。

kicker.en: The smallest group is the one most often misread.
kicker.zh: 最少的那一組，最容易被讀錯。

text.en: Two kinds of overreading are common. One takes the biggest group as an identity: “I’m a fire person.” The other takes a missing group as a flaw: “no water, so I have no empathy.”
text.zh: 常見的讀過頭有兩種：一是把最多的那一組當成身分，像「我是火象的人」；二是把缺的那一組當成缺點，像「我沒有水，所以我沒有同情心」。

text.en: Ten bodies split into four groups often leaves one group at zero or one; that is simply how the arithmetic works out.
text.zh: 十顆星分成四組，本來就常常有一組只有零個或一個，這是算術上很自然的結果。

text.en: More useful questions: does your biggest group make you react too fast in some situations? Is your smallest group the part you have to remind yourself about? Both questions only ask you to observe yourself.
text.zh: 比較有用的問法是：最多的那一組，會不會讓你在某些場合反應太快？最少的那一組，是不是你要刻意提醒自己的部分？這兩個問題，都只需要你觀察自己。

text.en: What the old texts say: the book treats these groupings as material for the rules that come later, used together with other conditions.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：書裡把這些分類當成後面判斷規則的材料，和其他條件放在一起使用。

alt.en: Table of four groups of three: fire is starting Aries, holding Leo, shifting Sagittarius; earth is starting Capricorn, holding Taurus, shifting Virgo; air is starting Libra, holding Aquarius, shifting Gemini; water is starting Cancer, holding Scorpio, shifting Pisces.
alt.zh: 對照表，四組各三個：火是開場牡羊、守成獅子、轉換射手；土是開場摩羯、守成金牛、轉換處女；風是開場天秤、守成水瓶、轉換雙子；水是開場巨蟹、守成天蠍、轉換雙魚。

caption.en: Drop your placements into this table and count. The groupings come from Book I chs. 11 and 18.
caption.zh: 把你的位置填進這張表再數。分組出自第一卷第 11 與第 18 章。

caveat.en: Fixed demonstration numbers: write the biggest group first, then the smallest, and one line of description takes shape.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範數字：先寫最多的一組，再寫最少的一組，一句描述就成形了。

lines.en: Of ten bodies: four air, three fire, two earth, one water.
lines.zh: 十顆星裡：四個風、三個火、兩個土、一個水。

lines.en: By way of moving: five starting, three holding, two shifting.
lines.zh: 動靜上：開場五個、守成三個、轉換兩個。

lines.en: You might write: handles things by talking and thinking, quick to start; the single water is a reminder worth noticing.
lines.zh: 可以這樣寫：習慣用講和想來處理事情，起步快；水只有一個，就把它當成一個值得留意的提醒。

limitations.en: A spread describes the approaches you use most, not a personality score; with a group at zero or one, such as a single water, you still have feelings.
limitations.zh: 分布描述的是你常用的方式，不是個性的分數；某一組是零或一，例如只有一個水，你一樣有感受。

limitations.en: Leave bodies with two candidates out of the total, then try each candidate in turn; each body counts once.
limitations.zh: 有候選的星先不算進總數，再把兩個候選各代入一次；每顆星只算一次。

limitations.en: The demonstration numbers are not a real chart and not a model answer.
limitations.zh: 示範數字不是真人的盤，也不是標準答案。

claim.en: “No water in my chart, so I’m cold.”
claim.zh: 「我沒有水，所以我很冷漠。」

correction.en: Ten bodies across four groups often leaves one at zero or one; that is arithmetic. A spread is a hint for looking at yourself.
correction.zh: 十顆星分四組，有一組是零或一很常見，那是算術。分布是用來觀察自己的提示。

claim.en: “With two candidates, just count one; it’s tidier.”
claim.zh: 「有候選的話，只算一種就好，比較整齊。」

correction.en: Leave it out of the total, then try each candidate in turn, so you know whether that uncertainty would flip your conclusion.
correction.zh: 先不算進總數，再把兩個候選各代入一次，才知道結論會不會因為那個不確定而翻過來。

notePrompt.en: Write down your counts, then one line on what fits you best and one on what fits worst.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下你的分布數字，再各寫一句：你覺得最像你、最不像你的地方。

objective.en: By the end you can count the element and modality spread in your own chart, and explain how to use a spread as a hint for looking at yourself.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你能數出自己盤上的元素和動靜分布，也能說明怎麼把分布當成觀察自己的提示來用。

personalIntro.en: Your turn to count. Leave out bodies with two candidates, then try each candidate in turn.
personalIntro.zh: 換你數自己的。有候選的星先不算進總數，再把兩個候選各代入一次。

personalSteps.en: Match each body’s sign to the table and count the elements.
personalSteps.zh: 把每顆星的星座對到表上，數元素。

personalSteps.en: Then count how many are starting, holding and shifting.
personalSteps.zh: 再數開場、守成、轉換各有幾個。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: where in your life does your biggest group show up most?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：最多的那一組，最常出現在你生活的哪種場合？

reason.en: Ten bodies across four groups often leaves one at zero or one.
reason.zh: 十顆星分四組，常常會有一組是零或一。

text.en: Usually just the result of arithmetic
text.zh: 通常只是算術的結果

reason.en: A spread is a hint for observing how you tend to do things.
reason.zh: 分布是觀察的提示，用來看你習慣怎麼做事。

text.en: You will never have that ability
text.zh: 你一輩子都不會有那種能力

reason.en: Zero is a common, normal result when ten bodies fall into four groups.
reason.zh: 十顆星分四組時，出現零是常見又正常的結果。

text.en: The chart was worked out wrong
text.zh: 盤算錯了

prompt.en: What does it mean when one element group is at zero?
prompt.zh: 盤上某一組元素是零，代表什麼？

reason.en: Leaving it out keeps the total to settled data; trying each candidate afterwards shows the difference.
reason.zh: 先不算進去，總數就全是確定的資料；再把候選各代入一次，就看得出差別。

text.en: Leave it out of the total, and note which bodies they are
text.zh: 先不算進總數，另外記下是哪幾顆

reason.en: Reading a chart means data first and description after, with the data noted as it is.
reason.zh: 讀盤是先看資料、再寫描述，資料要照實記。

text.en: Count the one that feels more like you
text.zh: 挑比較像自己的那一個來算

reason.en: Each body counts once, so the total matches the bodies you have.
reason.zh: 每顆星只算一次，總數才會等於你實際有的星。

text.en: Put both into the same single count
text.zh: 在同一次計算裡兩個都算進去

prompt.en: How should you count a body with two candidate signs?
prompt.zh: 有兩個候選星座的星，數元素分布時該怎麼處理？

detail.en: Book I ch. 11 names the solstitial, equinoctial, solid and bicorporeal signs; ch. 18 divides the zodiac into four equilateral triangles, the first through Aries, Leo and Sagittarius. The element and cardinal/fixed/mutable names and the crossed table are later arrangements, and reading a spread as repeated attention is this lesson's prompt.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 11 章逐一指名至點座、分點座、固定座與雙體座；第 18 章把黃道分成四個等邊三角，第一個通過牡羊、獅子、射手。火土風水與基本／固定／變動的名稱、以及把兩種分法交叉成表，皆為後世整理方式；「分布代表注意力重複用在哪裡」為本課的觀察提示。

label.zh: 第一卷第 11 章（至點、分點、固定、雙體座）
第一卷第 18 章（四個三角）

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Task: count your own element and modality spread.
summary.zh: 任務：數一數自己的元素和動靜分布。

title.zh: 看懂自己的元素分布

kicker.en: The aspect closest to its exact angle is the tightest.
kicker.zh: 離精確角度差最少的那個相位，就是最緊的。

text.en: This app lists each aspect and how many degrees it is from the exact angle. The one with the smallest gap is the closest relation in the chart.
text.zh: 這個 App 會列出每個相位，以及它離精確角度差了幾度。差最少的那一個，就是這張盤裡最接近精確的關係。

text.en: The natal orbs this app uses are 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, and 4 for sextile.
text.zh: 這個 App 用的本命容許度是：合相和對分相 8 度，四分相和三分相 6 度，六分相 4 度。

text.en: So a sextile half a degree off is far tighter than a conjunction seven degrees off.
text.zh: 所以，差 0.5 度的六分相，比差 7 度的合相緊得多。

text.en: “Tight” simply means close to the exact angle. When you read the list, look at the gap figure and read upwards from the smallest; the two or three tightest aspects are the best places to write your first line.
text.zh: 「緊」的意思，就是接近精確的角度。看清單時，先看「差幾度」那個數字，從最小的往上讀；前兩三個最緊的相位，就是最值得先寫一句的地方。

text.en: What the old texts say: in Book I ch. 13 of the Tetrabiblos, Ptolemy gives the four angles (180, 120, 90 and 60 degrees); ch. 24 says that when two places are not far apart, the one in front applies and the other separates.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 13 章給了四個相位的角度（180、120、90、60 度）；第 24 章說兩個位置「相隔不遠」時，前面的趨近、後面的分離。

heading.en: Write from what the two bodies mean

kicker.en: Say what each body is first, then how they get along.
kicker.zh: 先寫兩顆星各自是什麼，再寫它們怎麼相處。

text.en: When you write the line, first say what each body describes (from earlier lessons), then the relation between them. A line built this way has real content and says more than “I have a Mercury–Saturn square.”
text.zh: 寫句子時，先寫兩顆星各自描述什麼（前面幾堂學過），再寫它們之間的關係。這樣寫出來的句子有具體內容，比只寫「我有水土四分相」說得更多。

text.en: For example: “Mercury is how I think and talk, Saturn is how I set limits and demands on myself; they are square, so I often check myself before I speak.” A common reading: a square is like two forces pulling against each other, a trine or sextile like two forces running the same way; a smooth relation is easy to use, while one that needs coordinating is often where you put in the most work and grow the most solid.
text.zh: 例如：「水星是我思考和說話的方式，土星是我給自己設限、要求自己的方式；兩者成四分相，所以我講話前常先自我審查。」常見的說法是：四分相像兩股力氣互相拉扯，三分相和六分相像兩股力氣順著走；順的關係用起來輕鬆，要協調的關係常是你下最多功夫、也練得最紮實的地方。

text.en: To weigh the relation, ask two things: does it run smoothly, and does it take effort to coordinate? Those two questions let you describe the relation concretely. Either answer is a description, neither good nor bad; just hold it up against your recent experience.
text.zh: 評估這段關係時，問兩件事：它順不順？要不要花力氣協調？用這兩個問題，就能把關係描述得很具體。兩種答案都只是描述，沒有好壞之分，拿你最近的經驗去對照就好。

text.en: What the old texts say: the book sorts aspects into harmonious and disharmonious, based on whether the signs joined are of the same kind (Book I chs. 13 and 12).
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：書裡把相位分成和諧與不和諧，根據是連起來的星座是不是同一類（第一卷第 13 章、第 12 章）。

alt.en: Diagram: a circle with a solid chord from the top for the 60-degree sextile and a dashed chord on either side at 56 and 64 degrees, showing this app's 4-degree tolerance, beside a note of the natal and transit orbs. A concept figure, not a real chart.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個圓圈，從頂端畫出一條實線代表 60 度的六分相，兩側各有一條虛線代表 56 度與 64 度，表示本 App 的 4 度容許範圍。旁邊附文字說明本命與行運的容許度數字。概念圖，不是真實星盤。

caption.en: The orb decides whether an aspect counts; the smaller the offset, the closer to exact.
caption.zh: 容許度決定一個相位算不算；偏離越小，就越接近精確。

caveat.en: Fixed demonstration figures. What you compare is the gap from exact, not the size of the orb.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範度數。比的是離精確差幾度，不是容許度大小。

lines.en: Three aspects on the list: a conjunction 6 off, a trine 4 off, a sextile 0.5 off.
lines.zh: 清單上有三個相位：合相差 6 度、三分相差 4 度、六分相差 0.5 度。

lines.en: The sextile is the tightest, even though its orb is the smallest.
lines.zh: 最緊的是那個六分相，雖然它的容許度最小。

lines.en: How to write it: what each body is, then whether the relation runs smoothly.
lines.zh: 寫法：先寫兩顆星各自是什麼，再寫這段關係順不順。

limitations.en: The tightest aspect describes the relation closest to exact; it is a place to start observing and does not decide the theme of your life.
limitations.zh: 最緊的相位描述一段最接近精確的關係；它是觀察的起點，不決定你人生的主軸。

limitations.en: The orb figures are this app’s table: 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, 4 for sextile.
limitations.zh: 容許度的數字是這個 App 用的表：合相和對分相 8 度、四分相和三分相 6 度、六分相 4 度。

limitations.en: The demonstration figures are not a real person’s chart.
limitations.zh: 示範度數不是真人的盤。

claim.en: “More aspects means a more complex, more capable person.”
claim.zh: 「相位越多的人，越複雜、越厲害。」

correction.en: How many aspects you get depends on the orbs used; the count is simply what the settings produce. Each aspect describes a relation between two bodies, and the relation itself is what is worth looking at.
correction.zh: 相位有幾個，取決於容許度設多大；數量只是設定帶出來的結果。每個相位描述的是兩顆星之間的一段關係，值得看的是那段關係本身。

claim.en: “The tightest aspect is the main theme of my life.”
claim.zh: 「最緊的相位，就是我人生的主軸。」

correction.en: Tight means close to exact. The old text judges from many conditions taken together.
correction.zh: 緊代表接近精確。古書的判斷，是把很多條件放在一起看。

notePrompt.en: Write down your tightest aspect, what each body means, and whether it fits you.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下你最緊的相位、那兩顆星各自的意思，以及你覺得像不像。

objective.en: By the end you can find the tightest aspect in your own chart and describe it using what each of the two bodies means.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你能在自己的盤上找到最緊的那個相位，並用兩顆星各自的意思寫出一句描述。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: look at your own aspect list. Aspects need no birth time.
personalIntro.zh: 換你看自己的相位清單。相位不需要出生時間。

personalSteps.en: Find the aspect with the smallest gap from exact.
personalSteps.zh: 找出離精確角度差最少的那個相位。

personalSteps.en: Look back at what each of those two bodies described in earlier lessons.
personalSteps.zh: 回頭查那兩顆星，在前面幾堂各自描述什麼。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: do those two forces work together in you, or take turns?

detail.en: Book I ch. 13 gives the four angles and the basis for harmonious and disharmonious — whether the signs joined are of the same kind, per ch. 12 — and ch. 24 says that when the interval is not great the preceding applies and the following separates, without any orb figure. This app's natal orbs — 8 degrees for conjunction and opposition, 6 for square and trine, 4 for sextile — are a modern conventional table approved by Michael on 2026-09-30.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 13 章給出四個相位的角度與和諧／不和諧的分類依據（連接的星座是否同類，分類見第 12 章）；第 24 章說相隔不遠時前者趨近、後者分離，但未給容許度數字。本 App 的本命容許度（合相與對分相 8 度、四分相與三分相 6 度、六分相 4 度）為現代慣用簡表，2026-09-30 經 Michael 核定。

title.zh: 標出最緊的相位

kicker.en: See which sign is rising, then whether any body sits in the first house.
kicker.zh: 看上升在哪個星座，再看第一宮裡有沒有星。

text.en: When you read the first house, look at two things: which sign the Ascendant is in, and whether any body sits in the first house. Write both as a manner — how you show up in front of others.
text.zh: 讀第一宮時看兩件事：第一，上升落在哪個星座；第二，第一宮裡有沒有星。兩件事都寫成一種「方式」，描述你怎麼出現在別人面前。

text.en: The Ascendant shows how you enter a room: your pace, your bearing, the first feeling people get from you. Aries rising, for example, often comes across as direct and quick to move; Cancer rising as warm, tending the mood first. If a body sits in the first house, a common reading is that its manner shows up in the first impression people get of you as well.
text.zh: 上升看的是你進場的方式：步調、姿態、別人對你的第一個感覺。例如上升牡羊常給人直接、動作快的印象，上升巨蟹常給人親切、先照顧氣氛的印象。第一宮裡如果有星，常見的說法是那顆星的性質也會出現在別人對你的第一印象裡。

text.en: An empty first house is common; it simply means no body happens to fall in that stretch, and has nothing to do with how much presence you have, so you focus on the rising sign.
text.zh: 第一宮是空的很常見，意思只是那一段剛好沒有星落進去，跟存在感強弱無關；這時就專心讀上升的星座。

text.en: What the old texts say: William Lilly’s Christian Astrology of 1647, in “Of the Twelve Houses,” gives the first house life, stature, colour, complexion, form and shape; Ptolemy’s Tetrabiblos, Book III ch. 2, takes the rising degree as the chart’s starting point.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：William Lilly 1647 年的《Christian Astrology》在〈Of the Twelve Houses〉寫，第一宮管生命、身材、膚色、面貌和樣子；托勒密《四書》第三卷第 2 章，用上升的度數當整張盤的起點。

kicker.en: With no birth time, observe first impressions instead.
kicker.zh: 沒有出生時間，就改成觀察第一印象。

text.en: The Ascendant needs an exact birth time. Without one, the Ascendant row on your chart stays empty; observe first impressions instead, which practises the heart of the first house just as well: which side of you people see first.
text.zh: 上升需要確切的出生時間。沒有出生時間時，命盤上的上升那一行會空著；這時改做第一印象的觀察，一樣能練到第一宮的重點：別人最先看到你的哪一面。

text.en: Do this instead: ask two or three people who don’t know you well to describe the first impression you give, write it down, and compare it with the lines for your Sun and Moon. If all three differ, that gap is what this lesson gives you.
text.zh: 改做這件事：請兩三個不太熟的人，說說你給人的第一印象，寫下來，再拿來跟你太陽、月亮的描述比一比。如果三者都不太一樣，那個差距本身就是這一堂的收穫。

text.en: If you find your exact birth time later, come back and compare. Having your observations on record first is what makes the comparison worth anything.
text.zh: 以後如果查到確切的出生時間，再回來這一堂對照。先有觀察紀錄，對照才有意義。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos offers a method for working out the rising degree from the last new or full moon (syzygy) before birth, but it needs the whole set of domicile, exaltation and terms.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第三卷第 2 章提出一個方法，用出生前最近一次的新月或滿月（朔望）推算上升的度數，但要搭配守護、擢升、界這一整套規則。

alt.en: Table: house one is life, stature and form; house two estate, movable goods, money lent, profit and loss; house three brethren and kindred, neighbours, short journeys, letters and rumours; house four fathers, lands and houses, inheritance and the end of a matter. All from Lilly's own text.
alt.zh: 對照表：第一宮是生命、身材與樣貌；第二宮是財產、可移動的財物、借出的錢與損益；第三宮是兄弟姊妹、親族、鄰居、短程往來、書信與消息；第四宮是父親、土地房產、繼承與一件事的結尾。皆為 Lilly 原文項目。

caption.en: What the first house covers: you, your starting point, and the first impression you make.
caption.zh: 第一宮管的事：你本人、你的起點、別人對你的第一印象。

caveat.en: These are fixed demonstration placements, made for practice; this layer exists only with a birth time.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置，專門拿來練習；有出生時間才會有這一層。

lines.en: Capricorn rising, nothing in the first house: enters steadily, a bit formal.
lines.zh: 上升摩羯，第一宮裡沒有星：進場的方式穩重、偏正式。

lines.en: With Mars in the first house, that steadiness gets a forward push, and others feel the pace first.
lines.zh: 如果第一宮裡有火星：那份穩重會多一股往前推的力道，別人會先感覺到速度。

lines.en: Both describe a manner: how you show up in front of others.
lines.zh: 兩種寫的都是「方式」：你怎麼出現在別人面前。

limitations.en: Without a birth time the Ascendant row stays empty; observe first impressions instead, rather than using the Sun or any sign as a stand-in.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，上升那一行會空著；請改做第一印象的觀察，不要用太陽或隨便一個星座代替上升。

limitations.en: The demonstration placements are not a real person’s chart.
limitations.zh: 示範位置不是任何真人的盤。

claim.en: “The Ascendant tells you what someone looks like.”
claim.zh: 「看上升就知道一個人長什麼樣子。」

correction.en: The Ascendant describes how you enter: your pace, your bearing, the first feeling people get. To get a sense of someone’s Ascendant, watching how they walk into an unfamiliar room tells you more than their looks.
correction.zh: 上升描述的是你進場的方式：步調、姿態、別人對你的第一個感覺。想知道一個人的上升，看他怎麼走進一個陌生的場合，比看長相更有用。

claim.en: “No birth time? Just pick an Ascendant to practise with.”
claim.zh: 「沒有出生時間，隨便抓一個上升來練習也沒差。」

correction.en: Observing first impressions instead means every line you write has a basis, which is honest and useful.
correction.zh: 改做第一印象的觀察，記下來的每一句都有根據，誠實又有用。

notePrompt.en: Write down the first impression you give — your words or other people’s — and how far it is from how you see yourself.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下你的第一印象紀錄（自己寫的或別人說的），以及它跟你心裡認同的自己差多少。

objective.en: By the end you can read your own first house — the rising sign and anything in it — and know what to do with this lesson if you have no birth time.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你能讀自己的第一宮：上升在哪個星座、宮裡有沒有星；也知道沒有出生時間時這一堂該怎麼做。

summary.en: Task: read your first house, or observe first impressions instead.
summary.zh: 任務：讀自己的第一宮，或改做第一印象的觀察。

title.zh: 讀自己的第一宮

kicker.en: The Moon changes sign every couple of days, so it often has two candidates — read both.
kicker.zh: 月亮兩天多就換星座，所以常有兩個候選，兩個都要讀。

text.en: The Moon goes round the Earth in about 27.32 days (NASA figure), which works out at a new sign every couple of days. So people without a birth time very often get two candidates.
text.zh: 月亮繞地球一圈大約 27.32 天（依 NASA 數值），換算下來兩天多就換一個星座。所以不知道出生時間的人，很常會拿到兩個候選。

text.en: This time, read both, then see which one is closer to how you actually react.
text.zh: 這一堂請兩個都讀一次，再看哪一個比較像你實際的反應。

text.en: The comparison becomes one observation of your own, ready for your note. Both candidates stay side by side in the chart, so you can check them again whenever something new happens.
text.zh: 比完的結果，就是你自己的一筆觀察紀錄，可以寫進筆記。兩個候選會一直並列在盤上，以後有新的經驗，可以再拿來對一次。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 13 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos gives the feeling, non-rational part of a person to the Moon and the rational part to Mercury, and says such judgements need many observations together.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 13 章，把人身上感受的、非理性的那一塊歸給月亮，理性的那一塊歸給水星，並說這類判斷要很多觀察一起看。

heading.en: Check it against one real moment

kicker.en: Recall how you really reacted first, then read the description.
kicker.zh: 先回想你真的怎麼反應，再去看描述。

text.en: The check starts with something that really happened: recall it first, then compare. Think of the last time you really felt under pressure: was your first move to speak up, go quiet, leave, or busy yourself with something else? Write it down, then see whether the Moon's description matches.
text.zh: 檢查的方法是先回想一件真的發生過的事，再拿來比。想想最近一次你真的覺得有壓力的時候：你第一個反應是講出來、不說話、離開，還是先去忙別的事？寫下來，再看月亮的描述有沒有對上。

text.en: A mismatch is a result too. Maybe you read the wrong candidate, or maybe that reaction comes more from how you were raised than from the chart. Both are honest, and both belong in your note.
text.zh: 對不上也是一種結果。可能是候選看錯了，也可能那個反應更多是從你長大的環境來的。兩種都很誠實，都值得寫進筆記。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos says predictions sometimes fail, and that seed, place of birth, upbringing and custom all make a difference and must be considered too.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 2 章說預測有時會失準，而且種子、出生地、養育和習俗都會一起造成差別，要把這些也一起考慮。

alt.en: Table: the Moon stays in a sign about two days, the Sun about a month, Mars about two months, Jupiter about a year and Saturn about two and a half years. All averages from NASA orbit periods; retrograde motion changes any single pass.
alt.zh: 對照表：月亮一個星座約兩天多，太陽約一個月，火星約兩個月，木星約一年，土星約兩年半。都是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值，逆行會讓實際時間不同。

caption.en: The Moon is the fastest body, which is why two candidates are most common for it.
caption.zh: 月亮是最快的一顆，所以最容易出現兩個候選。

caveat.en: The point is that both candidates are listed, so you read and compare both.
caveat.zh: 重點是兩個候選都列出來，讓你兩個都讀、都比一次。

lines.en: Candidate one, Moon in Aries: under pressure, act and speak first.
lines.zh: 候選一，月亮牡羊：有壓力時先動、先講。

lines.en: Candidate two, Moon in Taurus: under pressure, stop and steady yourself first.
lines.zh: 候選二，月亮金牛：有壓力時先停下來、先穩住。

lines.en: Think of the last time plans changed at short notice: did you phone at once, or sit down and replan?
lines.zh: 回想上次行程臨時被改：你是馬上打電話確認，還是先坐下來重排？

limitations.en: Without a birth time the Moon often has two candidates; the comparison is your own observation, and both candidates stay side by side in the chart.
limitations.zh: 沒有出生時間時，月亮常有兩個候選；比對出來的結果是你自己的觀察，兩個候選都會繼續並列在盤上。

limitations.en: A chart is a language for describing yourself, not a prediction; when a description misses, the reaction may come mainly from upbringing.
limitations.zh: 星盤是用來描述自己的語言，不是預測；描述對不上時，那個反應也可能主要來自成長環境。

claim.en: “With two candidates, just pick the one that feels more like me.”
claim.zh: 「兩個候選，挑比較像的那個當答案就好。」

correction.en: The comparison is one observation of yours; both candidates stay, and more experiences can be checked against them later.
correction.zh: 比完的結果是你的一筆觀察紀錄；兩個候選都繼續留著，之後可以用更多經驗再對照。

claim.en: “The Moon description missed, so astrology is useless.”
claim.zh: 「月亮描述不準，代表占星沒用。」

correction.en: Book I ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos itself says predictions fail and that upbringing and custom make a difference too. A mismatch is a normal result.
correction.zh: 《四書》第一卷第 2 章自己就說預測會失準，養育和習俗也會造成差別；對不上本來就是常見的結果。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: your reaction under pressure, and where it matched or missed the Moon's description.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你有壓力時的反應，跟月亮的描述哪裡對上、哪裡沒對上？

objective.en: By the end you can read your own Moon — its sign, any two candidates, and how far it sits from your Sun — and check it against something that really happened.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你會讀自己的月亮：它在哪個星座、有沒有兩個候選、離太陽多遠，再拿一件真實發生的事來對照。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: write your reaction first, then read the description — not the other way round.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：先寫反應，再看描述，順序不要顛倒。

personalSteps.en: First write down your first move the last time you were under pressure.
personalSteps.zh: 先寫下最近一次有壓力時，你的第一個反應。

personalSteps.en: Then read your Moon sign. If there are two candidates, read both.
personalSteps.zh: 再看你的月亮星座。有兩個候選，就兩個都看。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: what matched, and what did not?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：哪裡對上了，哪裡沒對上？

reason.en: Worked out from NASA's 27.32 days; without a time, the day can straddle two signs.
reason.zh: 用 NASA 的 27.32 天換算出來的；不知道時間，那一天就可能跨兩個星座。

text.en: It changes sign every couple of days
text.zh: 它兩天多就換一個星座

reason.en: The Moon is computed precisely; the reason is that it moves fast.
reason.zh: 月亮算得很準，原因是它走得快。

text.en: Because the Moon is harder to compute
text.zh: 因為月亮比較難算

reason.en: Seen from Earth, the Moon always moves forward in the same direction.
reason.zh: 從地球看，月亮一直往同一個方向前進。

text.en: Because it goes retrograde
text.zh: 因為它會逆行

prompt.en: Why does the Moon most often have two candidates?
prompt.zh: 為什麼月亮最常出現兩個候選？

reason.en: Both candidates are real information, and reading both shows what has nothing to do with the sign.
reason.zh: 兩個候選都是真的資訊，都看過才分得出哪些其實跟星座無關。

text.en: Read both, and write what fits and what does not for each
text.zh: 兩個都讀，各寫下對上和沒對上的地方

reason.en: A feeling is one observation; your birth time is the same as before, so read both.
reason.zh: 感覺是一筆觀察，出生時間還是跟原本一樣，所以兩個都要讀。

text.en: Pick the one that fits better
text.zh: 挑比較像的那個當答案

reason.en: Two candidates are enough to start comparing; many people never find their birth time and still build up observations this way.
reason.zh: 有兩個候選就能開始比對；很多人一直查不到出生時間，照樣能用這個方法累積觀察。

text.en: Wait until you find your exact birth time
text.zh: 等查到確切出生時間再做

prompt.en: If your Moon has two candidate signs, what does this lesson ask you to do?
prompt.zh: 月亮有兩個候選星座時，這一堂要你怎麼做？

detail.en: Book III ch. 13 gives the sensory, non-rational part to the Moon and the rational to Mercury and says such judgments need many complicated observations; Book I ch. 2 says predictions sometimes fail and that seed, place of birth, rearing and custom contribute. Writing the reaction before reading the description is this lesson's arrangement.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 13 章把感受的、非理性的部分歸月亮、理性歸水星，並說這類判斷要靠許多複雜的觀察；第一卷第 2 章說預測有時失誤，且種子、出生地、養育與習俗一起造成差別。「先寫反應再看描述」的檢查順序為本課編排。

label.en: Book I ch. 2 (how far knowledge is attainable)
label.zh: 第一卷第 2 章（可知到什麼程度）

label.en: Book III ch. 13 (quality of the soul)
label.zh: 第三卷第 13 章（靈魂的性質）

detail.zh: 公轉週期 27.3217 天。「約兩天多換一個星座」是依此換算，不是原文數值。

title.zh: NASA NSSDCA, Moon Fact Sheet（2024-01-11 更新）

summary.en: Your task: read your Moon, then check it against one real moment of pressure.
summary.zh: 這一堂的任務：讀你的月亮，再用一次真的有壓力的經驗對照看看。

title.zh: 讀自己的月亮位置

kicker.en: Compare one layer at a time, never all mixed together.
kicker.zh: 一層一層比，不要混在一起。

text.en: Compare two charts in the same order you read your own: Sun first, then Moon, then Ascendant. For each layer write only “same” or where they differ, and save any conclusion until all three layers are done.
text.zh: 比兩張盤，順序跟讀自己那張一樣：先比太陽，再比月亮，最後比上升。每一層只寫「一樣」或「哪裡不一樣」，結論留到三層都比完再說。

text.en: The Sun is the direction a person faces outward, the Moon is how they settle themselves, and the Ascendant is how they walk into a room. When you compare, turn the three layers into three questions: where are they heading? How do they settle themselves? How do they walk into a new place?
text.zh: 太陽看一個人對外的方向，月亮看他怎麼讓自己安心，上升看他怎麼走進一個場合。比的時候，把這三層變成三個問題：他往哪裡走？他怎麼讓自己安心？他怎麼走進一個新場合？

text.en: Compare Ascendants only when both people have an exact birth time. If either one is missing it, skip straight past this layer and compare the Sun and Moon, so the whole comparison rests on solid data.
text.zh: 上升要兩邊都有確切的出生時間才比。只要有一邊缺時間，就直接跳過這一層，只比太陽和月亮，讓整個比較都建立在確實的資料上。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 13 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos says the impulses of the soul vary a great deal, so they need many observations together, never a simple or offhand judgement.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 13 章說，人心的衝動變化很多，要很多觀察一起看，不能用簡單或隨便的方法判斷。

kicker.en: Comparing two charts is for saying clearly how two people differ.
kicker.zh: 比兩張盤，是為了把兩個人的差異講清楚。

text.en: When you finish comparing two charts, you hold a list of differences: Sun, Moon and Ascendant, one line each on where the two people are the same and where they differ. A relationship is something two real people live out together, and this list helps you understand each other and start talking more easily.
text.zh: 比完兩張盤，你手上會有一張差異清單：太陽、月亮、上升，每一層一句話，寫兩個人哪裡一樣、哪裡不一樣。一段關係是兩個真人一起過出來的，這張清單的用處，是幫你們更看懂彼此、更好開口聊。

text.en: The useful part of comparing two charts is that it helps you say something specific, like “the way I settle is not the way they settle.” Being able to say the difference is worth far more than a score.
text.zh: 比兩張盤真正有用的地方，是幫你說出很具體的話，像是「我需要的安心方式，跟他不一樣」。把差異講清楚，比知道一個分數有用得多。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book IV ch. 5 of the Tetrabiblos is the marriage chapter, and it opens by looking at the Moon in men's charts and the Sun in wives'.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第四卷第 5 章是談婚姻的章節，開頭說男性的盤看月亮、妻子的盤看太陽。

alt.en: Diagram: an outer ring labelled Sun, an inner ring labelled Moon, and a point at the bottom labelled Ascendant, stacked on one vertical line to show three different layers rather than real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：外圈標示太陽，中圈標示月亮，底部標示上升 ASC，三者排在同一條垂直線上，代表三個不同層次的位置，不是真實度數。

caption.en: Compare two charts by these same three layers, one at a time.
caption.zh: 兩張盤也照這三層比，一層一層來。

caveat.en: Both sets are fixed demonstration placements, made for practising the order of comparison.
caveat.zh: 兩組都是固定的示範位置，專門拿來練習比較的順序。

label.en: Demonstration, neither is a real person

lines.en: Sun: one Libra, one Capricorn — one talks things over first, the other makes a schedule first.
lines.zh: 太陽：一個天秤、一個摩羯——對外一個先聊，一個先排行程。

lines.en: Moon: both in Aries — both react fast under pressure, so they easily blow up together.
lines.zh: 月亮：兩個都在牡羊——有壓力時都反應很快，所以容易一起爆。

lines.en: Ascendant: one side has no birth time, so this layer is skipped and only the Sun and Moon are compared.
lines.zh: 上升：有一邊沒有出生時間，這一層直接跳過，只比太陽和月亮。

limitations.en: Comparing two charts is a language for describing how two people differ, not a prediction; whether they get on, or stay together, shows in their life.
limitations.zh: 比兩張盤是描述兩個人差異的語言，不是預測；兩個人合不合、會不會在一起，要在生活裡看。

limitations.en: When one side has no birth time, that chart has no Ascendant, and a rough guess or noon should not fill it in; skip that layer and compare the Sun and Moon.
limitations.zh: 有一邊沒有出生時間時，那張盤就沒有上升，也不要用「大概幾點」或中午來補；比較時跳過這一層，只比太陽和月亮。

limitations.en: The two demonstration sets are not real people and use no real birth data.
limitations.zh: 示範的兩組位置都不是真人，也沒有用任何真的出生資料。

claim.en: “A compatibility table shows whether two people fit.”
claim.zh: 「星座配對表可以看出兩個人合不合。」

correction.en: Comparing charts is for saying the difference clearly, such as how each person settles themselves; how well two people get on shows in their life together.
correction.zh: 比兩張盤是為了把差異講清楚，像是兩個人各自怎麼讓自己安心；相處合不合，要靠兩個人自己在生活裡看。

claim.en: “They don't remember the hour, but a rough guess is good enough for the Ascendant.”
claim.zh: 「對方不記得幾點出生，抓個大概就能比上升。」

correction.en: The Ascendant changes sign about every two hours on average, so it needs an exact time to be right. Without one, just skip that layer.
correction.zh: 上升平均每兩小時就換一個星座，要有確切的時間才算得準。沒有時間，就直接跳過這一層。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: the three differences you found, and which one shows up most in daily life.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你比出來的三個差異，哪一個最常在生活裡出現？

objective.en: By the end you can compare two charts in one fixed order, and you will know why saying the differences clearly is more useful than a compatibility score.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你會用同一套順序比較兩張盤，也會知道為什麼把差異講清楚，比一個配對分數更有用。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: use the data of someone who has agreed, or practise on the demonstration placements.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：找一個願意讓你用他資料的人，或拿示範盤來練。

personalSteps.en: Ask before using anyone's birth data, and enter a time only when it is certain.
personalSteps.zh: 用對方的出生資料前先問過他；時間確定，才寫進去。

personalSteps.en: Compare Sun, Moon and Ascendant one layer at a time, one line of difference each.
personalSteps.zh: 太陽、月亮、上升一層一層比，每層寫一句差在哪。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: which layer's difference really shows up between you most often?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：哪一層的差異，最常在你們之間真的出現？

reason.en: The Ascendant and houses come from the birth time; skipping them keeps the comparison to solid data.
reason.zh: 上升和宮位要靠出生時間算；跳過它，比較就只用確實的資料。

text.en: Skip the Ascendant and house layer
text.zh: 跳過上升和宮位那一層

reason.en: Noon is only a guessed time; the Ascendant needs the exact birth time, so skip this layer.
reason.zh: 中午只是一個猜的時間；上升要用確切的出生時間，所以請跳過這一層。

text.en: Work one out from noon
text.zh: 用中午來推一個

reason.en: Sun, Moon and aspects can still be compared; only one layer is missing.
reason.zh: 太陽、月亮和相位都還能比，只是少了一層。

text.en: Give up on the whole comparison
text.zh: 整個比較都不要做

prompt.en: When comparing two charts, what do you do if one side has no birth time?
prompt.zh: 比兩張盤時，有一邊沒有出生時間，該怎麼辦？

reason.en: A line like “we settle ourselves in different ways” can be used straight away in daily life.
reason.zh: 像「我們讓自己安心的方式不一樣」這種話，能直接用在相處上。

text.en: Differences give you something specific to talk about together
text.zh: 差異說得出具體的話，可以拿來跟對方聊

reason.en: A score is easy to remember, but it cannot say how two people differ, so it gives you nothing to adjust.
reason.zh: 分數很好記，但說不出兩個人哪裡不一樣，也就沒辦法拿來調整相處。

text.en: Because a score is harder to remember
text.zh: 因為分數比較難記

reason.en: Differences describe two people's tendencies; how well they get on is lived out in their life together.
reason.zh: 差異描述的是兩個人的傾向；相處得好不好，要靠兩個人在生活裡過出來。

text.en: Because differences predict whether two people will split up
text.zh: 因為差異能預測兩個人會不會分開

prompt.en: When comparing two charts, why is writing down the differences more useful than a score?
prompt.zh: 比兩張盤時，為什麼寫下差異比給一個分數有用？

detail.en: Book III ch. 13 says the impulses of the soul vary greatly and such inquiry needs many complicated observations rather than a simple approach; Book IV ch. 5 opens by observing the Moon in men's charts and the Sun in wives', and only that fact is cited, with the chapter's framing of gender and marriage not carried over. The layer-by-layer order is this lesson's arrangement, and scoring no match is this app's choice, with the reason stated.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 13 章說靈魂的衝動變化很多，這類探討不能用簡單方式、要靠許多複雜的觀察；第四卷第 5 章〈婚姻〉開頭說男性看月亮、妻子看太陽，本課只引用這個事實，完全不沿用該章的性別與婚姻框架。逐層比較的順序為本課編排；不做配對評分是本 App 的選擇，已說明理由。

label.zh: 第三卷第 13 章（靈魂的性質）

summary.en: Your task: compare two charts in one order, and write down only where they differ.
summary.zh: 這一堂的任務：照同一套順序比兩張盤，只寫差在哪裡。

title.zh: 比較兩張盤

heading.en: How far it can be read

kicker.en: Split the chart into three columns: settled, candidates, absent.
kicker.zh: 把盤分成三欄：確定、候選、沒有。

text.en: Settled: the Sun and the slow planets usually sit here. Candidates: the Moon most often, and the fast planets on a day they change sign. Absent: the Ascendant, the Midheaven, the twelve houses, and every judgement that needs a house.
text.zh: 確定欄：太陽和走得慢的行星，通常都在這裡。候選欄：最常出現的是月亮，走得快的行星在剛好換星座的那天也會。沒有欄：上升、天頂、十二宮，還有所有要用到宮位的判斷。

text.en: With those three columns written, you hold an honest list of what you have. From then on, read any description using only the first two columns, so every line you read rests on real data.
text.zh: 寫完這三欄，你手上就有一份老實的材料清單。之後讀任何描述，都只用前兩欄的東西，讀到的每一句，就都有真的資料撐著。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 2 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos takes the rising degree as the starting point, and admits the moment of birth is often unreliable — sundials shift and water clocks get stuck.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 2 章把上升的度數當成起算點，也承認出生時刻常常不可靠——日晷會偏，水鐘會卡住。

heading.en: What the demonstration chart is for

kicker.en: The demonstration chart is clearly marked as a demo: a teaching picture for understanding the structure.
kicker.zh: 示範盤會清楚標明「示範」，是一張用來看懂結構的教學圖。

text.en: With no birth time, the personal section still lists your own Sun and Moon, with both candidates when one changed sign on your birthday; only the Ascendant row uses a position marked as a demonstration, so you can see what an Ascendant looks like. The demonstration value stays in that row, and your data holds only your own placements.
text.zh: 沒有出生時間時，個人觀察那一段仍會列出你自己的太陽和月亮，出生那天剛好換星座的，兩個候選都會列出來；只有上升那一格，會改用一個標明「示範」的位置，讓你看懂上升長什麼樣子。示範的數值只留在那一格，你的資料裡只放你自己的位置。

text.en: So read that row as a teaching picture. Use it to understand where the Ascendant sits, then go back to your own first two columns to observe.
text.zh: 所以讀到示範那一格時，把它當成一張教學用的圖。正確的用法是：先看示範理解上升的位置，再回到你自己的前兩欄去觀察。

text.en: If one day you find your birth time, the house layer really appears, and you can read your own houses directly.
text.zh: 哪天你查到了出生時間，宮位那一層就會真的出現，那時候就能直接讀你自己的宮位。

alt.en: Table: the Sun's sign is present, with two candidates on a changeover day; most planetary signs are present, with candidates for the fast ones on a boundary day; the Moon often has two candidates; aspects are present and need no birth time; the Ascendant is absent, its row empty; and the twelve houses are absent, the whole layer missing.
alt.zh: 對照表：太陽星座有（交界日列兩個候選）；多數行星星座有，走得快的在交界日列候選；月亮常有兩個候選；相位有，不需要出生時間；上升沒有，那一格是空的；十二宮沒有，整層不存在。

caption.en: This is the three-column list: settled, candidates, blank.
caption.zh: 這就是三欄清單：確定、候選、留白。

caveat.en: These are fixed demonstration placements; the list shows the format for you to copy when you write your own.
caveat.zh: 這是固定的示範位置；這份清單是讓你照著學寫法，再寫你自己的。

lines.en: Settled: Sun in Libra, Jupiter in Gemini, Saturn in Capricorn.
lines.zh: 確定：太陽天秤、木星雙子、土星摩羯。

lines.en: Candidates: Moon in Aries or Taurus; Mercury in Libra or Scorpio.
lines.zh: 候選：月亮牡羊或金牛；水星天秤或天蠍。

lines.en: Absent: Ascendant, Midheaven, the twelve houses, and anything that needs a house.
lines.zh: 沒有：上升、天頂、十二宮，以及任何要用到宮位的描述。

limitations.en: Read descriptions from the first two columns only; without a birth time the third column (Ascendant, Midheaven, houses) does not exist, so do not read it in.
limitations.zh: 讀描述時只用前兩欄；第三欄（上升、天頂、十二宮）的內容，沒有出生時間就不存在，不要讀進去。

limitations.en: The demonstration chart is a fixed set of teaching placements, not your chart; its values stay in the demonstration section, so write your own list from your own placements only.
limitations.zh: 示範盤是一組固定的教學位置，不是你的盤；示範數值只留在示範那一段，寫自己的清單時只用你自己的位置。

claim.en: “The demonstration chart is the app's guess at mine.”
claim.zh: 「示範盤就是系統幫我推出來的盤。」

correction.en: The demonstration is a fixed set of teaching placements, and the screen clearly marks it as a demonstration; your chart comes only from your own birth data.
correction.zh: 示範是一組固定的教學位置，畫面上也清楚標明「示範，非真人」；你的盤只來自你自己的出生資料。

claim.en: “Something in the third column means my chart is worse.”
claim.zh: 「第三欄有東西，代表我的盤不完整、比較差。」

correction.en: The third column simply records which piece of data is missing. The first two columns can still be read and are well worth observing.
correction.zh: 第三欄只是記下少了哪一項資料。前兩欄照樣能讀，也照樣值得好好觀察。

notePrompt.en: Write your three columns here; the next lessons keep coming back to them.
notePrompt.zh: 把你的三欄清單寫在這裡，後面幾堂會一直用到。

objective.en: By the end you can read a chart with no birth time as far as it goes, and write an honest list: what is settled, what has two candidates, and what simply is not there.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你會把一張沒有出生時間的盤讀到它能讀的最遠，並寫出一份老實的清單：哪些確定、哪些有兩個候選、哪些根本沒有。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: write your own three columns. It works with a birth time too — the third column will just be empty.
personalIntro.zh: 換你寫自己的三欄清單。有出生時間的人也能做，只是第三欄會是空的。

personalSteps.en: Write down the settled placements.
personalSteps.zh: 寫下確定的位置。

personalSteps.en: Write down the ones with two candidates, both of them.
personalSteps.zh: 寫下有兩個候選的位置，兩個都寫。

personalSteps.en: Write down the absent layer, and one line on how you will handle it.
personalSteps.zh: 寫下沒有的那一層，再寫一句你打算怎麼處理它。

reason.en: They depend on the Earth's turning, so without a moment there is no starting point.
reason.zh: 它們靠的是地球自轉的角度，沒有時刻就沒有起算點。

text.en: The Ascendant, Midheaven and twelve houses
text.zh: 上升、天頂和十二宮那一層

reason.en: Aspects need no birth time.
reason.zh: 相位不需要出生時間。

text.en: The aspects
text.zh: 相位

reason.en: On most days the date settles it; on a changeover day both candidates are listed.
reason.zh: 大多數日子靠生日就能確定，剛好換星座的那天列兩個候選。

text.en: The Sun's sign
text.zh: 太陽星座

prompt.en: With no birth time, which layer is always empty?
prompt.zh: 沒有出生時間時，哪一層一定是空的？

reason.en: Naming the missing layer stops it looking like something you forgot to fill in.
reason.zh: 把沒有的那層寫出來，之後才不會誤以為是忘了填。

text.en: The layer this chart does not have, such as the Ascendant and the houses
text.zh: 這張盤沒有的那一層，像是上升和十二宮

reason.en: That is something else; this column is about what data exists.
reason.zh: 那是另一件事；這一欄講的是有沒有資料。

text.en: The questions you most want answered
text.zh: 你最想知道的問題

reason.en: Your list holds only your own placements, so you can always tell which ones are yours.
reason.zh: 自己的清單只寫自己的位置，之後才分得清哪些是你的。

text.en: The demonstration chart's values for it
text.zh: 示範盤上對應的數值

prompt.en: For a chart with no birth time, what goes in the third column?
prompt.zh: 沒有出生時間的盤，三欄清單的第三欄寫什麼？

detail.en: Book III ch. 2 takes the rising degree as the starting point and admits the moment of birth is often unreliable, through a sundial's shifted position or gnomon and a water clock's stoppages or uneven flow. The three-column format and the use of a demonstration chart are this lesson's and this app's doing, not the text's.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 2 章以上升度數為起算點，並承認出生時刻常不可靠（日晷位置或指針偏移、水鐘阻塞或流速不均）。三欄清單的寫法與示範盤的使用方式皆為本課與本 App 的做法，非原文內容。

label.zh: 第三卷第 2 章（上升度數）

rights.en: The Robbins translation is in the public domain, as the University of Chicago LacusCurtius copyright page records. The transcriber's own notes and layout are not cited.
rights.zh: Robbins 英譯本已進入公共領域，芝加哥大學 LacusCurtius 版權說明頁如此記載。轉錄者自己的註解與編排不在引用範圍。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Your task: read a chart with no time as far as it goes, and write it as three columns.
summary.zh: 這一堂的任務：把沒有時間的盤讀到底，寫成三欄清單。

title.zh: 處理沒有出生時間的盤

kicker.en: A transit says which moving body has reached which of your placements.
kicker.zh: 一條行運講的是：哪一顆星，走到你盤上的哪個位置。

text.en: A transit has three parts: the body that is moving, the placement of yours it has reached, and the angle between them. Pull those three apart before you think about meaning; in that order, what you see is a clear relationship between positions.
text.zh: 一條行運有三個部分：正在走的那一顆、你盤上被碰到的那個位置、兩者之間的角度。先把這三個拆出來，再去想意思；照這個順序，你看到的就是一個清清楚楚的位置關係。

text.en: This app works out the day's positions once a day and compares them with your positions at birth. The allowed gap is 1 degree in general and 2 for the Sun and Moon; within 0.1 of a degree counts as “exact.”
text.zh: 本 App 每天算一次當天的位置，拿來跟你出生那一刻的位置比。容許的誤差一般是 1 度，太陽和月亮是 2 度；差在 0.1 度以內就算「正好」。

text.en: What the old texts say: the timing chapter of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos is Book IV ch. 10, the division of times, which splits a life into stretches by rule and reads each stretch in turn.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》講時間的是第四卷第 10 章〈時間的劃分〉，做法是照規則把一生分成幾段來看。

kicker.en: To know how long it lasts, look first at which body is moving.
kicker.zh: 要知道持續多久，先看是哪一顆在走。

text.en: The same angle can last very different lengths of time depending on which body is moving. The Moon is past in a day; the Sun in about two; Mars within 1 degree usually a few days; Jupiter a week or two; Saturn and the planets further out can come and go over months, because retrograde motion brings them back. These are rough figures worked out from NASA orbit periods.
text.zh: 同一個角度，換一顆星在走，長短可以差非常多。月亮一天就過去；太陽大約兩天；火星在 1 度以內通常是幾天；木星可能一兩週；土星和更外面的行星可能來來回回好幾個月，因為逆行會讓它折回來。這些是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的大概值。

text.en: So when you see a transit, first ask who is moving. If it is the Moon, it is today's matter at most.
text.zh: 所以看到一條行運，先問「是誰在走」。如果是月亮，頂多就是今天的事。

text.en: If Saturn is the one moving, it is a theme you have been meeting again and again lately, one that stays for quite a while. Ask yourself: which matter has kept coming back to me these past months?
text.zh: 如果走的是土星，那是你最近這段時間反覆碰到、會持續好一陣子的題目。這時候可以問自己：這幾個月一直回來找我的是哪一件事？

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 2 of the Tetrabiblos says predictions sometimes fail, and that more than the heavens shapes a person.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：《四書》第一卷第 2 章說，預測有時會失準，而且影響一個人的不只有天上。

alt.en: Table: the Moon stays in a sign about two days, the Sun about a month, Mars about two months, Jupiter about a year and Saturn about two and a half years. All averages from NASA orbit periods; retrograde motion changes any single pass.
alt.zh: 對照表：月亮一個星座約兩天多，太陽約一個月，火星約兩個月，木星約一年，土星約兩年半。都是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值，逆行會讓實際時間不同。

caption.en: Which body is moving decides roughly how long a transit lasts. Averages worked out from NASA orbit periods.
caption.zh: 走的是誰，決定一條行運大概持續多久。數字是依 NASA 公轉週期換算的平均值。

caveat.en: This shows how to read a line; your own transits for today are on the today page.
caveat.zh: 這裡示範的是讀法；你自己今天的行運，在今天頁上。

lines.en: “Today's Moon conjunct your Sun”: split it into the Moon, your Sun, and a conjunction.
lines.zh: 「今天的月亮與你的太陽合相」：拆成月亮、你的太陽、合相。

lines.en: The Moon moves on within a day, so this is about today.
lines.zh: 月亮一天就走開，所以這是今天的事。

lines.en: Put Saturn in the same line and you read it over months.
lines.zh: 同一句換成土星，就要用「這幾個月」來看。

limitations.en: The today page's descriptions are a language for checking yourself against, not predictions and not warnings.
limitations.zh: 今天頁的描述是讓你對照自己的語言，不是預測，也不是警告。

limitations.en: The allowed gap (1 degree in general, 2 for the Sun and Moon, exact inside 0.1) is this app's setting; durations are rough figures from orbit periods, and retrograde motion changes any single pass.
limitations.zh: 容許誤差（一般 1 度、太陽和月亮 2 度、0.1 度以內算正好）是本 App 的設定；持續多久是依公轉週期換算的大概值，逆行會讓實際時間不同。

limitations.en: The demonstration shows a method; it is not a real person's chart or your transits today.
limitations.zh: 示範是讀法，不是真人的盤，也不是你今天的行運。

claim.en: “The today page predicts what will happen to me.”
claim.zh: 「今天頁是在預測我今天會遇到什麼。」

correction.en: The today page describes two sets of degrees — the day's and your birth chart's — forming an angle. You can check it against how your day went.
correction.zh: 今天頁描述的是：當天的星和你出生時的星，兩組度數形成了一個角度。你可以拿它來對照今天的經驗。

claim.en: “If I feel nothing, it was worked out wrong.”
claim.zh: 「行運沒感覺，就是算錯了。」

correction.en: The positions really are calculated, but Ptolemy himself says predictions fail and that more than the sky shapes a person. Feeling nothing is a normal result.
correction.zh: 位置是真的算出來的，但托勒密自己也說預測會失準，而且影響人的不只有天上。沒感覺是很正常的結果。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: the transit you picked, roughly how long it lasts, and what you actually noticed.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你挑的那條行運、它大概持續多久，以及你實際的感覺。

objective.en: By the end you will understand how the transits on the today page are worked out, and use which body is moving to tell a matter of days from a matter of months.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你會看懂今天頁上的行運是怎麼算出來的，也會用「是哪一顆在走」判斷這是幾天還是幾個月的事。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: open the today page and pick one transit.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：打開今天頁，挑一條行運。

personalSteps.en: Split it into three: who is moving, which of your placements, which angle.
personalSteps.zh: 把它拆成三部分：誰在走、碰到你哪個位置、什麼角度。

personalSteps.en: Use how fast that body moves to judge whether this is days or months.
personalSteps.zh: 用那顆星走多快，判斷這是幾天還是幾個月的事。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: does the description match what today was really like?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：那段描述跟你今天實際的經驗對得上嗎？

reason.en: The Moon is past in a day; Saturn can come and go over months.
reason.zh: 月亮一天就過去，土星可能來回好幾個月。

text.en: How fast the moving body is
text.zh: 正在走的那顆星有多快

reason.en: How long it lasts is decided by the moving body's speed.
reason.zh: 持續多久由在走那顆的速度決定。

text.en: Which angle it is
text.zh: 是哪一種角度

reason.en: Your placement is the one being reached; how long it lasts depends on the body that is moving.
reason.zh: 你的位置是被碰到的那一端；持續多久，看在走的那一顆。

text.en: Your birth sign
text.zh: 你的出生星座

prompt.en: What mainly decides how long a transit lasts?
prompt.zh: 一條行運會持續多久，主要看什麼？

reason.en: The Moon shifts within a day; an outer planet takes years over the same stretch.
reason.zh: 月亮一天就換位置，外行星同一段要走好幾年，差很多。

text.en: By how fast the moving body is
text.zh: 看在走的那顆星有多快

reason.en: Time comes from the moving body's speed; the tone of the wording is just style.
reason.zh: 時間要看在走那顆的速度；描述的語氣只是寫法。

text.en: By how serious the wording sounds
text.zh: 看那句描述寫得多嚴重

reason.en: How long it lasts comes from the moving body's speed; the list order is just the order shown.
reason.zh: 持續多久看在走那顆的速度；排在第幾條只是列出來的順序。

text.en: By where it sits in today's list
text.zh: 看它排在今天頁的第幾條

prompt.en: How do you judge roughly how long a transit lasts?
prompt.zh: 怎麼判斷一條行運大概持續多久？

detail.en: Book IV ch. 10, the division of times, is the text's timing chapter and divides a life into stretches by rule, unlike modern transits; that chapter also generalises about peoples in its era's terms, which this lesson neither cites nor uses. Book I ch. 2 says predictions sometimes fail and that more than the heavens shapes a person. The transit orbs — 1 degree, 2 for the lights, exact inside 0.1 — and the rough durations are this app's numbers and this lesson's arithmetic.
detail.zh: 第四卷第 10 章〈時間的劃分〉是原文處理時間的章節，做法為依規則劃分一生階段，與現代行運不同；該章另含以族群概括人的敘述，本課未引用、未使用。第一卷第 2 章說預測有時失誤，且不只天象影響人。行運容許度（一般 1 度、日月 2 度、0.1 度為正好）與持續時間粗估皆為本 App 數值與本課換算。

label.en: Book I ch. 2 (how far knowledge is attainable)
label.zh: 第一卷第 2 章（可知到什麼程度）

label.en: Book IV ch. 10 (the division of times)
label.zh: 第四卷第 10 章（時間的劃分）

rights.en: The Robbins translation is in the public domain, as the University of Chicago LacusCurtius copyright page records. The transcriber's own notes and layout are not cited.
rights.zh: Robbins 英譯本已進入公共領域，芝加哥大學 LacusCurtius 版權說明頁如此記載。轉錄者自己的註解與編排不在引用範圍。

title.en: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos, trans. F. E. Robbins (Loeb Classical Library, 1940)
title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Your task: read one transit on the today page and judge how long it lasts.
summary.zh: 這一堂的任務：讀懂今天頁的一條行運，判斷它會持續多久。

title.zh: 今天的行運怎麼看

kicker.en: Writing the summary in four parts keeps your observations whole.
kicker.zh: 摘要分成四段寫，最能把你的觀察完整留下來。

text.en: Part one: what data you have, including the layer that is missing. Part two: one line for each of the three key placements. Part three: the clearest single gap. Part four: which descriptions did not fit you, and your guess at why.
text.zh: 第一段：我手上有哪些資料（包括沒有的那一層）。第二段：三個重點位置，各寫一句。第三段：最明顯的一個落差。第四段：哪些描述我覺得對不上，以及我猜為什麼。

text.en: Part four matters most. Being willing to write down what did not fit is what makes this your own record of observation, every line grown from your own experience.
text.zh: 第四段最重要。願意把對不上的寫下來，這份摘要才會是你自己的觀察紀錄，每一句都從你的經驗裡長出來。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book III ch. 13 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos says such judgements need many observations together, never a simple or offhand approach; Book I ch. 2 also asks that seed, place of birth, upbringing and custom be considered.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第三卷第 13 章說，這類判斷要很多觀察一起看，不能用簡單或隨便的方法；第一卷第 2 章也要求把種子、出生地、養育和習俗一起考慮。

kicker.en: After every line, mark which kind of basis it has.
kicker.zh: 每一句後面，標上它是哪一種根據。

text.en: As you write, mark each line with one of three bases: computed (positions, aspects, degrees); traditional (things with a chapter you can look up); or my own observation (things you have really lived through).
text.zh: 寫摘要時，每一句後面標一種根據，三選一：「算出來的」（星體位置、相位、度數）；「傳統說法」（查得到章節的那些）；「我自己的觀察」（你真的經歷過的事）。

text.en: Once you have marked them, you will notice that the useful lines are mostly the third kind, and the second kind only supplies words. If a line fits none of the three, delete it — it came from somewhere else and you are not actually sure of it.
text.zh: 標完你會發現：真正有用的句子，大多是第三種；第二種只是提供用詞。如果一句話三種都標不上，就刪掉它——那是從別的地方抄來、你自己其實不確定的話。

text.en: What the old texts say: the text explains how a rule was worked out (Book I ch. 17 explains why Leo goes to the Sun, for example), and says which judgements need more conditions.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：原文會說明某條規則是怎麼推出來的（像第一卷第 17 章解釋為什麼獅子座歸太陽），也會說哪些判斷需要更多條件。

alt.en: Diagram: an outer ring labelled Sun, an inner ring labelled Moon, and a point at the bottom labelled Ascendant, stacked on one vertical line to show three different layers rather than real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：外圈標示太陽，中圈標示月亮，底部標示上升 ASC，三者排在同一條垂直線上，代表三個不同層次的位置，不是真實度數。

caption.en: The second part of the summary is these three layers, one line each.
caption.zh: 摘要的第二段就是這三層，各一句。

caveat.en: These three lines show how to mark a basis, in a format you can copy for your own.
caveat.zh: 這三句示範的是怎麼標根據，你可以照這個格式寫自己的。

lines.en: “My Moon has two candidates” — basis: computed.
lines.zh: 「月亮有兩個候選」——根據：算出來的。

lines.en: “The Moon rules the feeling side” — basis: traditional, Book III ch. 13.
lines.zh: 「月亮管感受的那一塊」——根據：傳統說法，第三卷第 13 章。

lines.en: “When plans change, I phone first” — basis: my own observation.
lines.zh: 「行程被改時，我會先打電話」——根據：我自己的觀察。

limitations.en: A summary is a record of describing yourself through the chart, not a verdict or a prediction; every line should lead back to a basis or your own experience.
limitations.zh: 摘要是用星盤描述自己的紀錄，不是定論，也不是預測；每一句都要接得回根據或你自己的經驗。

limitations.en: The three demonstration lines only show the format; they are not anyone's summary.
limitations.zh: 示範的三句只是格式示範，不是真人的摘要。

claim.en: “A summary should be one catchy line.”
claim.zh: 「摘要寫成一句話，比較好記。」

correction.en: Book III ch. 13 of the Tetrabiblos asks for many observations together; writing in parts keeps the gaps and the open questions in view.
correction.zh: 《四書》第三卷第 13 章要求很多觀察一起看；分段寫，才留得住落差和還不確定的地方。

claim.en: “Writing down what did not fit is embarrassing.”
claim.zh: 「把對不上的寫出來，很丟臉。」

correction.en: That part is your own observation. The text itself says predictions sometimes fail and that more than the sky shapes a person.
correction.zh: 那一段才是你自己的觀察。原文自己也說預測有時會失準，而且影響人的不只有天上。

notePrompt.en: Write your four-part summary here, with a basis after each line. It is your own version, and you can change it any time.
notePrompt.zh: 把四段摘要寫在這裡，每句後面標根據。這是你自己的版本，隨時可以改。

objective.en: By the end you can turn your earlier notes into a summary in your own words, and say what each line is based on.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你會把前面的筆記整理成一段自己的摘要，而且每一句都說得出根據。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: write your own. You can bring your earlier notes over and rework them.
personalIntro.zh: 換你寫自己的。可以把前面幾堂的筆記直接搬過來再改。

personalSteps.en: Write the four parts: data, three lines, the gap, and what did not fit.
personalSteps.zh: 照四段寫：資料、三句、落差、對不上的地方。

personalSteps.en: Mark each line: computed, traditional, or my own observation.
personalSteps.zh: 每一句標一種根據：算出來的、傳統說法、我自己的觀察。

personalSteps.en: Delete any line you cannot mark.
personalSteps.zh: 刪掉標不出根據的句子。

reason.en: It usually came from elsewhere and you are not really sure of it.
reason.zh: 那通常是從別處抄來、你自己其實不確定的話。

text.en: Delete it
text.zh: 刪掉它

reason.en: A hunch is fine if marked as your own observation, with the real experience behind it.
reason.zh: 直覺可以寫，但要標成「我自己的觀察」，並寫上真的經歷。

text.en: Keep it as a hunch
text.zh: 留著，當成直覺

reason.en: A basis comes from the three kinds; writing doubt down as it is keeps the summary reliable.
reason.zh: 根據要從三種裡標；把不確定照實寫出來，摘要才可靠。

text.en: Rewrite it to sound more certain
text.zh: 改成比較肯定的語氣

prompt.en: What do you do with a line in your summary that has no basis?
prompt.zh: 摘要裡有一句話標不出任何根據，該怎麼辦？

reason.en: With the basis marked, you can tell later which lines you may revise and which you should not.
reason.zh: 標了根據，以後回來看，才知道哪一句可以改、哪一句不能亂改。

text.en: Its basis: computed, traditional, or your own observation
text.zh: 根據：算出來的、傳統說法，還是自己的觀察

reason.en: Every line carries a basis; many lines come from your own life, and a basis marks them most clearly.
reason.zh: 每句要標的是根據；很多句子來自你自己的經歷，用根據來標最清楚。

text.en: A sign name
text.zh: 一個星座名稱

reason.en: A score cannot say where a line came from; with a basis marked, you know later which lines to revise.
reason.zh: 分數說不出這句話從哪裡來；標上根據，以後回頭檢查才知道哪一句可以改。

text.en: A score
text.zh: 一個分數

prompt.en: What must every line of the summary carry?
prompt.zh: 摘要裡每一句都要標什麼？

detail.en: Book III ch. 13 says such inquiry cannot be simple or offhand but needs many complicated observations; Book I ch. 2 asks for seed, place of birth, rearing and custom to be considered; and Book I ch. 17 is an example of the text explaining how a rule was derived. The four-part structure and the three basis tags are this lesson's arrangement.
detail.zh: 第三卷第 13 章說這類探討不能用簡單或隨便的方式、要靠許多複雜的觀察；第一卷第 2 章要求把種子、出生地、養育與習俗一併考慮；第一卷第 17 章是原文說明規則推導理由的例子。四段結構與三種依據標記法為本課編排。

label.en: Book I ch. 2 (how far knowledge is attainable)
label.zh: 第一卷第 2 章（可知到什麼程度）

label.en: Book I ch. 17 (the houses of the several planets)
label.zh: 第一卷第 17 章（行星各自的星座）

label.en: Book III ch. 13 (quality of the soul)
label.zh: 第三卷第 13 章（靈魂的性質）

title.zh: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos，Robbins 英譯（Loeb Classical Library, 1940）

summary.en: Your task: write your own summary, and say what every line is based on.
summary.zh: 這一堂的任務：寫一段自己的摘要，每一句都要說得出根據。

title.zh: 寫一段自己的摘要

kicker.en: Check your summary item by item; each one goes back to an earlier lesson.
kicker.zh: 一項一項對照你的摘要，每一項都對應到前面某一堂。

text.en: One: did you treat a sign as who you are (“I'm just a Scorpio person”)? Two: did one layer stand in for everything (only the Sun)? Three: did a candidate get written as settled? Four: did you read a layer that is not there (houses with no birth time)? Five: did a category turn into good and bad (good aspects, bad aspects, lucky and unlucky planets)? Six: did a description turn into a prediction (what will happen, whether you will succeed)?
text.zh: 一、有沒有把星座當成身分（「我就是天蠍座的人」）？二、有沒有只講一層就代表全部（只講太陽）？三、有沒有把候選寫成確定？四、有沒有讀到一層根本沒有的東西（沒有時間卻寫了宮位）？五、有沒有把分類寫成好壞（好相位、壞相位、吉星、凶星）？六、有沒有把描述寫成預測（會發生什麼、會不會成功）？

text.en: If none of the six apply, your summary broadly holds up. If even one does, go back and reread the lesson it belongs to.
text.zh: 六項都沒中，你的摘要大致站得住。只要中了一項，就回到對應的那一堂再讀一次。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 2 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos says predictions sometimes fail and that seed, place of birth, upbringing and custom must be considered too; Book III ch. 13 says such judgements need many conditions together, never one thing alone.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 2 章說預測有時會失準，要把種子、出生地、養育和習俗一起考慮；第三卷第 13 章說這類判斷要很多條件一起看，不能只看一項就下結論。

heading.en: Why these six are so easy to fall into
heading.zh: 為什麼這六項特別容易中

kicker.en: Each of the six is a shortcut, which is why they are so easy to fall into.
kicker.zh: 這六項都是偷懶的捷徑，所以特別容易中。

text.en: The six have one thing in common: each is less work. Calling yourself a sign says it all in one line. Picking one candidate spares you the doubt. Sorting into good and bad spares you working out how things fit together. Writing a prediction spares you admitting you do not know. The honest way is more work at every step; that is its only drawback.
text.zh: 這六項有個共同點：都比較省力。把星座當身分，一句話就講完；挑一個候選，就不用面對不確定；分好壞，就不用想怎麼調和；寫成預測，就不用承認自己也不知道。老實的寫法每一步都比較累，這是它唯一的缺點。

text.en: So the checklist is a reminder. You will keep reaching for the shortcut, and that is normal. What matters is whether you have one fixed habit that pulls you back.
text.zh: 所以這張檢查表是一個提醒。你會一直想走捷徑，這很正常；差別只在你有沒有一個固定的動作，把自己拉回來。

alt.en: Table: the Sun's sign is present, with two candidates on a changeover day; most planetary signs are present, with candidates for the fast ones on a boundary day; the Moon often has two candidates; aspects are present and need no birth time; the Ascendant is absent, its row empty; and the twelve houses are absent, the whole layer missing.
alt.zh: 對照表：太陽星座有（交界日列兩個候選）；多數行星星座有，走得快的在交界日列候選；月亮常有兩個候選；相位有，不需要出生時間；上升沒有，那一格是空的；十二宮沒有，整層不存在。

caption.en: Check four is the one people trip on most: houses need a birth time. This table is the line.
caption.zh: 第四項最常中：宮位要有出生時間才能寫。這張表就是界線。

caveat.en: Both lines were written to show the rewrite; you can follow the same steps with your own lines.
caveat.zh: 這兩句是為了示範改寫特地編的，你可以照同樣的步驟改自己的句子。

lines.en: Falls into one and six: “I'm a Capricorn, so I'm bound to succeed.”
lines.zh: 中了第一和第六項：「我是摩羯，所以我一定會成功。」

lines.en: Rewritten: “My Saturn is in Capricorn, which tradition reads as building slowly; I do tend to prepare first.”
lines.zh: 改寫後：「我的土星在摩羯，傳統讀成慢慢累積；我確實習慣先準備好。」

lines.en: The difference: it has a subject, a basis, and it speaks about a habit you can already see now.
lines.zh: 差在哪：有主角、有根據，講的是現在已經看得到的習慣。

limitations.en: Passing all six only means you avoided these six writing mistakes; it does not guarantee the reading is right.
limitations.zh: 檢查表六項都沒中，只代表避開了這六種寫法上的錯，不保證讀得對。

limitations.en: The two demonstration lines were made up; neither is anything a real person said.
limitations.zh: 示範的兩句是編出來的，不是真人說的話。

claim.en: “The honest version is too wordy for anyone to read.”
claim.zh: 「老實的寫法太囉唆，沒人要看。」

correction.en: The honest version can be short: a subject, a basis and what you can see now fit in one sentence.
correction.zh: 老實的寫法也可以很短：有主角、有根據、講現在看得到的事，一句話就寫得完。

claim.en: “Passing the checklist means my reading is right.”
claim.zh: 「檢查表都過了，就代表我讀對了。」

correction.en: The checklist blocks six known mistakes; whether the content is right goes back to the basis and your real experience. The text itself says predictions sometimes fail.
correction.zh: 檢查表幫你擋掉已知的六種錯；內容對不對，要回到根據和你實際的經驗去看。原文自己也說預測有時會失準。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: which items you fell into, your rewritten line, and how you will remind yourself.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：你中了哪幾項、改寫後的那一句，以及你打算怎麼提醒自己。

objective.en: By the end you can run a checklist over your own readings to catch the mistakes you make most, and say why each one is a mistake.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你會用一張檢查表，抓出自己讀盤時最容易犯的錯，也知道每一項為什麼算錯。

personalIntro.en: Your turn: take the summary you wrote last lesson and check it item by item.
personalIntro.zh: 換你自己：拿出上一堂寫的摘要，一項一項檢查。

personalSteps.en: Go through the six and mark which ones you fell into.
personalSteps.zh: 六項一一對照，標出中了哪幾項。

personalSteps.en: Pick one line that fell into one, and rewrite it like the example.
personalSteps.zh: 挑一句中了的，照示範改寫一次。

personalSteps.en: Write one line: which one do you fall into most, and why?
personalSteps.zh: 寫一句：你最常中哪一項？為什麼？

reason.en: With no birth time there are no houses; that layer does not exist.
reason.zh: 沒有出生時間就沒有宮位，那一層不存在。

text.en: Reading a layer that is not there
text.zh: 讀到一層根本沒有的東西

reason.en: The problem here lies in the house layer.
reason.zh: 這句的問題出在宮位那一層。

text.en: Treating a sign as who you are
text.zh: 把星座當成身分

reason.en: This line describes a position now; the problem is a house that needs a birth time to work out.
reason.zh: 這句講的是現在的位置；問題是用了要靠出生時間才算得出來的宮位。

text.en: Turning a description into a prediction
text.zh: 把描述寫成預測

prompt.en: “I have no birth time, but my Sun is in the tenth house” — which item does this fall into?
prompt.zh: 「我沒有出生時間，但我的太陽在第十宮」——這句中了哪一項？

reason.en: The checklist is about how you wrote it; whether it is right goes back to the basis.
reason.zh: 檢查表管的是寫法，內容對不對要回去看根據。

text.en: That the writing passes, and the content still goes back to its basis
text.zh: 代表寫法過關了，內容還要回去對根據

reason.en: A line with a basis can still miss your real experience.
reason.zh: 一句有根據的話，也可能跟你實際的經驗對不上。

text.en: That your summary is now correct
text.zh: 代表你的摘要已經是對的

reason.en: The gap section is a fixed part of the summary, written every time.
reason.zh: 落差那一段是摘要固定的一段，每次都要寫。

text.en: That you can leave out the gap section
text.zh: 代表可以不用寫落差那一段

prompt.en: If none of the six apply, what does that mean?
prompt.zh: 檢查表六項都沒中，代表什麼？

detail.en: Book I ch. 2 says predictions sometimes fail and asks for seed, place of birth, rearing and custom to be considered; Book III ch. 13 says such judgments need many conditions together. Both argue against concluding from one thing. The six checklist items and their order are this lesson's arrangement.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 2 章說預測有時失誤，並要求把種子、出生地、養育與習俗一併考慮；第三卷第 13 章說這類判斷要許多條件一起看，兩者都反對只憑一項就下結論。六項檢查表的條目與排序為本課編排。

summary.en: Your task: go back over your own summary with the checklist.
summary.zh: 這一堂的任務：拿檢查表，把自己的摘要再檢查一遍。

title.zh: 常見誤讀自我檢查

heading.en: Tidying so you can come back

kicker.en: When you tidy your notes, keep the dates, the bases and the doubts.
kicker.zh: 整理筆記時，留下日期、根據和不確定的地方。

text.en: Records are only worth comparing if you can tell them apart. So keep three things when you tidy. First, dates: six months on, that is how you tell what you wrote then from what you changed later. Second, the basis marks: computed, traditional, or my own observation. Third, the doubts: candidates, descriptions that missed, things you have not worked out yet.
text.zh: 紀錄要分得出彼此，之後才有得比。所以整理時留下三件事。第一是日期：半年後，你才分得出哪一句是當時寫的、哪一句是後來改的。第二是根據標記（算出來的／傳統說法／我自己的觀察）。第三是不確定的地方：候選、對不上的描述、你還沒想清楚的事。

text.en: Keep those three and every line can be traced to its source and compared six months on — that is exactly what makes notes useful.
text.zh: 留著這三件事，每一句都查得到來源，半年後還能拿來比——這正是筆記最有用的地方。

text.en: What the old texts say: Book I ch. 2 of Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos says one reason predictions fail is that the examples they rest on are not alike.
text.zh: 古書怎麼說：托勒密《四書》第一卷第 2 章說，預測會失準的原因之一，是拿來參考的例子彼此並不相同。

kicker.en: Your notes are kept on your own device, and they are still there after a membership lapses.
kicker.zh: 筆記存在你自己的裝置上，會員到期後也都還在。

text.en: Your notes, read marks and last reading position are kept on this device, together with your birth data. Delete all data in settings clears the notes and progress together, and it cannot be undone.
text.zh: 你的筆記、已讀標記和上次讀到的位置，都存在這台裝置上，跟你的出生資料放在一起。設定頁的「刪除全部資料」會把筆記和進度一起清掉，而且救不回來。

text.en: The first three lessons are free; from lesson four on, approved lessons are member content and need a membership to open. Every lesson opens once it has been approved. When a membership lapses, member lessons lock again, and notes and progress stay on the device; notes on the locked lessons are put aside and return to the notes overview when you are a member again.
text.zh: 前三堂免費；第四堂之後已核定的課是會員內容，需要會員才能打開。每一堂課都要先核定，才會開放。會員到期時，會員課會重新鎖起來，筆記和進度都還留在裝置上；鎖住那幾堂的筆記會先收起來，重新成為會員後就會回到筆記總覽。

text.en: Your notes stay on this device, in your own keeping.
text.zh: 筆記只留在這台裝置上，由你自己保管。

text.en: So if a line matters to you for the long run, copy it into your own notes app as well.
text.zh: 所以重要的句子，如果你想長期留著，建議另外抄一份到你自己的筆記工具。

alt.en: Diagram: a double ring. The outer ring is divided into twelve parts for the signs, the inner ring stands for the houses, and a horizontal line on the left is labelled ASC, the starting point. A concept figure with no real degrees.
alt.zh: 示意圖：一個雙層圓環，外圈分成十二等分代表十二星座，內圈代表十二宮，左側有一條水平線標著 ASC，代表起算點。概念圖，沒有真實度數。

caption.en: Once round the ring: from what a chart is, to your own notes.
caption.zh: 走完一圈了：從盤是什麼開始，到你自己的筆記。

caveat.en: These two lines show how to tidy, and you can rework your own notes the same way.
caveat.zh: 這兩句示範的是整理的做法，你可以照著改自己的筆記。

lines.en: Before: “Moon Aries, impulsive.”
lines.zh: 整理前：「月亮牡羊，衝動。」

lines.en: After: “2026-10, Moon is Aries or Taurus (computed); when plans change I phone first (my own observation); 'impulsive' does not fit — too much of a label.”
lines.zh: 整理後：「2026-10 月亮候選牡羊或金牛（算出來的）；行程被改時我會先打電話（我自己的觀察）；『衝動』這個詞我覺得不準，太像標籤。」

lines.en: The second is longer, but six months on you can still read it and still compare it.
lines.zh: 後面那句長一點，但半年後還讀得懂、還能拿來比。

limitations.en: For prices and plans, the membership page is what counts.
limitations.zh: 價格和方案以會員頁上顯示的為準。

limitations.en: Lessons not yet approved stay closed to everyone, member or not.
limitations.zh: 還沒核定的課，不管是不是會員都不開放。

limitations.en: When a membership lapses, notes on the locked lessons drop out of the notes overview for now, but they are not deleted.
limitations.zh: 會員到期時，鎖住那幾堂的筆記暫時不會出現在筆記總覽，但不會被刪掉。

limitations.en: Notes live only on this device and are not backed up to a cloud or sent anywhere; copy out any line you want to keep for the long run.
limitations.zh: 筆記只存在這台裝置上，不會備份到雲端或傳到別的地方；想長期留著的句子，請另外抄一份。

limitations.en: The before-and-after lines are only a demonstration, not anyone's real notes.
limitations.zh: 整理前後的兩句只是示範，不是真人的筆記。

claim.en: “The shorter the notes, the better.”
claim.zh: 「筆記越短越好。」

correction.en: Keep the dates, bases and doubts, and a note can be traced to its source and compared later.
correction.zh: 留著日期、根據和不確定的地方，筆記才查得到來源，之後也才能拿來比。

claim.en: “My notes disappear when my membership lapses.”
claim.zh: 「會員到期，筆記就不見了。」

correction.en: A lapsed membership only locks the member lessons again; it deletes no notes, and your progress stays too. What really clears them is delete all data in settings.
correction.zh: 會員到期只會讓會員課重新鎖起來，不會刪掉筆記，進度也還在；真正會清掉的是設定頁的「刪除全部資料」。

notePrompt.en: Write it down: the three lines from this course you most want to keep, each with a date and a basis.
notePrompt.zh: 寫下來：這一輪你最想留著的三句話，每句都標上日期和根據。

objective.en: By the end your notes will be in a shape you can still understand when you come back, and you will know where they are kept and what would delete them.
objective.zh: 做完這一堂，你的筆記會整理成以後回來看還讀得懂的樣子，你也會知道筆記存在哪裡、什麼情況下會被刪掉。

personalIntro.en: One last task: tidy the notes you have made along the way.
personalIntro.zh: 最後一次動手：整理你這一輪留下的筆記。

personalSteps.en: Add a date and a basis mark to each note.
personalSteps.zh: 幫每則筆記補上日期和根據標記。

personalSteps.en: Keep the candidates and the mismatches; they are the most useful part.
personalSteps.zh: 候選和對不上的地方都留著，它們最有用。

personalSteps.en: Copy the lines that matter into your own notes app as well.
personalSteps.zh: 重要的句子，另外抄一份到你自己的筆記工具。

reason.en: It clears notes and progress together, and cannot be undone.
reason.zh: 它會把筆記和進度一起清掉，而且救不回來。

text.en: Delete all data in settings
text.zh: 設定頁的「刪除全部資料」

reason.en: A lapse only locks the member lessons again; notes and progress are still there.
reason.zh: 會員到期只會讓會員課重新鎖起來，筆記和進度都還在。

text.en: Your membership lapsing
text.zh: 會員到期

reason.en: After switching language, your notes and reading position are all still there.
reason.zh: 切換語言後，筆記和讀到的位置都還在。

text.en: Switching language
text.zh: 切換語言

prompt.en: Which action clears your notes and progress?
prompt.zh: 哪一個動作會清掉你的筆記和進度？

reason.en: They record what you actually checked, which is what helps most when you look back.
reason.zh: 它們記下你真正檢查過的地方，回頭看時最有參考價值。

text.en: Keep them; they are the most useful part when you come back
text.zh: 留著，以後回來看，它們最有用

reason.en: Keep the basis, and a few months later you can still follow what you wrote.
reason.zh: 留著根據，過幾個月你還看得懂自己寫了什麼。

text.en: Delete them; shorter notes are better
text.zh: 刪掉，筆記越短越好

reason.en: Write doubts as doubts, and your notes stay a true record.
reason.zh: 不確定的地方照實寫，筆記才是真的紀錄。

text.en: Rewrite them as settled facts
text.zh: 改寫成確定的說法

prompt.en: When you tidy your notes, what do you do with the mismatches and candidates?
prompt.zh: 整理筆記時，對不上的地方和候選要怎麼處理？

detail.en: Book I ch. 2 gives the disparity of the examples as one reason predictions fail, which is why this lesson says records must be distinguishable to be worth comparing. The dates, basis tags and keeping of uncertainties are this lesson's arrangement, and where notes are stored, what delete all data does, and that the first three lessons are free, approved lessons from four on need a membership, and a lapse locks them again without deleting notes, are this app's actual behaviour today.
detail.zh: 第一卷第 2 章說預測失誤的原因之一是所依據的例子彼此並不相同，本課據此說明紀錄要能彼此分辨才有比較價值。日期、依據標記與保留不確定的整理方式為本課編排；筆記儲存位置、刪除全部資料的後果，以及前三堂免費、第四堂之後已核定的課需要會員、到期重新上鎖但不刪筆記，皆為本 App 當前的實際行為。
